# Phase F3: the Launchpad pack - implementation plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or
> superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** The Launchpad control surface lands on the package mechanism as a pack, and the LSDj MI.MAP app beside it as a
second one. `packages/launchpad` gets the branch's TypeScript - the Launchpad protocol, the decoder, the surface, the
profiles, `PortScan`, the controller session and its `rp.controller.session` node (label 22, moved out of the shell) -
with every fix `feature/launchpad` found carried over and expressed in the graph's terms: the relocate, the link
**generation**, the drop repaint, the model confirmation, one claim per port across processes, a scan in TypeScript, and
the idle block's dirty shortcut. `packages/lsdj-launchpad` contributes the MI.MAP app through a new contribution kind,
`controllerApps`, whose two halves are joined by id and whose sync override is **manifest data**. The pack's native half
is the E2 shape (a portable `SurfaceLink` with generations and its two surface nodes, a desktop transport on fixed slots
with a writer thread, `PortClaim`, `MidiPortPool`, a provider and a 12-method RPC facet), the provider ABI goes to **2**
(`reserve_midi`, `suspend_hardware_inputs`, `restored`, the provider's `wake`), and each product names the providers it
starts (`PROVIDERS`, no default). **F3 changes no audio and no cart:** strict parity, the kit and render baselines, the
box's two images and the `bliptoaster` pack's bytes hold unmodified. The re-records are the design's five, each in the
task that causes it (the `[packages]` golden, the role goldens' `drops` wire, one `ProtocolNodes` digest, the device
check's image hash, and two descriptor goldens recorded as new files); Task 6 is the acceptance run.

**Architecture:** Per [modular-graph-phase-f3-design.md](modular-graph-phase-f3-design.md), whose section 12 ("As built")
records the build and which Task 5 lands, sections 1 to 10 corrected in place to what the prototype found. Task 1 lands
the `launchpad` package's TypeScript, the node it moves out of the shell, the branch's fixes and the **scenario mode** of
`build-device-pack.mjs` (the portability proof that replaces `check:portable`). Task 2 lands the `controllerApps` kind
(generator, augmentation, fixtures, the zod-free runtime route), the `lsdj-launchpad` bridge, the second scenario, and
the session's clocked-tick fix that re-records one `ProtocolNodes` digest. Task 3 lands the pack's two native targets,
`SurfaceLink` /2 with generations and a `drops` output, the fixed-slot link with its writer thread, the provider and the
facet, ABI 2, `PROVIDERS`, the transport's 49 cases, and the three goldens the surface nodes move. Task 4 lands the
products on the provider (the SDL's rendezvous, the headless fake, the CLI), the shell on the facet
(`launchpadDevices.ts`, the menu, `config.json`'s `controlSurface`, the store's merge-on-write), deletes the legacy host,
and adds `sdl:controller` with its **port filter**. Task 5 lands the docs and the design's record. Task 6 is the
acceptance run.

**Tech stack:** TypeScript 7 per package (`tsc -p tsconfig.json`), the F1 package generator
(`packages/retroplug/scripts/lib/packages.mjs`, three gitignored modules), esbuild with the pinned options, zod only where
a package's `app` member is (never in `launchpad`), the E4 device toolchain (`build-device-pack.mjs`'s node mode and its
new scenario mode, `retroplug-mqjs-run`), C++20 with Catch2 for the transport, RtMidi at root scope with
`POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE`, the provider ABI (`rp_provider.h`) at 2, CMake's `retroplug_product(... PROVIDERS ...)`, and
the Pico SDK only where Task 6 rebuilds the device images. No submodule moves, no dependency version changes.

**Spec:** [modular-graph-phase-f3-design.md](modular-graph-phase-f3-design.md) and
[package-split.md](package-split.md) (F3 is the second of its four phases). The mechanism it builds on is F1's
([modular-graph-phase-f1-design.md](modular-graph-phase-f1-design.md) section 11 and spec/06's "Adding a package"), the
shape it copies is the N8 pack's ([modular-graph-phase-e2-design.md](modular-graph-phase-e2-design.md)), the toolchain's
scenario mode extends [modular-graph-phase-e4-design.md](modular-graph-phase-e4-design.md),
[modular-graph-phase-f1-plan.md](modular-graph-phase-f1-plan.md) is the plan executed the way this one is, and
[launchpad-plan.md](launchpad-plan.md) is the branch's own design (its section 8.6 is the controller contract).

**Where this plan departs from the design as committed (`fcdb47361`).** The design was written before the prototype;
this plan follows what was built, and Task 5 lands the design with section 12's record and sections 1 to 10 corrected
in place. In short (a bullet quotes the design where it uses quotation marks):

- **The pack has no `script` member, and no `app` member either.** The scenario mode is the portability proof: no
  box image carries a controller (the box has one root port and the N8 holds it, and the core measures 61440 bytes
  against a 64 KiB arena), so a `heapBytes` would be a claim nobody holds the pack to. `launchpad` contributes no
  controller app - only the kind's mechanism and the node - so it needs no zod, and the MI.MAP app's control-plane
  half lives in the bridge, which is where its schema and label belong.
- **`protocol.apps[].syncOverride` is data, and `protocol.module` is optional.** A manifest cannot carry a function,
  and the planner must not read the generated `packages.ts` (which imports every app module and so every app's zod:
  `bundle-protocol.test.ts` holds `buildGraph` to no app and no zod). So the override is `{ node, mode, listening,
  off }`, validated by the generator, rendered into `generated/protocol.ts` as `CONTROLLER_SYNC` and applied by the
  shell's generic code; a package that declares only apps names no node module, and one that names a module with no
  nodes to export is refused.
- **The session counts the ticks the host clocked, with the cart's own walk.** The first answer inferred elapsed
  time from the tick difference against the previous block, which drifts on ragged blocks (the review's Critical)
  and loses a block at a loop wrap, a seek made while stopped and a device taken again. As built the node walks
  `TickClock` - the same walk the cart's protocol node runs - and hands the session the previous block's **count**,
  so `relocate`, the `lastTick` diff and the `started` gate are gone. That fix is what moved one `ProtocolNodes`
  digest, not the surface nodes' `drops` wire, which changes no byte of it.
- **`PROVIDERS` is each product's list, and it has no default.** Stage 3's first cut started every listed provider
  in every product: the provider's surface link then refused the SDL's own install (the standalone's Launchpad was
  dead), and the plugin started a control surface it cannot use. A product now names the packages whose providers it
  starts (`n8 launchpad` for the SDL, the headless host and the CLI; `n8` for the plugin, whose `plugin.cmake` also
  refuses a plugin target linked to the pack's desktop target), and a manifest item that carries both an `entry` and
  a `provider` is refused at configure.
- **The ABI is 2 with strict equality both ways, and it carries four calls.** `reserve_midi(in, out)` keeps the
  claimed pair out of the product's shared stream; `suspend_hardware_inputs(bool)` is the held edge a scan raises
  (Windows only: an ALSA or CoreMIDI input is shared); `restored()` is the rendezvous's product half, so the product
  names no class of the pack; and `rp_provider::wake(self)` is the per-frame pump, generated as
  `rp_wake_providers(providers)`. A host and a provider refuse each other across a version in both directions.
- **A pair whose input and output share one name is one claim.** Two locks refused each other, so the ordinary
  Launchpad on ALSA, CoreMIDI and WinMM could never be claimed; the claim now takes one token when the names match,
  runs in the branch's order (the old pair let go, presence checked against the lister, the claims taken, the pair
  reserved, the ports opened), and a refusal at the claims keeps the reservation so the other instance's pads never
  reach this stream.
- **`send()` never waits for a write, and `disconnect()` can.** The UI thread's `send()` pushes into a 16-message
  queue the writer drains, so a scan's sends never wait behind a bulk SysEx; what is still owed is `disconnect()`,
  which runs on the UI thread for a claim, a release and the provider's stop, joins a writer that may be mid-drain
  and writes the close bytes itself. That is Task 6's owed Windows item, not a fix.
- **The headless host runs the real facet over a scripted opener.** `FakePorts.hpp`'s `scriptedOpenerFor` answers
  like a Pro MK3, so the claim logic, the pool, the link and the facet are the product's code and `test:native` (and
  CI) drive the real thing; the host keeps its harness surface link, because the parity baseline stages pad presses
  into one, which is why `ProviderHost` grew `installLinks`.
- **The hardware-safety seams are an environment variable and two test-only hooks.** `RP_MIDI_PORT_ALLOW` (a
  comma-separated list of name substrings) is honoured by the pack's lister, its opener, `MidiPortPool`,
  `ControllerLink` and the host's `MidiIo`; `RETROPLUG_LAUNCHPAD_CLAIM_DIR` fixes the headless host's claim
  directory, and the host removes only a directory it created; `RETROPLUG_SDL_TEST_SCAN` drives the standalone's
  scan from the harness. The filter rule is held twice (the package boundary forbids a shared header) and one
  table-driven case in `retroplug-midi-test` holds the two copies to each other.
- **The re-records, and the one that only looks like one.** The `[packages]` golden (two types register from their
  own package after `core`), the role goldens' `drops` wire (one wire in each of the eleven controller documents)
  and the two surface descriptor goldens (new files: the tree had none for the legacy nodes) are Task 3's; the moved
  `ProtocolNodes` controller-out digest is Task 2's, with the tick fix. The `device:check` image hash moves
  `8cc7ae7d` -> `706e26cf` (Task 3's first cut: the nodes join the image) -> `38665e2c` (Task 3's fix pass: the
  generation mapped into `1..2^24-1`), so this plan's Task 3 expects `38665e2c`; the box's two images and the
  `bliptoaster` pack's bytes never move.


**The user's decisions** (`.superpowers/f-split/decisions.md`, the F3 entries; design section 2, and the brainstorm's
A/C/A/A choices):

- **The port is the whole thing in one phase, and it is a port, not a merge.** `feature/launchpad` forked at
  `cfeb80e00`, before the graph existed, and rebuilt the control surface on the old DSP kernel's controller channel;
  this tree replaced that channel with the graph (`rp.launchpad.surface-in` / `-out` over `rp.host.devices/2`, the
  `rp.controller.session` script node). The branch is read as a specification and its fixes are carried over in this
  tree's terms; the parity baseline's controller group is the proof the port moved no audio.
- **The LSDj app is the bridge's, and neither package knows the other.** `lsdj-launchpad` depends on `core`,
  `launchpad`, `lsdj` and `tracker` and contributes through `controllerApps`; `launchpad` imports neither the bridge
  nor `lsdj`; `lsdj` is unchanged. A tracker with its own app adds its own bridge.
- **TS owns the selection and native is a protocol-free transport.** `config.json` gains an additive
  `controlSurface: {input, output, device, enabled}` (schema 3, no migration step), written by a merge-on-write
  store that re-reads the file first; `launchpad.cfg` is never imported, so a user re-scans once. The startup
  rendezvous is the product's: it holds MIDI and audio, the TS claims its pair through the facet and calls
  `restored()`, and the product starts anyway after 500 ms of wall clock.
- **The proof is headless, and the desk is owed.** The C++ transport's cases, `PortScan`, the two scenarios, the
  unchanged oracles, `sdl:controller` over the ALSA fake, and a facet-level fake behind the headless host for
  `test:native` and CI. The real-device checklist (design section 8) and the Windows items are **owed to the user**,
  who runs them at a desk; findings become follow-ups. There is no hardware leg in this plan.
- **The model routing, which this plan's execution follows:** DeepSeek Flash wrote the prototype's stages, this plan
  and the follow-ups; Flash-Next at `--thinking xhigh` (two at most) implements the plan's tasks and runs the
  acceptance; Opus reviews the prototype's stages and the final tree; the controller coordinates, reviews this plan
  and reviews the risky code.
- **What only the record backs.** The design's section 12 is the description of what was built and of what no log
  records; the stage reports in `/tmp/f3pro` are the working record (which run each figure is from, every review
  finding and its fix, the departures a fix pass forced), and `results.md` is the controller's log of them, with
  each verdict and call. Where this plan quotes a figure, it quotes the report or log that states it; where nothing
  does, it says so and asks for the count.


**Hardware safety: this plan touches no real MIDI port, ever.** The rig this plan was generated on has a Zoom L6, a CH345
and possibly a Launchpad Pro MK3 attached, and a real NES with an N8, a Pico box and a probe are wired in. Nothing in
this plan may list, open, write to or claim any of them. The rules:

- **A run that lists or opens system MIDI ports must carry `RP_MIDI_PORT_ALLOW` set to the fakes' exact names, and
  nothing else.** `tools/run-sdl-controller.sh` sets it itself, from the two ALSA fakes' own `ready` lines, and
  **refuses** to run when a caller has preset the variable: run `pnpm sdl:controller`, never a bare `retroplug-sdl`, and
  never with that variable preset. `pnpm sdl:smoke` and `pnpm sdl:pipewire` run under a scratch `RETROPLUG_USER_CONFIG_DIR`
  with `RP_MIDI_PORT_ALLOW=RP_NO_PORT`, a list that matches nothing (an EMPTY list means "every port", so the
  nothing-matching list has to name something).
- **The fake is `RPFakeLPProMK3` and the list is two whole RtMidi names**, because the filter matches substrings: a list
  holding `LPProMK3 MIDI` would admit a real Pro MK3 (`Launchpad Pro MK3:Launchpad Pro MK3 LPProMK3 MIDI 24:0` contains
  it), which is the hazard the last fix pass closed. The harness also fails when a listed port that is not a fake
  contains `LPProMK3` or `Launchpad`.
- **The listing-only proof comes first, and it opens nothing.** The step that runs it sets
  `RETROPLUG_SDL_MIDI_LIST=1 RETROPLUG_SDL_EXIT_AFTER_FRAMES=5`, so the standalone enumerates and exits: no port is
  opened and no byte is sent. Run it before `pnpm sdl:controller`, and stop if its filtered half names a port that is
  not one of the two fakes.
- **`retroplug-device-mode-test`, `test:plugin`, `test:native`, `pnpm test` and the CLI legs open no port**: the fakes
  are scripted openers in C++ and TypeScript, and the headless host's provider runs over `scriptedOpenerFor`. If a run
  of one of them seems to be waiting on MIDI, stop and report it rather than reaching for a queueing tool.
- **Never run `amidi`, `aconnect`, `aseqdump`, `aplaymidi` or any other port tool against this machine's devices**, and
  never `git`-checkout or build with a saved `controlSurface` in the real `~/.config/retroplug`: a saved, enabled pair
  is claimed at startup and its close bytes go out at quit (which is why the two SDL tools take a scratch config dir).
- `deps/sameboy` shows as modified after any configure (two tracked patches). That is expected; never stage, reset or
  stash it, and never touch any submodule.

**Ground rules for whoever executes this:**

- This plan lives at `docs/modular-graph-phase-f3-plan.md` and is committed before Task 1 (a docs commit of its own):
  the header's links are relative to that location; every command and path in the steps is relative to the worktree
  root.
- Commit after each task (the commands are given; Task 6 commits nothing unless a step fails and is fixed, in a commit
  of its own, named for what it fixes). A commit message is a subject line, a blank line, then the body, and the
  prototype's bodies are quoted whole: use `git commit -F -` as the blocks show. No `Co-Authored-By` or "generated with"
  trailer. Do not push, and do not open a PR.
- Never use an emdash character in code, comments, docs or commit messages; use " - ", ":" or ";". Some diffs below
  carry emdashes on lines the prototype did not write (context lines of older code and of the specs): leave those be.
- Run every command from the worktree root with absolute paths or a subshell (`(cd x && ...)`); never `cd` the session
  itself. Never bare `git stash`, never switch branches with uncommitted work in the tree, and never `rm -rf build` to
  fix CMake: investigate.
- **Every whole-file block below (a `Create`) is followed by the `sed -n` range that extracts it from this plan and by
  the blob hash the file must have:** write or extract the file, then `git hash-object <path>` must print the hash the
  step quotes, which is the prototype commit's blob. **Every diff block is followed by its extraction, a
  `git apply --check`, and the blob hash of each file it changes**, so an applied diff is the prototype's bytes and not
  just something that applies. **Every `patch` block is a TEMPORARY mutation**: apply it, watch the run fail or print
  what the step says, then reverse it with the range the next command gives, so the task's tree is what the commit
  expects.
- **`pnpm-lock.yaml` is a manifest change's companion, and only one install runs, ever:** the steps that change a
  package's dependencies place the lockfile's diff as it stands and then run
  `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --offline`, which must leave the lockfile's bytes alone (the step quotes its blob).
  Never run a bare `pnpm install`: offline, a non-frozen one re-resolves the lockfile and silently prunes every other
  platform's optional packages. Task 1, Task 2 and Task 3 each bring one diff; Task 4 and Task 5 change no manifest's
  dependencies.
- **The generated modules are never committed.** `packages/retroplug/src/generated/{packages,protocol,scriptNodes}.ts`
  are written by `packages/retroplug/scripts/lib/packages.mjs`, gitignored, and regenerated by the runners,
  `pnpm typecheck` and the CMake `retroplug-ts-packages` target. A worktree a prototype build ran in may hold three of
  them, untracked and stale: Task 1 Step 1 deletes them either way, and no `git status` list below shows them. If one
  ever does, the `.gitignore` entry is wrong: stop and report it.
- **Three goldens are re-recorded, each in the task that causes it and each named where it happens, and NOTHING ELSE
  IS.** Never set `RP_PARITY_UPDATE`, `RP_KIT_GOLDEN_UPDATE`, `RP_RENDER_GOLDEN_UPDATE`, `RP_GOLDEN_UPDATE`,
  `RP_GRAPH_GOLDEN_UPDATE` or `RP_PLAN_BLOB_UPDATE`. Task 1 and Task 2 re-record **no golden**, and prove it: strict
  parity (30 files, 250 cases, the controller group among them) and the `[packages]` golden's file do not appear in
  their `git status` lists. Task 2's one re-record is a **literal** in `ProtocolNodes.test.cpp` (the controller-out
  digest), in a file diff, with the failing run quoted before it. Task 3 re-records the `[packages]` golden, the role
  goldens' `drops` wire and writes the two surface descriptor goldens as **new files**, and its steps say which command
  writes each (`RP_PRODUCT_REGISTRATIONS_UPDATE=1` for the `[packages-dump]` half, `RP_GOLDEN_UPDATE=1 pnpm test
  graph/build-graph-role-goldens` for the role goldens, `RP_GRAPH_GOLDEN_UPDATE=1` for the descriptors). The device
  images and the pack's bytes are hashed in every task and must not move (but for the check image in Task 3, whose hash
  is that task's own `38665e2c`).
- **Case counts are exact. Assertion totals are exact too, with three exceptions:** a run of
  `retroplug-engine-graph-test` that includes `[engine-jobs]` reports a total that moves from run to run (its threaded
  cases assert in loops), so does `retroplug-launchpad-test`'s (its swap case counts in a loop), and so does the
  ThreadSanitizer run of `[script-pack]`; for those the case count must match and the total is the prototype's, quoted
  for scale. Catch2 pads its `test cases:` columns with spaces, which the quotes below collapse to one. `pnpm test`'s
  final line counts FILES; a case total is quoted from the reports and is not the runner's own line.
- **`pnpm typecheck`'s project count moves with the tree**: `Scope: 19 of 20 workspace projects` at Task 1 (the
  baseline is 18 of 19; Task 1 adds `launchpad`) and `20 of 21` from Task 2 on (the bridge). Quote the line your step
  gives, and treat a *different* count at the same task as a finding.
- The Catch2 binaries and `retroplug-render-host-test` are `EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL` or outside the default build:
  `cmake --build build` does not rebuild them, so a library edit needs the target built by name before a run
  (`pnpm test:plugin`, `test:n8` and `test:native` build theirs first). `tools/build-device-check.sh` and
  `tools/build-box.sh` build the exporter in the desktop build themselves. **A new or removed CMake source, a new
  package, or a manifest change needs `cmake -S . -B build` first**, and every task that adds a package needs that
  configure, because `retroplug_product()` refuses a package it was never told about.
- **A `pnpm install` is needed before a configure that reads a new package's `node_modules` link**, and before a
  configure that reads a new product-list entry: each task's frozen install comes before its configure, and Task 1 and
  Task 2's steps check the two links exist.
- The build trees were last built at the prototype's tip, so each task's first build re-runs CMake and recompiles what
  changed; that is expected. `build-device/`, `build-box/` and `pico/n8-host/build/` hold the prototype's images and
  `build/` its bytecode: Task 3 rebuilds the `bliptoaster` pack and the check image before it hashes them, Task 4 does
  the same, Task 5 hashes them without rebuilding (it changes prose only), and Task 6 rebuilds all of it from removed
  dirs.
- **`sdl:controller` is Linux only and needs `libasound2-dev` and an ALSA sequencer**, which this devcontainer has. It
  is not in CI. Its five legs run against `tools/fixtures/fake-launchpad.c` and nothing else, and the two hardware-safety
  rules above are what make that true.
- **When a step's result differs from its Expected, stop and report.** A different exit status, case count or quoted
  text is a finding. Three exceptions: an assertion total the rule above calls moving; a predicted failure whose failing
  file, case or target is the one predicted but whose wording differs (the mutation steps say which are predicted); and
  a trap probe's quoted lines, whose object path and `(.text.startup.main+0x...)` offsets are this devcontainer's and
  this binutils' (the device scripts judge a probe by its own object and the two symbol names, `__wrap__Znwj` and
  `__wrap_malloc`, and that check is the pass criterion). Never edit code, a test or a golden to make a step pass. In
  Tasks 1 to 5 each task's tree must equal its prototype commit, so a real defect found there is reported, not fixed; a
  fix belongs to a commit of its own after the plan.
- **Track progress outside the committed plan:** never tick its checkboxes. Ticking one modifies
  `docs/modular-graph-phase-f3-plan.md`, and every task's expected `git status` list would then gain a line it does not
  show.
- The Windows build has not seen this tree (the prototype is local and Linux-only), so an MSVC-only warning or error is
  a real finding to report, not a stale quote; `/W4 /WX` was widened to the pack's four targets in Task 3 and no step
  below builds on Windows. macOS and the arm64 Linux CI job have not run either: `build.yml` runs on
  `workflow_dispatch`, pull requests and pushes to `main` only, so their first run is a dispatched run or a PR the user
  starts. **No step below needs a real device, and none may touch one.**
**Commit this plan before Task 1.** Before the commit, check where the tree is: `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` must
print `feature/modularize`, `git rev-parse --short=8 HEAD` must print `fcdb4736`, and `git status --short --untracked-files=all` must show
` m deps/sameboy` and nothing else, or that and the three untracked generated modules a prototype build may have left
(`packages/retroplug/src/generated/packages.ts`, `protocol.ts` and `scriptNodes.ts`, which are derived: Task 1 Step 1
deletes them). If the branch or the commit differs, stop: every step below assumes the design commit on a tree with
nothing else in it. (`git -C deps/sameboy status --short` shows the five files the two tracked SameBoy patches change:
`Core/apu.c`, `Core/apu.h`, `Core/camera.c`, `Core/random.c` and `Core/sgb.c`.) The run below copies the plan to its home
in the repository and commits it on its own, so every later task's `git status` and `git add` see a clean tree:

## File structure

| Path | Responsibility |

| `packages/launchpad/ts/` | the protocol (`protocol`, `decode`, `profile`, `surface`), `PortScan`, the session, the zod-free runtime registry and the `controllerApps` mechanism, `launchTarget`, `enums`, `ports`, the `rp.controller.session` node and the manifest's protocol module, the facet's client (`client.ts`), and the portable-core scenario (Tasks 1, 2, 3) |

### Task 1: the launchpad package's TypeScript, its session node and a scenario

Design sections 2, 4, 6, 7 and 9's first stage. The Launchpad protocol, its decoder, the surface, the profiles and
`PortScan` move out of the shell into `packages/launchpad`, with the controller session and the `rp.controller.session`
node (label 22) beside them; the branch's fixes go in as this tree's code, each with the test the report names; and
`build-device-pack.mjs` gains a **scenario mode** that proves the package's core portable on MicroQuickJS, which is what
replaces the branch's `check:portable`.

The package is deliberately not a device pack and has no control-plane half: no `script` member (no box image carries a
controller, so nothing would hold a `heapBytes` to a claim), no `app` member and no zod (the MI.MAP app's label and
schema are stage 2's bridge). What it does have is `protocol`: the session node's type and label 22, moved out of the
shell's own manifest, so `packages/launchpad/package.json` is the node's home from here on.

This stage keeps one dependency the design does not: `@retroplug/lsdj`, because the MI.MAP app and the predictor move
with the node in this stage (the node's bundle must contain the app it runs, and parity's controller group runs the real
script bundle), and `launchpad` is therefore listed after `lsdj` in the product order rather than after `core`. Stage 2
moves both out to `lsdj-launchpad` and restores the order; the task says so where it happens, and stage 1's report
records it as a ruling.

Fifteen files move and fifteen of them change on the way (git's similarity scores are 58 to 98 per cent), so each takes
its `git mv` and then the prototype's diff of its new path; two shell files are deleted. The new files are the package's
manifest and tsconfig, six modules the package gains (`enums`, `ports`, `portable`, `nodes`, `portScan`, `registry`), the
launchpad-core scenario, three test files, thirteen scenario and node-pack fixtures, and the store's new test. The rest
is the shell's call sites, the scenario mode, the docs' links and a lockfile that gains one importer.

The task's first step moves and deletes only; nothing is built until Step 11, because no step before it leaves a tree
that compiles.

````diff
+/** Whether anything the grid shows has changed since it was last painted: the page, follow, the cued row, any
+ *  channel's playhead, or the song itself. The app runs every audio block and the answer is nearly always no, so
+ *  this keeps the steady state to a handful of comparisons instead of repainting all 64 pads to find out. The
+ *  surface keeps what was painted, so a reconnect's full repaint needs no paint here either. */
+function needsPaint(st: MapState, grid: ReturnType<ControllerCtx["playback"]["grid"]>, pos: PlaybackPosition): boolean {
+  const p = st.painted ?? (st.painted = { page: -1, follow: false, pending: null, revision: -1, rows: [] });
+  const revision = grid.revision ?? -2; // no revision: cannot tell, so always repaint
+  let changed = p.page !== st.page || p.follow !== st.follow || p.pending !== st.pending
+    || p.revision !== revision || revision === -2;
+  const channels = pos.channels;
+  for (let i = 0; i < channels.length; i++) {
+    const row = channels[i].playing && channels[i].songRow !== null ? channels[i].songRow! : -1;
+    if (p.rows[i] !== row) {
+      changed = true;
+      if (i < p.rows.length) p.rows[i] = row;
+      else p.rows.push(row);
+    }
+  }
+  p.page = st.page!;
+  p.follow = st.follow!;
+  p.pending = st.pending ?? null;
+  p.revision = revision;
+  return changed;
````

````ts
//
// These are the DSP kernel node's, port for port, as B3a sized them, since each output carries what that kernel
// output carried for its system; a queue drops what does not fit, and the drop is counted per port. The node's

// controls are a message each.

import type { QueueCapacity } from "@retroplug/core/descriptor";

 *  4096 bytes, measured at 5 messages holding 206 bytes in one block. */
export const CONTROLLER_OUT: QueueCapacity = { messages: 256, bytes: 4096 };
````

````ts
// The PORTABLE CORE: everything a control surface needs that is not a host, as one entry point.
//
// This is what a host other than the desktop builds - the planned one being MicroQuickJS on a Pico 2, on top of
// pico/ - so it is held to what that engine runs, and the scenario mode of
// packages/retroplug/scripts/build-device-pack.mjs proves it: the bundle may import nothing outside the package's
// own tree and its declared dependencies (no zod, no backend, no native seam), it is lowered to ES5, and a
// scenario run under MicroQuickJS must produce byte-for-byte what the same scenario produces here.
//
// The rules that keeps to, beyond "no I/O":
//
//   - ES5 SYNTAX is the compiler's problem, not the source's: classes, arrows, let/const, destructuring and spread
//     are all lowered. Write normal TS.
//   - The LIBRARY is ours to respect. MicroQuickJS has no Map, Set or Symbol, iterates only arrays with for-of, and
//     lacks most ES2015+ methods (Object.values/entries/assign, Array find/includes/fill/from, Number.isInteger,
//     padStart...). Plain objects, arrays and loops cover every use here.
//   - Arrays may not be written past their end (no holes): build them by push, or full-length up front.
//
// What is deliberately NOT here: the app registry's config schemas (zod, which belong to the control plane), the
// script node that runs a session on the audio thread (ts/controllerSession.ts), the LSDj app and its launch target
// (they live with the tracker, in its bridge package) and every UI seam. A host wires these pieces itself - feed the
// session bytes and a 24 PPQN tick, write what it returns to the device, and hand the target a `send` that reaches
// the cart.

export { ControllerSession, isPredictive } from "./session";
export type { ControllerApp, ControllerCtx, SessionInput, SessionOptions } from "./session";
export type { PlaybackGrid, PlaybackModel, PlaybackPosition, PredictivePlaybackModel } from "@retroplug/tracker/playbackModel";
export { nullTarget, type TrackerTarget } from "./trackerTarget";
export { PortScan, IDLE_SCAN, MAX_REPLIES, GAP_MS } from "./portScan";
export type { MidiPortApi, ScanReply, ScanStatus } from "./portScan";

export {
  PRO_MK3, PROFILES, profileForFamily, profilesForFamily, familyHex, deviceName,
  deviceInquiry, parseInquiryReply, modelQuery, isModelReply, enterProgrammerMode, exitToLiveMode,
  Surface, decodeMessage, decodeMessages, Palette, palette, rgb,
} from "./index";
export type { LaunchpadProfile, Led, SurfaceEvent } from "./index";
````

Create `packages/launchpad/ts/portScan.ts`:

````ts
// Find which MIDI port PAIR a device is on, by writing a probe out of each output in turn and listening on
// every input for what comes back.
//
// Device-agnostic: the probe is whatever bytes the caller hands in (a Universal Device Inquiry, for a
// Launchpad) and the replies come back raw, for the caller to recognise. Host-agnostic too: it runs over an
// injected `MidiPortApi` and a clock it is TOLD, never one it reads, so the whole thing is a deterministic
// state machine a test can drive a millisecond at a time. The standalone steps it from a frame poll.
//
// Why a probe at all, rather than watching for a device to announce itself: a Launchpad on TRS/DIN arrives
// through an ordinary MIDI interface, and DIN has no enumeration and no idle heartbeat - the OS sees the
// interface and nothing else. The inquiry is the only identification MIDI 1.0 has, and it is also the only
// way to learn the PAIRING, since the reply tells you which input belongs to the output you wrote to - which
// may be a different interface entirely. Hence user-initiated: never on a timer, never at startup.

/** Single-direction MIDI ports by handle - what a host provides (the standalone's facet calls). */
export interface MidiPortApi {
  /** Open every input at once, a handle each (0 for one that will not open - another application holds
   *  it). One call rather than one per port, because a host may have to step its own MIDI stream aside to
   *  let an input go, and that is a cost to pay once per scan, not once per refusing port. */
  openInputs(names: readonly string[]): number[];
  /** A handle > 0, or 0 when the port will not open. */
  openOutput(name: string): number;
  send(handle: number, bytes: readonly number[]): boolean;
  /** What an input received since the last read, oldest first. */
  read(handle: number): number[][];
  close(handle: number): void;
}

/** One message an input returned while a given output was being probed. */
export interface ScanReply {
  output: string; // the port the probe went out of
  input: string; // the port this came back on
  bytes: number[];
}

export interface ScanStatus {
  busy: boolean;
  done: boolean; // a scan finished (with or without replies)
  phase: string; // short label while running, e.g. "Probing MIDISPORT 2x2 Port A"
  error: string; // "" = ok
  skipped: number; // ports that would not open (in use elsewhere)
  version: number; // bumped on any change, so a poller re-renders only when it moves
  replies: ScanReply[];
}

export const IDLE_SCAN: ScanStatus = {
  busy: false, done: false, phase: "", error: "", skipped: 0, version: 0, replies: [],
};

/** Replies kept per scan. Only SysEx is kept (an inquiry answer is nothing else), so a keyboard or a fader
 *  riding through the scan cannot fill this; it only has to be deeper than the number of devices that answer
 *  a universal inquiry. */
export const MAX_REPLIES = 64;

/** The quiet between one output's answer window and the next probe. Anything arriving in it is dropped
 *  rather than credited to either side, so a device that answers late is lost instead of being blamed on the
 *  NEXT output - a reply credited to the wrong output records a pair whose LEDs go nowhere. */
export const GAP_MS = 50;

/** A question to ask on the SAME pair, the moment a reply arrives on it - while the ports are still open and
 *  the answer window is still running. How a scan confirms WHAT answered without a second stage: reopening
 *  the ports would cost a Windows host another round of stepping its MIDI stream aside, and a port another
 *  program grabs in between would make a real device look like it never confirmed. Return the messages to
 *  send (none for a reply that needs no follow-up); each distinct message goes out once per output. */
export type FollowUp = (reply: ScanReply) => readonly (readonly number[])[];

export interface PortScanOptions {
  followUp?: FollowUp;
}

export class PortScan {
  private readonly listeners: { name: string; handle: number }[] = [];
  private next = 0; // index into outputs of the next port to probe
  private probing: { name: string; handle: number; since: number } | null = null;
  private quietUntil = -Infinity; // the gap after a window closes: no probe goes out before this
  // The scan's OWN clock, advanced only by forward steps of the time it is told. A wall clock stepping
  // backwards (an NTP correction) would otherwise freeze every window open until it caught up - with every
  // input held and, on Windows, the host's MIDI stream stepped aside the whole time.
  private elapsed = 0;
  private lastNow: number | null = null;
  private readonly asked: { [key: string]: true } = {}; // follow-ups already sent, by output + bytes
  private readonly followUp: FollowUp | undefined;
  private st: ScanStatus;

  constructor(
    private readonly api: MidiPortApi,
    inputs: readonly string[],
    private readonly outputs: readonly string[],
    private readonly probe: readonly number[],
    private readonly windowMs: number,
    options: PortScanOptions = {},
  ) {
    this.followUp = options.followUp;
    this.st = { ...IDLE_SCAN, busy: true, phase: "Listening", version: 1, replies: [] };
    // Every input is opened ONCE and kept open for the whole scan, so a device is heard whichever output it
    // turns out to be paired with. A port that will not open is counted and stepped over: on Windows a MIDI
    // input is exclusive, so anything else already holding it shows up here rather than failing the scan.
    const handles = inputs.length > 0 ? api.openInputs(inputs) : [];
    for (let i = 0; i < inputs.length; i++) {
      const handle = handles[i] ?? 0;
      if (handle > 0) this.listeners.push({ name: inputs[i], handle });
      else this.st.skipped++;
    }
  }

  status(): ScanStatus {
    return this.st;
  }

  /** Advance to `nowMs`. Call often (each frame is plenty); returns whether the scan is still running. A
   *  throw from the port API ends the scan with the error recorded and every port closed, so a host never
   *  ends up holding inputs for a scan that can no longer move. */
  step(nowMs: number): boolean {
    if (!this.st.busy) return false;
    if (this.lastNow !== null && nowMs > this.lastNow) this.elapsed += nowMs - this.lastNow;
    this.lastNow = nowMs;
    try {
      this.advance(this.elapsed);
    } catch (e) {
      this.edit().error = e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e);
      this.finish();
    }
    return this.st.busy;
  }

  /** Stop now, closing everything. Leaves the replies gathered so far. */
  cancel(): void {
    if (!this.st.busy) return;
    this.finish();
  }

  private advance(nowMs: number): void {
    // Read BEFORE moving on. Whatever has arrived so far came back while the current output was the only one
    // written to, so it is attributed to that output; arrivals outside a window are dropped.
    this.collect(nowMs);

    if (this.probing && nowMs - this.probing.since >= this.windowMs) {
      const handle = this.probing.handle;
      this.probing = null; // cleared first, so a close that throws is not closed again by finish()
      this.api.close(handle);
      this.quietUntil = nowMs + GAP_MS;
      this.edit();
    }
    if (!this.probing && nowMs >= this.quietUntil) this.probeNext(nowMs);
  }

  private collect(nowMs: number): void {
    for (const l of this.listeners) {
      const messages = this.api.read(l.handle);
      const probing = this.probing;
      if (!probing) continue; // drained either way, so a stale arrival cannot surface in a later window
      for (const bytes of messages) {
        // SysEx only. A Device Inquiry answer is nothing else, and everything else on a live rig - clock,
        // notes, a fader ride - would otherwise eat the reply cap before the device we are looking for has
        // been asked.
        if (bytes.length === 0 || bytes[0] !== 0xf0) continue;
        if (this.st.replies.length >= MAX_REPLIES) return;
        const reply = { output: probing.name, input: l.name, bytes };
        this.edit().replies.push(reply);
        this.askFollowUp(probing, reply, nowMs);
      }
    }
  }

  private askFollowUp(probing: { name: string; handle: number; since: number }, reply: ScanReply, nowMs: number): void {
    if (!this.followUp) return;
    for (const msg of this.followUp(reply)) {
      const key = probing.name + "|" + msg.join(",");
      if (this.asked[key]) continue; // the same device heard on several inputs is asked once
      this.asked[key] = true;
      this.api.send(probing.handle, msg);
      probing.since = nowMs; // the answer gets a full window of its own
    }
  }

  private probeNext(nowMs: number): void {
    while (this.next < this.outputs.length) {
      const name = this.outputs[this.next++];
      const handle = this.api.openOutput(name);
      if (handle <= 0) {
        this.edit().skipped++;
        continue;
      }
      this.probing = { name, handle, since: nowMs };
      this.edit().phase = `Probing ${name}`;
      if (this.probe.length > 0) this.api.send(handle, this.probe);
      return;
    }
    this.finish();
  }

  private finish(): void {
    const probing = this.probing;
    this.probing = null;
    const listeners = this.listeners.splice(0, this.listeners.length);
    const st = this.edit();
    st.busy = false;
    st.done = true;
    st.phase = "";
    // Closed last, and each on its own: one close that throws must not leave the rest open.
    if (probing) this.closeQuietly(probing.handle);
    for (const l of listeners) this.closeQuietly(l.handle);
  }

  private closeQuietly(handle: number): void {
    try {
      this.api.close(handle);
    } catch (e) {
      if (!this.st.error) this.edit().error = e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e);
    }
  }

  /** A fresh status to write into. Copied BEFORE the change, so a consumer holding an earlier status (a React
   *  render) never sees it move underneath it. */
  private edit(): ScanStatus {
    this.st = { ...this.st, version: this.st.version + 1, replies: this.st.replies.slice() };
    return this.st;
  }
}
````

Create `packages/launchpad/ts/registry.ts`:

````ts
// The controller-app registry mechanism: name -> app module, mirroring RoleRegistry (@retroplug/core's
// systemRoles.ts).
//
// An app is a function over the session's context, registered by name, with a config schema owning its shape,
// defaults and clamping - the same rails a DSP role runs on, down to reusing RoleConfigSchema rather than
// inventing a second config abstraction. The schema itself belongs to the app's owner: this module only holds the
// table.
//
// The control plane's half (an app's label and its config's schema) is the shell's registry, which pairs each runtime
// it finds here with its schema. Loading user scripts at runtime stays the deferred extension model (spec/07).

import type { RoleConfigSchema } from "@retroplug/core/systemRoles";
import type { ControllerApp } from "./session";

export interface ControllerAppType {
  /** Stable id, as stored in config. */
  readonly id: string;
  /** Menu label. */
  readonly label: string;
  readonly schema: RoleConfigSchema;
  readonly app: ControllerApp;
}

export class ControllerRegistry {
  // An array, not a Map: this module is in the portable core, and MicroQuickJS has no Map. The tables are a handful of
  // apps, so a linear lookup costs nothing a menu would notice.
  private readonly types: ControllerAppType[] = [];

  register(type: ControllerAppType): void {
    for (let i = 0; i < this.types.length; i++) {
      if (this.types[i].id !== type.id) continue;
      this.types[i] = type; // a re-registration replaces in place, keeping the app's position
      return;
    }
    this.types.push(type);
  }

  get(id: string): ControllerAppType | undefined {
    for (let i = 0; i < this.types.length; i++) if (this.types[i].id === id) return this.types[i];
    return undefined;
  }

  /** Every registered app, in registration order - the menu's source. */
  list(): ControllerAppType[] {
    return this.types.slice();
  }

  /** A full config for `id` with defaults filled and values clamped, or undefined for an unknown app. */
  defaultConfig(id: string): Record<string, unknown> | undefined {
    const type = this.get(id);
    return type ? type.schema.parse({}) : undefined;
  }
}
````

Create `packages/launchpad/ts/scenario/launchpadCore.ts`:

````ts
// The Launchpad core, end to end, through the PORTABLE CORE only - run by
// packages/retroplug/scripts/build-device-pack.mjs --scenario under Node and under MicroQuickJS, whose two
// transcripts must match byte for byte.
//
// It plays what a host does: take the device, feed it pad presses and a 24 PPQN clock block by block, write out
// what comes back, give the device back - plus a port scan against a fake rig. Every line printed is something a
// real host would put on a wire (LED bytes to the device, launch bytes to the cart) or a scan result it would act
// on, so a difference between the engines is a difference a player would see.
//
// It also has to REACH the core, not just import it: MicroQuickJS parses the whole bundle, so a syntax problem
// anywhere fails the run, but a missing library call or an array written past its end only fails on the path that
// executes it. So past the end-to-end session below, the later sections deliberately walk the branches a session
// does not: every LED form, the decoder's other message kinds, the profiles and their model confirmation, and a
// scan's follow-up / cancel / failure / quiet paths.

import {
  ControllerSession, PRO_MK3, Palette, PortScan, Surface, decodeMessages, deviceInquiry, deviceName, familyHex,
  isModelReply, modelQuery, parseInquiryReply, palette, profileForFamily, profilesForFamily, rgb,
  type MidiPortApi, type PlaybackPosition, type PlaybackGrid,
} from "../portable";

const out = (line: string): void => console.log(line);
const emit = (what: string, data: unknown): void => out(what + " " + JSON.stringify(data));

// --- a session --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

/** A dependency-free playback model: four channels that advance one row per 96 ticks, wrapping at six rows. Rows
 *  0..3 have content on pu1/pu2, 0..1 on wav, and noi is empty. Enough to see a playhead move and channels diverge. */
class FakeModel {
  readonly channelCount = 4;
  private readonly rows = [0, 0, 0, 0];
  private readonly remaining = [96, 96, 96, 96];
  private readonly playing = [false, false, false, false];
  private advanced = 0;
  private readonly pos: PlaybackPosition = { playing: false, channels: [] };
  private readonly gridView: PlaybackGrid & { revision: number };

  constructor() {
    for (let i = 0; i < 4; i++) this.pos.channels.push({ playing: false, songRow: null });
    const rows = [4, 4, 2, 0];
    this.gridView = {
      rowCount: 6,
      channelCount: 4,
      revision: 0,
      hasContent: (ch: number, row: number) => row >= 0 && row < 6 && row < rows[ch],
    };
  }

  position(): PlaybackPosition {
    return this.pos;
  }

  grid(): PlaybackGrid {
    return this.gridView;
  }

  launch(row: number): void {
    for (let i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
      this.rows[i] = row;
      this.remaining[i] = 96;
      this.playing[i] = true;
    }
    this.sync();
  }

  advance(ticks: number): void {
    this.advanced += ticks;
    for (let i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
      if (!this.playing[i]) continue;
      this.remaining[i] -= ticks;
      while (this.remaining[i] <= 0) {
        this.rows[i] = (this.rows[i] + 1) % 6;
        this.remaining[i] += 96;
      }
    }
    this.sync();
  }

  stop(): void {
    for (let i = 0; i < 4; i++) this.playing[i] = false;
    this.sync();
  }

  reset(): void {
    for (let i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
      this.rows[i] = 0;
      this.remaining[i] = 96;
      this.playing[i] = false;
    }
    this.sync();
  }

  advancedTicks(): number {
    return this.advanced;
  }

  private sync(): void {
    let any = false;
    for (let i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
      const p = this.pos.channels[i];
      p.playing = this.playing[i];
      p.songRow = this.playing[i] ? this.rows[i] : null;
      any = any || p.playing;
    }
    this.pos.playing = any;
  }
}

const launches: number[][] = [];
const model = new FakeModel();
const session = new ControllerSession((c) => {
  // Paint a row of content, the playhead bright, and launch on a press - the shape every controller app has.
  for (let y = 0; y < 4; y++) {
    c.surface.setPad(0, y, { mode: "static", colour: palette(Palette.greenDim) });
  }
  const row = c.playback.position().channels[0].songRow ?? 0;
  c.surface.setPad(1, row, { mode: "static", colour: palette(Palette.greenBright) });
  if (c.events.length > 0) c.target.launch(1);
}, {
  playback: model,
  target: { maxRow: 253, launch: (row) => launches.push([0x90, row, 100]), release: (row) => launches.push([0x80, row, 0]) },
  config: {},
});

const pad = (x: number, y: number, velocity: number): number[] => [0x90, (7 - y) * 10 + x + 11, velocity];
const cc = (n: number, value: number): number[] => [0xb0, n, value];

emit("connect", session.connect());

interface Block {
  input: number[][];
  tick: number;
  transport: boolean;
  relocate: boolean;
  /** The link reports a NEW device before this block, as a pair swapped inside one UI frame does: the host takes it
   *  again, which invalidates the surface so the block repaints everything. */
  reconnect?: boolean;
}
const blocks: Block[] = [
  { input: [], tick: 0, transport: false, relocate: false },
  { input: [pad(0, 2, 127), pad(0, 2, 0)], tick: 0, transport: false, relocate: false },
];
for (let tick = 0; tick <= 480; tick += 12) {
  const input: number[][] = [];
  if (tick === 108) input.push(pad(1, 4, 100));
  if (tick === 300) input.push(cc(PRO_MK3.buttons.up, 127), cc(PRO_MK3.buttons.up, 0));
  if (tick === 312) input.push(cc(PRO_MK3.buttons.down, 127));
  if (tick === 396) input.push(pad(6, 1, 90));
  blocks.push({ input, tick, transport: true, relocate: false });
}
// A generation change mid-run: the link reports a NEW device, so the host takes it again - Programmer mode and a full
// repaint, with the predictor left where the cart is.
blocks.push({ input: [pad(2, 1, 100)], tick: 492, transport: true, relocate: false, reconnect: true });
// A seek: the tick jumps far ahead. The session must not advance the model through it, so `ticks` is 0.
blocks.push({ input: [], tick: 4000, transport: true, relocate: true });
blocks.push({ input: [], tick: 480, transport: false, relocate: false });

for (let i = 0; i < blocks.length; i++) {
  launches.length = 0;
  if (blocks[i].reconnect) emit("reconnect " + i, session.connect());
  const leds = session.update(blocks[i]);
  if (leds.length > 0 || launches.length > 0) emit("block " + i, { leds, launches: launches.slice() });
}
emit("ticks", model.advancedTicks());
emit("disconnect", session.disconnect());

// --- a scan -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

// Two outputs, one busy; the device answers on a different interface's input than the output it was asked
// through, with a keyboard chattering clock and notes into every window. The follow-up asks the model question
// on the pair that answered, and only the model's own reply confirms it.
const PRO_MK3_REPLY = [0xf0, 0x7e, 0x00, 0x06, 0x02, 0x00, 0x20, 0x29, 0x13, 0x01, 0, 0, 0, 1, 2, 3, 0xf7];
const MODEL_REPLY = [0xf0, 0x00, 0x20, 0x29, 0x02, 0x0e, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0xf7];
const queues: { [handle: string]: number[][] } = {};
const names: { [handle: string]: string } = {};
let nextHandle = 1;
const deliver = (input: string, bytes: number[]): void => {
  for (const h of Object.keys(queues)) if (names[h] === input) queues[h].push(bytes);
};
const openPort = (input: boolean, name: string): number => {
  if (name === "Busy out" || name === "Busy in") return 0;
  const h = String(nextHandle++);
  names[h] = name;
  if (input) queues[h] = [];
  return Number(h);
};
const api: MidiPortApi = {
  openInputs: (list) => list.map((n) => openPort(true, n)),
  openOutput: (name) => openPort(false, name),
  send(handle, bytes) {
    const name = names[String(handle)];
    deliver("Keys", [0xf8]);
    deliver("Keys", [0x90, 60, 64]);
    if (name === "IF B out" && bytes[1] === 0x7e) deliver("IF A in", PRO_MK3_REPLY);
    if (name === "IF B out" && isModelReply(PRO_MK3, bytes)) deliver("IF A in", bytes.slice()); // an echo: not an answer
    if (name === "IF B out" && bytes[1] === 0x00 && bytes[2] === 0x20) deliver("IF A in", MODEL_REPLY);
    return true;
  },
  read(handle) {
    const q = queues[String(handle)] ?? [];
    queues[String(handle)] = [];
    return q;
  },
  close(handle) {
    delete queues[String(handle)];
    delete names[String(handle)];
  },
};

const scan = new PortScan(api, ["Keys", "Busy in", "IF A in"], ["Busy out", "Keys", "IF B out"], deviceInquiry(), 300, {
  followUp: (reply) => {
    const parsed = parseInquiryReply(reply.bytes);
    return parsed && profileForFamily(parsed.family) ? [modelQuery(PRO_MK3)] : [];
  },
});
for (let t = 0; scan.step(t); t += 16) { /* a frame at a time */ }
const status = scan.status();
emit("scan", status);
for (const r of status.replies) {
  const parsed = parseInquiryReply(r.bytes);
  if (parsed) emit("found", { input: r.input, output: r.output, name: deviceName(parsed.family) });
  emit("model reply", [r.bytes, isModelReply(PRO_MK3, r.bytes)]);
}
emit("open handles", Object.keys(names).length);

// --- the branches a session does not walk -----------------------------------------------------------------------

// Every LED form through the surface: static/pulse/flash in palette and RGB (RGB forces the bulk SysEx), a refused
// one (pulse carries a palette index only), edge buttons by name, and the indices that are not there.
const surface = new Surface();
surface.setPad(0, 0, { mode: "static", colour: palette(Palette.red) });
surface.setPad(1, 0, { mode: "pulse", colour: palette(Palette.yellow) });
surface.setPad(2, 0, { mode: "flash", colour: palette(Palette.greenBright), alt: palette(Palette.greenDim) });
surface.setPad(3, 0, { mode: "static", colour: rgb(127, 40, 200) });
surface.setPad(4, 0, { mode: "flash", colour: rgb(1, 2, 3), alt: rgb(300, -5, NaN) }); // clamped, NaN -> 0
surface.setPad(5, 0, { mode: "pulse", colour: rgb(1, 2, 3) }); // not renderable: refused, stays off
surface.setButton("logo", { mode: "static", colour: palette(Palette.red) });
surface.setButton("nonexistent", { mode: "static", colour: palette(Palette.red) });
surface.set(0, { mode: "static", colour: palette(1) });
surface.set(11.5, { mode: "static", colour: palette(1) });
surface.set(200, { mode: "static", colour: palette(1) });
surface.setPad(-1, 9, { mode: "static", colour: palette(1) });
emit("surface bulk", surface.flush());
surface.setPad(0, 0, { mode: "off" });
surface.setPad(1, 1, { mode: "static", colour: palette(Palette.greenDim) });
emit("surface short", surface.flush());
emit("surface steady", surface.flush());
emit("peek", [surface.peek(81), surface.peek(82), surface.peek(0), surface.peek(11.5), surface.peek(-3)]);
surface.invalidate();
emit("surface repaint", surface.flush().dirty);
surface.clear();
emit("surface clear", surface.flush().dirty);

// The decoder's other message kinds: pad down/up, aftertouch, every named edge button, an unknown CC, a short
// message, a stray status byte and a data byte that is not MIDI.
const toDecode: number[][] = [[0x90, 81, 127], [0x80, 81, 0], [0x90, 81, 0], [0xa0, 81, 64], [0xd0, 64, 0], [0xb0, 1, 0]];
for (const name of Object.keys(PRO_MK3.buttons)) toDecode.push([0xb0, PRO_MK3.buttons[name], 127]);
toDecode.push([0xb0, 127, 127], [0x90, 81], [0xc0, 1, 2], [0x90, 200, 5], [0x90, PRO_MK3.buttons.down, 127]);
emit("decode", decodeMessages(PRO_MK3, toDecode));

// Identification: a known family, an unknown Novation, junk, and the model question the family cannot answer.
emit("profiles", [profileForFamily([0x13, 0x01])?.name ?? null, profileForFamily([0x37, 0x01]),
  profilesForFamily([0x13, 0x01]).length, familyHex([0x37, 0x01]), deviceName([0x37, 0x01]),
  deviceName([0x13, 0x01]), parseInquiryReply([0xf0, 0x7e]), parseInquiryReply([0x90, 1, 2]),
  isModelReply(PRO_MK3, MODEL_REPLY), isModelReply(PRO_MK3, modelQuery(PRO_MK3))]);

// A scan's other endings: cancelled mid-window, a port API that throws, and a reply landing in the quiet
// between windows (dropped).
const quiet: { [handle: string]: number[][] } = {};
let quietNext = 1;
const late: MidiPortApi = {
  openInputs: (list) => list.map(() => { const h = quietNext++; quiet[String(h)] = []; return h; }),
  openOutput: () => quietNext++,
  send: () => true,
  read: (h) => { const q = quiet[String(h)] ?? []; quiet[String(h)] = []; return q; },
  close: (h) => { delete quiet[String(h)]; },
};
const lateScan = new PortScan(late, ["In"], ["Out 1", "Out 2"], deviceInquiry(), 300);
lateScan.step(0);
lateScan.step(300); // Out 1's window closes
for (const h of Object.keys(quiet)) quiet[h].push([0xf0, 0x01, 0xf7]); // too late for Out 1
for (let t = 310; lateScan.step(t); t += 10) { /* Out 2 goes out after the quiet */ }
emit("late reply", lateScan.status().replies.length);
const cancelled = new PortScan(late, ["In"], ["Out 1", "Out 2"], deviceInquiry(), 300);
cancelled.step(0);
cancelled.cancel();
emit("cancelled", [cancelled.status().busy, cancelled.status().done, cancelled.step(10)]);
const broken = new PortScan({ ...late, read: () => { throw new Error("gone"); } }, ["In"], ["Out"], deviceInquiry(), 300);
broken.step(0);
emit("broken", [broken.status().error, broken.status().done]);
emit("quiet handles", Object.keys(quiet).length);
````

Run: `mkdir -p packages/launchpad/ts/scenario; sed -n '2055,2345p' docs/modular-graph-phase-f3-plan.md > packages/launchpad/ts/scenario/launchpadCore.ts`
Expected: exit 0: the file is the block above, byte for byte.

Run: `git hash-object packages/launchpad/ts/scenario/launchpadCore.ts`
Expected: `dc8a6b94334ea829ae0a3de087176642fd453610`: the blob e4226eaa0 holds for this file, so a retyped slip fails here rather than in a test that never reads the line.

The launchpad-core scenario: every LED form the protocol writes, the decoder's message kinds, each quantise mode, a
session update across a relocate and a generation change, and `PortScan` through its follow-up, cancel, failure and
quiet paths. It is what `build-device-pack.mjs --scenario` runs, and it prints a transcript both engines must agree
on.

Then the tests beside them: `portScan.test.ts` (19 cases: follow-up, cancel, failure, quiet, an echo that confirms
nothing), `profile.test.ts` (3), and `scenario.test.ts` (1, which runs the toolchain and asserts 14 lines of the
transcript - so a run that stopped early cannot pass merely because both engines agreed).

Create `packages/launchpad/ts/test/portScan.test.ts`:

````ts
// PortScan, driven a millisecond at a time over a fake port API.
//
// The scan is the one place RetroPlug writes MIDI at a stranger's gear, and what it records decides which
// pair a control surface gets claimed on - so the cases here pin ATTRIBUTION (a reply belongs to the output
// that was being probed when it arrived, never the next one), what happens to ports that will not open, and
// that every port it opens is closed again. It never interprets a byte: the probe and the replies are
// opaque, exactly as they are to native.
import { test, expect } from "@retroplug/testing";
import { GAP_MS, MAX_REPLIES, PortScan, type MidiPortApi } from "../portScan";

const PROBE = [0xf0, 0x7e, 0x7f, 0x06, 0x01, 0xf7];
const WINDOW = 300;

/** Ports by name. `answer` maps an output to what comes back on which input when it is written to. */
function rig(opts: { answer?: Record<string, { input: string; bytes: number[] }>; busy?: string[] } = {}) {
  const open = new Map<number, { input: boolean; name: string; queue: number[][] }>();
  const log: string[] = [];
  let next = 1;
  let inputCalls = 0;
  const openOne = (input: boolean, name: string): number => {
    if (opts.busy?.includes(name)) return 0;
    const h = next++;
    open.set(h, { input, name, queue: [] });
    log.push(`open ${input ? "in" : "out"} ${name}`);
    return h;
  };
  const api: MidiPortApi = {
    openInputs(names) {
      inputCalls++;
      return names.map((n) => openOne(true, n));
    },
    openOutput: (name) => openOne(false, name),
    send(h, bytes) {
      const p = open.get(h)!;
      log.push(`send ${p.name} ${bytes.length}`);
      const a = opts.answer?.[p.name];
      if (a) for (const q of open.values()) if (q.input && q.name === a.input) q.queue.push(a.bytes);
      return true;
    },
    read(h) {
      const p = open.get(h)!;
      const out = p.queue;
      p.queue = [];
      return out;
    },
    close(h) {
      log.push(`close ${open.get(h)!.name}`);
      open.delete(h);
    },
  };
  const hear = (input: string, bytes: number[]) => {
    for (const q of open.values()) if (q.input && q.name === input) q.queue.push(bytes);
  };
  return { api, log, open, hear, inputCalls: () => inputCalls };
}

function run(scan: PortScan, from = 0): number {
  let t = from;
  while (scan.step(t)) t += 10;
  return t;
}

test("probes every output in turn, one answer window each, and closes everything", () => {
  const r = rig();
  const scan = new PortScan(r.api, ["A in", "B in"], ["A out", "B out"], PROBE, WINDOW);
  const end = run(scan);
  expect(r.log).toEqual([
    "open in A in", "open in B in",
    "open out A out", "send A out 6", "close A out",
    "open out B out", "send B out 6", "close B out",
    "close A in", "close B in",
  ]);
  expect(r.open.size).toBe(0);
  expect(end >= 2 * WINDOW).toBe(true);
  expect(scan.status()).toEqual({ ...scan.status(), busy: false, done: true, phase: "", skipped: 0, replies: [] });
});

test("an answer is tagged with the output probed AND the input it came back on", () => {
  // The two differ - that pairing is the thing a scan exists to discover.
  const r = rig({ answer: { "IF Port B": { input: "IF Port A", bytes: [0xf0, 1, 0xf7] } } });
  const scan = new PortScan(r.api, ["Keys", "IF Port A"], ["Keys", "IF Port B"], PROBE, WINDOW);
  run(scan);
  expect(scan.status().replies).toEqual([{ output: "IF Port B", input: "IF Port A", bytes: [0xf0, 1, 0xf7] }]);
});

test("an answer inside its window counts even if it is only read as the window closes", () => {
  const r = rig();
  const scan = new PortScan(r.api, ["IF in"], ["Out 1", "Out 2"], PROBE, WINDOW);
  scan.step(0); // Out 1 probed
  scan.step(WINDOW - 1);
  r.hear("IF in", [0xf0, 0x11, 0xf7]); // just inside Out 1's window; nothing reads it until the next step
  scan.step(WINDOW); // reads FIRST, then closes Out 1's window
  expect(scan.status().replies.map((x) => x.output)).toEqual(["Out 1"]);
});

test("a late answer lands in the quiet between windows and is dropped, never credited to the next port", () => {
  const r = rig();
  const scan = new PortScan(r.api, ["IF in"], ["Out 1", "Out 2"], PROBE, WINDOW);
  scan.step(0);
  scan.step(WINDOW); // Out 1's window closes; Out 2 is NOT probed yet
  expect(r.log.filter((l) => l.startsWith("send"))).toEqual(["send Out 1 6"]);
  r.hear("IF in", [0xf0, 0x11, 0xf7]); // Out 1's device, late
  scan.step(WINDOW + GAP_MS - 1);
  scan.step(WINDOW + GAP_MS); // the quiet is over: Out 2 goes out now
  expect(scan.status().phase).toBe("Probing Out 2");
  run(scan, WINDOW + GAP_MS + 10);
  expect(scan.status().replies).toEqual([]);
});

test("talk from before the first probe, or after the last window, is not an answer", () => {
  const r = rig();
  const scan = new PortScan(r.api, ["IF in"], ["Out 1"], PROBE, WINDOW);
  r.hear("IF in", [0x90, 60, 1]); // the inputs are open before any probe goes out
  run(scan);
  expect(scan.status().replies).toEqual([]);
});

test("System Real-Time is the stream within the stream, never a reply", () => {
  const r = rig({ answer: { Out: { input: "In", bytes: [0xf8] } } });
  const scan = new PortScan(r.api, ["In"], ["Out"], PROBE, WINDOW);
  scan.step(0);
  r.hear("In", [0xfe]);
  r.hear("In", [0xfa]);
  run(scan, 10);
  expect(scan.status().replies).toEqual([]);
});

test("ports that will not open are counted and stepped over, not fatal", () => {
  const r = rig({ busy: ["Held in", "Held out"], answer: { "Free out": { input: "Free in", bytes: [0xf0, 0xf7] } } });
  const scan = new PortScan(r.api, ["Held in", "Free in"], ["Held out", "Free out"], PROBE, WINDOW);
  run(scan);
  expect(scan.status().skipped).toBe(2);
  expect(scan.status().replies.length).toBe(1);
});

test("a rig with nothing to probe finishes on its first step", () => {
  const r = rig();
  const scan = new PortScan(r.api, ["In"], [], PROBE, WINDOW);
  expect(scan.step(0)).toBe(false);
  expect(scan.status().done).toBe(true);
  expect(r.open.size).toBe(0);
});

test("only SysEx is a reply, so a fader ride cannot hide the device", () => {
  // A controller sending CCs every frame must not fill the reply cap before the Launchpad, asked third, has
  // answered.
  const DEVICE = [0xf0, 0x7e, 0x00, 0x06, 0x02, 0x00, 0x20, 0x29, 0x13, 0x01, 0, 0, 0, 1, 2, 3, 0xf7];
  const r = rig({ answer: { "LP out": { input: "LP in", bytes: DEVICE } } });
  const scan = new PortScan(r.api, ["Faders", "LP in"], ["Faders", "Other", "LP out"], PROBE, WINDOW);
  for (let t = 0; scan.step(t); t += 16) {
    for (let k = 0; k < 5; k++) r.hear("Faders", [0xb0, 7, (t + k) & 0x7f]);
    r.hear("Faders", [0x90, 60, 100]);
    r.hear("Faders", [0xd0, 40]);
  }
  expect(scan.status().replies).toEqual([{ output: "LP out", input: "LP in", bytes: DEVICE }]);
});

test("replies are capped, so a port flooding SysEx cannot grow the list without bound", () => {
  const r = rig();
  const scan = new PortScan(r.api, ["Chatty"], ["Out"], PROBE, WINDOW);
  scan.step(0);
  for (let i = 0; i < MAX_REPLIES + 20; i++) r.hear("Chatty", [0xf0, i & 0x7f, 0xf7]);
  run(scan, 10);
  expect(scan.status().replies.length).toBe(MAX_REPLIES);
});

test("every input is opened in ONE call, so a host steps its own stream aside once per scan", () => {
  const r = rig({ busy: ["Held A", "Held B"] });
  const scan = new PortScan(r.api, ["Held A", "Held B", "Free"], ["Out"], PROBE, WINDOW);
  run(scan);
  expect(r.inputCalls()).toBe(1);
  expect(scan.status().skipped).toBe(2);
});

test("a port API that throws ends the scan with the error, and every port it opened is closed", () => {
  const r = rig();
  const api: MidiPortApi = { ...r.api, read: () => { throw new Error("device vanished"); } };
  const scan = new PortScan(api, ["A", "B"], ["Out"], PROBE, WINDOW);
  expect(scan.step(0)).toBe(false);
  expect(scan.status().error).toBe("device vanished");
  expect(scan.status().done).toBe(true);
  expect(r.open.size).toBe(0); // a host would otherwise keep its shared MIDI inputs suspended until quit
});

test("cancel closes every port and keeps what was gathered", () => {
  const r = rig({ answer: { "Out 1": { input: "In", bytes: [0xf0, 0xf7] } } });
  const scan = new PortScan(r.api, ["In"], ["Out 1", "Out 2"], PROBE, WINDOW);
  scan.step(0);
  scan.step(5);
  scan.cancel();
  expect(r.open.size).toBe(0);
  expect(scan.status().busy).toBe(false);
  expect(scan.status().replies.length).toBe(1);
});

test("a follow-up is asked on the SAME pair while it is open, and its answer gets a window of its own", () => {
  // How a scan confirms WHAT answered without reopening anything: reopening would cost a Windows host another
  // round of stepping its MIDI stream aside, and a port grabbed in between would make a real device look silent.
  const r = rig({ answer: { "IF out": { input: "IF in", bytes: [0xf0, 0x7e, 0x01, 0xf7] } } });
  const ASK = [0xf0, 0x00, 0x20, 0x29, 0x02, 0x0e, 0x00, 0xf7];
  const scan = new PortScan(r.api, ["IF in"], ["IF out", "Other"], PROBE, WINDOW, {
    followUp: (reply) => (reply.bytes[2] === 0x01 ? [ASK] : []),
  });
  scan.step(0); // the inquiry goes out and is answered at once
  scan.step(WINDOW - 10); // the reply is read, and the follow-up sent - restarting the window
  expect(r.log.filter((l) => l.startsWith("send"))).toEqual(["send IF out 6", "send IF out 8"]);
  r.hear("IF in", [0xf0, 0x00, 0x20, 0x29, 0x02, 0x0e, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0xf7]); // the model answers late-ish
  scan.step(WINDOW + 50); // past the ORIGINAL window, inside the restarted one
  expect(scan.status().phase).toBe("Probing IF out");
  run(scan, WINDOW + 60);
  expect(scan.status().replies.some((x) => x.output === "IF out" && x.bytes.length === 10)).toBe(true);
});

test("a follow-up goes out once per output, however many inputs the device was heard on", () => {
  const r = rig();
  const ASK = [0xf0, 0x01, 0xf7];
  let asked = 0;
  const api: MidiPortApi = { ...r.api, send: (h, b) => { if (b.length === 3) asked++; return r.api.send(h, b); } };
  const scan = new PortScan(api, ["A", "B"], ["Out"], PROBE, WINDOW, { followUp: () => [ASK] });
  scan.step(0);
  r.hear("A", [0xf0, 0x7e, 0xf7]); // a merge: the same answer on two inputs
  r.hear("B", [0xf0, 0x7e, 0xf7]);
  run(scan, 10);
  expect(asked).toBe(1);
});

test("a status handed out is never mutated by a later step", () => {
  // Held at EVERY step, not just the first: a mutation once a probe is under way is the case that matters.
  const r = rig({ busy: ["Gone"], answer: { Out: { input: "In", bytes: [0xf0, 0xf7] } } });
  const scan = new PortScan(r.api, ["In"], ["Gone", "Out"], PROBE, WINDOW);
  const held: { status: ReturnType<PortScan["status"]>; snapshot: string }[] = [];
  for (let t = 0; ; t += 10) {
    const st = scan.status();
    held.push({ status: st, snapshot: JSON.stringify(st) });
    if (!scan.step(t)) break;
  }
  held.push({ status: scan.status(), snapshot: JSON.stringify(scan.status()) });
  for (const h of held) expect(JSON.stringify(h.status)).toBe(h.snapshot);
  expect(scan.status().replies.length).toBe(1);
});

test("the version strictly increases on every change - a probe, a reply, the end", () => {
  // A poller re-renders on version alone, so a change that does not move it freezes the Settings row.
  const r = rig({ answer: { "Out 1": { input: "In", bytes: [0xf0, 0x01, 0xf7] } } });
  const scan = new PortScan(r.api, ["In"], ["Out 1", "Out 2"], PROBE, WINDOW);
  let last = scan.status();
  let changes = 0;
  for (let t = 0; ; t += 10) {
    const busy = scan.step(t);
    const now = scan.status();
    if (now !== last) {
      expect(now.version > last.version).toBe(true);
      changes++;
    } else {
      expect(now.version).toBe(last.version);
    }
    last = now;
    if (!busy) break;
  }
  expect(changes >= 5).toBe(true); // probe 1, reply, window close, probe 2, window close, finish
});

test("one close that throws does not leave the other ports open", () => {
  const r = rig();
  let first = true;
  const api: MidiPortApi = {
    ...r.api,
    close(h) {
      if (first) { first = false; throw new Error("close failed"); }
      r.api.close(h);
    },
  };
  const scan = new PortScan(api, ["A", "B", "C"], [], PROBE, WINDOW);
  scan.step(0); // nothing to probe: finishes, closing all three inputs
  expect(scan.status().done).toBe(true);
  expect(scan.status().error).toBe("close failed");
  expect(r.open.size).toBe(1); // only the one whose close threw; the other two closed
});

test("a wall clock stepping backwards neither stalls nor rushes the scan", () => {
  // An NTP correction mid-scan. Time measured off the raw clock would hold the window open until the clock
  // caught up - an hour, for an hour's step - with every input held the whole time.
  const r = rig();
  const scan = new PortScan(r.api, ["In"], ["Out 1", "Out 2"], PROBE, WINDOW);
  scan.step(1_000_000);
  scan.step(1_000_000 + 100);
  scan.step(1_000_000 - 3_600_000); // back an hour: no time passes
  expect(scan.status().phase).toBe("Probing Out 1");
  let t = 1_000_000 - 3_600_000;
  let steps = 0;
  while (scan.step((t += 10))) steps++;
  expect(steps < 100).toBe(true); // finished in about the scan's own length, not an hour
});
````

````ts
// The per-model facts every other file reads: the grid's coordinate flip, the button table, and the family bytes a
// Device Inquiry can and cannot identify a model by.
import { test, expect } from "@retroplug/testing";
import {
  PRO_MK3, PROFILES, GRID_SIZE, familyHex, deviceName, isPad, padIndex, padAt, buttonName, profileForFamily,
  profilesForFamily,
} from "../profile";

test("the grid's coordinates flip exactly once: the manual's three stated anchors", () => {
  // The device counts rows upwards from the bottom, as row * 10 + col + 11; this module presents a top-left origin.
  expect(padIndex({ x: 0, y: 7 })).toBe(11);
  expect(padIndex({ x: 0, y: 0 })).toBe(81);
  expect(padIndex({ x: 7, y: 7 })).toBe(18);
  expect(padAt(11)).toEqual({ x: 0, y: 7 });
  expect(padAt(81)).toEqual({ x: 0, y: 0 });
  expect(padAt(18)).toEqual({ x: 7, y: 7 });
  // Off-grid coordinates and edge-button numbers are not pads, rather than a nonsense index.
  expect(padIndex({ x: -1, y: 0 })).toBe(-1);
  expect(padAt(19)).toBe(null);
  expect(padAt(10)).toBe(null);
  expect(padAt(0)).toBe(null);
  expect(isPad({ x: GRID_SIZE, y: 0 })).toBe(false);
  expect(isPad({ x: 0.5, y: 0 })).toBe(false);
});

test("every named button reverse-looks-up to itself, and an unknown CC is nothing", () => {
  const names = Object.keys(PRO_MK3.buttons);
  expect(names.length).toBe(33);
  for (const name of names) expect(buttonName(PRO_MK3, PRO_MK3.buttons[name])).toBe(name);
  expect(buttonName(PRO_MK3, 1)).toBe(null);
});

test("family bytes find a model but do not identify one: Novation reuses them", () => {
  // The Mini MK3 and the Pro MK3 both answer 13 01, which is why the scan asks the model its own question.
  expect(profilesForFamily([0x13, 0x01])).toEqual([PRO_MK3]);
  expect(profileForFamily([0x13, 0x01])).toBe(PRO_MK3);
  expect(profileForFamily([0x0d, 0x01])).toBe(null); // an unknown family: no profile, but still a Novation
  expect(profilesForFamily([0x0d, 0x01])).toEqual([]);
  expect(familyHex([0x0d, 0x01])).toBe("0d 01");
  expect(deviceName([0x13, 0x01])).toBe(PRO_MK3.name);
  expect(deviceName([0x0d, 0x01])).toBe("Novation device (family 0d 01)");
  // The table is by a short key, and its family bytes are the ones profileForFamily matches.
  expect(PROFILES["pro-mk3"]).toBe(PRO_MK3);
});
````
