Create `packages/launchpad/ts/test/scenario.test.ts`:

````ts
// The Launchpad core's scenario (packages/launchpad/ts/scenario/launchpadCore.ts) through the device-pack
// toolchain's scenario mode (packages/retroplug/scripts/build-device-pack.mjs): bundled, lowered to ES5, scanned for
// library calls MicroQuickJS lacks, then run under Node and on build/bin/retroplug-mqjs-run, whose transcripts must
// agree byte for byte inside the heap it is given.
//
// The toolchain is Node's (esbuild and TypeScript are not txiki modules), so this runs it in a node child: the runner's
// own node (RP_NODE, which scripts/run-tests.mjs sets), else the node on the PATH when run by hand.
import { test, expect } from "@retroplug/testing";

// Just enough of txiki's spawn and a child's pipe, declared locally as bundle-no-zod.test.ts does.
interface ByteStream {
  getReader(): { read(): Promise<{ done: boolean; value?: Uint8Array }> };
}
declare const tjs: {
  env: Record<string, string | undefined>;
  readFile(path: string): Promise<Uint8Array>;
  spawn(
    args: string[],
    opts: { stdout: "pipe"; stderr: "pipe" },
  ): {
    stdout: ByteStream | null;
    stderr: ByteStream | null;
    wait(): Promise<{ exit_status: number; term_signal: string | null }>;
  };
};

async function text(stream: ByteStream | null): Promise<string> {
  if (!stream) return "";
  const chunks: Uint8Array[] = [];
  const reader = stream.getReader();
  for (;;) {
    const { done, value } = await reader.read();
    if (done) break;
    if (value) chunks.push(value);
  }
  let total = 0;
  for (const c of chunks) total += c.length;
  const all = new Uint8Array(total);
  let at = 0;
  for (const c of chunks) {
    all.set(c, at);
    at += c.length;
  }
  return new TextDecoder().decode(all);
}

// The suite runs from packages/retroplug.
const SCENARIO = "../../packages/launchpad/ts/scenario/launchpadCore.ts";
const PACK_DIR = "../../packages/launchpad";
const OUT = ".test-build/launchpad-scenario";
// The least heap the run needs, measured on this tree by bisecting --heap-bytes: it passes at 61552 bytes and fails
// below 61300. The budget is 1.25x that, so a path the scenario adds shows up as a refusal rather than quietly needing
// more. It is the scenario's own figure, not a claim about the box's 64 KiB arena (there is no Pico controller path).
const LEAST_HEAP = 61300;
const HEAP = Math.ceil(LEAST_HEAP * 1.25 / 256) * 256; // 76800

async function runScenario(): Promise<{ ok: boolean; out: string; err: string }> {
  const args = [tjs.env.RP_NODE || "node", "scripts/build-device-pack.mjs", "--scenario", SCENARIO,
                "--name", "launchpad-core", "--heap-bytes", String(HEAP), "--out-dir", OUT, "--pack-dir", PACK_DIR];
  const child = tjs.spawn(args, { stdout: "pipe", stderr: "pipe" });
  // Both pipes drained beside the wait, so a child that fills one cannot block on it.
  const [out, err, status] = await Promise.all([text(child.stdout), text(child.stderr), child.wait()]);
  return { ok: !status.term_signal && status.exit_status === 0, out, err };
}

test("the Launchpad core runs on MicroQuickJS as on Node, byte for byte", async () => {
  const run = await runScenario();
  expect(run.ok, `the toolchain refused the scenario:\n${run.out}${run.err}`).toBe(true);
  expect(run.out.includes("matches Node byte for byte")).toBe(true);
  expect(run.out.includes("device pack scenario launchpad-core OK")).toBe(true);
  expect(run.out.includes("no library calls outside MicroQuickJS's stdlib, in the pack or anywhere in the SDK")).toBe(true);
  // The package's WHOLE core is scanned, not only what the scenario reaches: the scan is the guard a path neither the
  // scenario nor a node runs. (It is what caught launchMessage's Number.isInteger, which tree shaking had dropped.)
  expect(run.out.includes("no library calls outside MicroQuickJS's stdlib, in the core's ")).toBe(true);

  // The transcript the two engines agreed on, kept beside the outputs: it has the sections the scenario claims to
  // walk, so a run that silently stopped early cannot pass on the two engines merely agreeing.
  const transcript = new TextDecoder().decode(
    await tjs.readFile(`${OUT}/launchpad-core.transcript.txt`),
  );
  const lines = transcript.split("\n");
  expect(lines.length > 25, `${lines.length} transcript lines`).toBe(true);
  for (const part of [
    'connect [[240,0,32,41,2,14,14,1,247]]', // Programmer mode
    "reconnect 43 [[240,0,32,41,2,14,14,1,247]]", // a generation change mid-run re-takes the device
    "ticks 480", // and the seek after it advanced the model nothing
    '"phase":"","error":"","skipped":2',
    'found {"input":"IF A in","output":"IF B out","name":"Launchpad Pro [MK3]"}',
    "model reply [[240,126,0,6,2,0,32,41,19,1,0,0,0,1,2,3,247],false]", // an echo confirms nothing
    "model reply [[240,0,32,41,2,14,0,0,0,247],true]",
    "surface bulk ",
    "surface steady",
    "decode [",
    "profiles [",
    "late reply 0",
    "cancelled [false,true,false]",
    'broken ["gone",true]',
  ])
    expect(transcript.includes(part), part).toBe(true);
});
````

`packages/retroplug/scripts/build-device-pack.mjs` gains `--scenario <file.ts>`, and it is more than a flag: it
bundles **every module under the pack directory's `ts/`** but its `test/` and `testSupport/` (with `treeShaking:

dependencies (a node pack's allowlist does not: `--entry` and `--scenario` name different things, and passing both is
refused). It lowers to ES5, scans the lowered core for library calls MicroQuickJS lacks, runs the scenario under
**Node** and under **`retroplug-mqjs-run`**, requires the two transcripts to be byte-identical, checks the heap
against `--heap-bytes`, and writes **no pack**: a scenario is not a pack, and `launchpad` has no `script` member. The
whole-core scan is the part a review forced. The first version scanned only the scenario's own import graph, and a
`Number.isInteger` in `ts/trackerTarget.ts` that no scenario path called survived it; the fix pass widened the scan to
every module and found it (and the registry's `Map`). The refusals are the toolchain's own: "no core to scan", "the
package's core calls library functions MicroQuickJS does not have" (naming the helper and the file), the undeclared
scenario import, "the scenario prints nothing, so it proves nothing ran", "the scenario threw under Node", and a
transcript that "disagrees with Node".

- [ ] **Step 8: The store's clean app config, red first**

The branch's `beb451cbd`: a `setController` patch that names a DIFFERENT app replaces that app's config with the
patch's, so the old app's knobs no longer ride along in the `.rplg`; a patch that names the same app still merges, one
knob at a time. The case lives in the store's tests (`test/project/controller.test.ts`, one case), not in the menu's,
and `test/project/tolerance.test.ts` gains the malformed-controller case.

````diff

    *  the controller node is placed from these settings at each publish, so a change that was never published would
    *  leave the audio thread running the previous app.
-   *  `appConfig` merges rather than replaces, so a menu row can set one knob without knowing the others. */
+   *  `appConfig` merges one knob at a time into the app's own config, so a menu row can set one knob without knowing
+   *  the others; a DIFFERENT app starts from what the patch gives it, because the old app's keys mean nothing to it
+   *  and merging kept them in the .rplg forever. */
   setController(patch: Partial<ControllerSettings>): void {
     const current = this.projectSettings.controller;
-    this.projectSettings = {
-      ...this.projectSettings,
-      controller: { ...current, ...patch, appConfig: { ...current.appConfig, ...(patch.appConfig ?? {}) } },
-    };
+    const switching = patch.app !== undefined && patch.app !== current.app;
+    const appConfig = switching ? { ...(patch.appConfig ?? {}) } : { ...current.appConfig, ...(patch.appConfig ?? {}) };
+    this.projectSettings = { ...this.projectSettings, controller: { ...current, ...patch, appConfig } };
     this.markDirty();
     this.publishGraph(false);
     this.notifySystemsChange();
````

Create `packages/retroplug/test/project/controller.test.ts`:

````ts
// setController's app config: one knob at a time merges into the app's config, but a DIFFERENT app starts from what
// the patch gives it. Merging across a switch kept every key of every app ever chosen in the .rplg, handed to
// whichever app came next.
import { test, expect } from "@retroplug/testing";
import { MockBackend } from "../../testing/mockBackend";
import { RecentStore } from "../../src/recentStore";
import { ProjectStore } from "../../src/projectStore";
import { buildAppRegistry } from "../../src/appHost";

function newProject(): ProjectStore {
  const be = new MockBackend("/cfg");
  return new ProjectStore(be, new RecentStore(be), buildAppRegistry());
}

test("switching to a different app starts it from a clean config, not the old app's knobs", () => {
  const project = newProject();
  project.setController({ appConfig: { follow: false, quantise: "beat" } });
  project.setController({ app: "some-other-app", appConfig: {} });
  expect(project.settings().controller.appConfig).toEqual({});
  project.setController({ app: "some-other-app", appConfig: { x: 1 } }); // the same app: merges as before
  project.setController({ appConfig: { y: 2 } });
  expect(project.settings().controller.appConfig).toEqual({ x: 1, y: 2 });
});
````

- [ ] **Step 9: The session node's fixes, red first**

The node and the session carry the branch's behaviour and this stage's two corrections. The **relocate** is the one
the review called Critical: a tick jump larger than a block can cover is a seek, not elapsed time, and the threshold
must be the PREVIOUS block's projected end (`ppq * 24 + frames / sampleRate * (tempo / 60) * 24`), with the walk's own
one tick of slack - the first answer measured the previous block against the current one's length and drifted on
ragged blocks. The **generation** re-anchor and the **drop repaint** ride on the same code: the session re-takes the
device when `controllerConnected` changes (it carries the link's generation as a number, 0 for nothing attached), and
repaints when `controllerDrops` rises. `controllerDrops` is a new control input of the node and is unwired by
`buildGraph` until Task 3 gives `surface-in` its `drops` output; an omitted input reads 0, so every existing document
behaves as before. The test file carries the cases: `ragged blocks and a tempo change are elapsed time, not a seek:
the playhead keeps every tick` (two patterns at 44.1 kHz, a long block then a short one at 240 BPM, and a tempo drop
between two large blocks), `a forward seek is a relocate` (the 16-row table, so a walked 200-tick jump lands on row 2
rather than wrapping), the generation re-take, the drop repaint, and the anchor case whose stimulus changed from four
quarters to 200 small blocks because under the relocate rule that jump IS a seek. `test-native/lsdj-launchpad` and
`-role` and parity's controller group name the package's paths and nothing else.

````diff
+test("ragged blocks and a tempo change are elapsed time, not a seek: the playhead keeps every tick", () => {
+  // A host under FL-style splits hands the audio thread uneven blocks, and a tempo change makes a long block hold
+  // fewer ticks than the one before it. What a block covers comes from its OWN length and tempo, so neither is a
+  // seek; a threshold measured against the PREVIOUS block's elapsed ticks would read both as one and drop the
+  // block's ticks, leaving the lit playhead (and what the app quantises against) behind the cart.
+  const quarters = (frames: number, tempo: number) => (frames / 44100) * (tempo / 60); // 44.1 kHz, 24 PPQN
+  const patterns: Array<[string, ReadonlyArray<readonly [number, number]>]> = [
+    ["a long block then a short one", [[4096, 240], [2048, 240]]],
+    ["a tempo drop between two long blocks", [[4096, 240], [4096, 120]]],
+  ];
+  for (const [name, pattern] of patterns) {
+    const rig = quiet(); // rows 0 and 1 of 96 ticks each
+    const dev = new Device();

+    dev.feed(rig.run(blockOf({ playing: true, ppq, connected: true, tempo: firstTempo, surface: [PRESS_ROW_0] }, firstFrames)));
+    ppq += quarters(firstFrames, firstTempo);
+    for (let cycle = 1; cycle < 8; cycle++) {
+      for (const [frames, tempo] of pattern) {
````

````ts
// A node pack whose manifest DECLARES the package it imports: a node pack's allowlist is still its own directory and
// the portable node SDK, so the toolchain must refuse the import, naming the module and its importer
// (test/graph/device-pack.test.ts). Only a scenario may reach its declared dependencies.
import { decodeMessage } from "@retroplug/launchpad/decode";
import { PRO_MK3 } from "@retroplug/launchpad/profile";
import { defineNode, events } from "@retroplug/core/defineNode";
import { registerScriptNodes } from "@retroplug/core/register";

export const decode = defineNode({
  id: "rp.test.device.decode",
  ports: { in: events.in() },
  create: () => ({
    process(b) {
      const messages = b.messages("in");
      for (let i = 0; i < messages.length; i++) decodeMessage(PRO_MK3, messages[i].data);
    },
  }),
});

registerScriptNodes([decode]);
````

````ts
// A core module whose missing call nothing in the scenario reaches: the whole-core scan is the only guard a path
// neither the scenario nor a node runs has.

/** Whole-number check the ES5 way, as the portable core has to write it. */
export function whole(n: number): boolean {
  return typeof n === "number" && Math.floor(n) === n;
}

/** The launchable row check, which MicroQuickJS would fail on: it has no Number.isInteger. Nothing calls it. */
export function launchable(row: number): boolean {
  return Number.isInteger(row) && row >= 0 && row <= 253;
}
````

(The `TinyUSB submodule has not been initialized` hint above it is `/opt/pico-sdk`'s own: the check needs no USB, which is why it uses that SDK.)

An image carries the day it was built: the Pico SDK's standard binary info stamps it with `__DATE__`
(`pico_standard_binary_info`, since nothing sets `PICO_NO_BI_PROGRAM_BUILD_DATE`), once, a fixed-length string. So the
check counts that string (it must be exactly one) and hashes a copy with it normalised to 8 November 2026, as
`/tmp/f3pro/norm-sha.sh` normalises it for the baseline's and every stage's run; nothing else may differ, and the
sizes the device scripts print do not move with the date. The bytes also rest on the build's inputs, so a hash
compares only an image built from this worktree's path, against the same SDK checkouts (`/opt/pico-sdk` for the check,
`/workspaces/pico-sdk` for the box), the same Pico-PIO-USB checkout (`/workspaces/Pico-PIO-USB`) and
`arm-none-eabi-g++` 13.2.1.

Run: `bash -c 'R="(Jan|Feb|Mar|Apr|May|Jun|Jul|Aug|Sep|Oct|Nov|Dec) [ 0-9][0-9] 20[0-9]{2}"; for e in build-device/rp-device-check.elf; do arm-none-eabi-objcopy -O binary $e /tmp/f3-img.bin && LC_ALL=C grep -a -c -E "$R" /tmp/f3-img.bin && LC_ALL=C sed -E "s/$R/Nov  8 2026/" /tmp/f3-img.bin | sha256sum; done; rm -f /tmp/f3-img.bin'`

````bash
git commit -F - <<'EOF'
feat(launchpad): the package's TS core, its session node and a scenario

Create @retroplug/launchpad and move the generic controller TypeScript into it: the Launchpad
protocol (profile, message encoding, decoding, surface diff), the controller session, the app
registry mechanism, PortScan, the launch target contract and the two controller-owned port/enum
declarations. The moved files are git renames and every importer names the package's path: the
shell's launchpad/controller shims and the dead src/script/shellNodes.ts are gone. The LSDj app, its
target and the predictor wiring move with the node for this stage; the lsdj-launchpad bridge takes
them back next.

Port feature/launchpad's TypeScript fixes onto the moved code: the portable rules (arrays instead of
Map, indexed loops, no ES2015 library calls), PortScan with its follow-up, cancel, failure and quiet
paths, Model Query confirmation for the Mini/Pro MK3 family the Device Inquiry cannot tell apart,
the surface's dirty shortcut and array slots, the decoder's data-byte and note-vs-CC guards, the
app's needsPaint / grid revision, isTickCount, the session node's link generation and drop repaint,
and setController starting a different app from a clean config. The node gains a controllerDrops
control input; buildGraph leaves it unwired until surface-in reports drops.

The relocate compares the previous block's PROJECTED END, from its own frames and tempo, as
walkTicks resyncs: a block that starts more than a tick past it is a seek. Measuring the previous
block's elapsed ticks against the current block's length read a ragged split or a tempo drop as a
seek and dropped an ordinary block's ticks, so the lit playhead fell behind the cart. The node's
seek case asserts the playhead's colour, which the earlier row-content assertion could not; and an
anchor case now walks 200 small blocks where it jumped four quarters, because that jump is a seek,
as it is on the branch.

The scenario mode of build-device-pack.mjs bundles, lowers and scans a scenario, runs it under Node
and MicroQuickJS and requires byte-identical transcripts in the heap it is given; it also scans the
package's WHOLE core, every module under its ts/ but its tests with exports kept, which is the guard
for a path the scenario never runs. It takes no node entry, refuses an import outside the scenario's
allowlist (the package's declared dependencies, which a node pack still does not get), a silent,
throwing or engine-disagreeing scenario, and --entry with --scenario. The launchpad core's scenario
is run by pnpm test and its transcript is kept beside the outputs and asserted.

The shell's protocol member goes: rp.controller.session is the launchpad package's node (label 22).
Temporarily, launchpad depends on lsdj (the predictor) and lists after it in the product order, until
the bridge package owns that wiring.
EOF
````

---

### Task 2: the controllerApps kind, and the LSDj bridge that contributes MI.MAP

Design sections 2, 4 and 9's second stage. The controller app becomes a **contribution kind**, and the MI.MAP app leaves
`launchpad` for a bridge package that depends on both sides: `packages/lsdj-launchpad` contributes the app's control plane
(its id, its label, its zod schema and its menu rows) through the `app` member, and its runtime (a factory, a playback
model and a launch target) through `protocol.apps`, joined by id. Neither `lsdj` nor `launchpad` learns about the other,
which is the brainstorm's choice C, and `launchpad` loses its `lsdj` dependency and its apps, so the product order
returns to `core launchpad ... lsdj lsdj-launchpad ...`.

Three things make the kind work, and each is the design's section 4 read against this tree:

- **The runtime half names a MODULE, not functions.** A manifest is JSON, so `protocol.apps` is
  `[{ id, module, syncOverride? }]` and the module default-exports `{ id, factory, playbackModel, target }`, which is the
  shape `protocol.nodes` already has. `protocol.module` becomes **optional** for a package that declares only apps; a
  module named with no nodes to export is refused.
- **The sync override is manifest data**: `{ node, mode, listening, off }`. The first version was a function in a fourth
  generated module, which the review found declared the override twice; a function cannot live in a manifest, and the
  planner must not read the generated `packages.ts` (it imports every app module and so every app's zod, and
  `bundle-protocol.test.ts` holds `buildGraph` to no app and no zod). So the generator validates the data, renders it
  into `generated/protocol.ts` as `CONTROLLER_SYNC`, and the shell's `controllerSyncOverride` reads it by the stored app
  id and applies it to the cart sync node of that type, holding no node type and no app id.
- **The refusals are split by what is visible where.** A duplicate runtime id is refused statically by the generator,
  naming both packages; a duplicate control-plane id and both unpaired halves are refused at load by the generated
  `packages.ts`, the only place both halves are visible; the script entry holds the registered runtimes to the
  manifests' ids and registers them **before** the session node.

And the fix this stage owes the one before it: **the session counts the ticks the host clocked**, which is why one
`ProtocolNodes` digest is re-recorded here rather than in Task 3. The prototype's stage 3 recorded it, and the design's
section 12 says it was the tick fix that moved it; the last fix pass proved that (the tree with the old literal fails,
and the pack's surface nodes change no byte of it) and folded the literal into this commit, so this task's tree is green
on the engine-graph binary and Task 3's is too.

- [ ] **Step 2: The bridge package**

`packages/lsdj-launchpad/package.json` is the kind's worked example: `exports` with **no bare `.`** (so the bare
specifier cannot load zod, which `bundle-no-zod` pins), `./app` (the control plane: `definePackage({ controllerApps
})` with the id `lsdj-midimap`, the label "LSDj MI.MAP", the zod schema for `quantise`, `follow` and `page`, and the
menu rows the app supplies), `./appRuntime` (the runtime: `{ id, factory, playbackModel, target }`, importing
`@retroplug/lsdj/playback/predict`, the leaf, so no WRAM reader and no sav codec reach the bundle), `./launchTarget`
and `./lsdjMidiMap`; and the `retroplug` member: `app: ts/app.ts` and `protocol.apps` with the runtime module and the
sync override `{ node: "rp.lsdj.sync", mode: "midiMap", listening: "MidiMap", off: "off" }`. Its dependencies are
`core`, `launchpad`, `lsdj`, `tracker` and `zod`. `launchpad`'s own additions are the kind's mechanism and its
contract: `packageContributions.ts` is the `declare module "@retroplug/core/definePackage"` augmentation that declares
`controllerApps`, as `tracker` and `dsp` declare theirs, and `launchTarget.ts` is `nullTarget(maxRow)` and the
contract both the bridge and the station's own tests use.

Create `packages/lsdj-launchpad/ts/app.ts`:

````ts
// The LSDj bridge's contribution to the app (docs/modular-graph-phase-f3-design.md sections 2 and 4): the control
// plane's half of the MI.MAP controller app - its id, the menu's label and the knobs' schema. The runtime half (the app,
// its playback model and its launch target) is the package's `protocol.apps` entry, ts/appRuntime.ts, and the two are
// joined by id. Which sync mode the cart those launches drive must be in is the same entry's `syncOverride` data
// (package.json), which graph/controller.ts applies: data, not code, because the planner must carry no app and no zod.
//
// The direction is the reason this package exists: neither lsdj nor launchpad knows the other, so neither names this
// app. The bridge imports both, contributes the app to the app's registry and to the script bundle's, and the control
// plane's schema is here too - so the control plane has the schema and the bundle has none of it.
import { definePackage } from "@retroplug/core/definePackage";
import { z } from "zod";
import { boolField, clampedInt, enumField } from "@retroplug/core/configFields";
import type { ControllerAppContribution } from "@retroplug/launchpad/registry";
import { MAX_PAGE, QUANTISE_VALUES } from "./lsdjMidiMap";
// The key the launchpad package adds to the contract (its ts/packageContributions.ts augments it): type-only, so nothing
// of it loads at run time.
import type {} from "@retroplug/launchpad/packageContributions";

/** MIDI note rows 254 and 255 are the MI.MAP handshake and clock sentinels, so the page's last row is one short. */
const MI_MAP: ControllerAppContribution = {
  id: "lsdj-midimap",
  label: "LSDj MI.MAP",
  // quantise: when a pressed pad's launch actually fires. Default `bar` - one bar is also exactly one LSDj phrase at the
  // factory groove, so launches land where the music does. follow: scroll the 16-row window to keep the playhead
  // visible. page: which window to start on.
  config: z.object({
    quantise: enumField(QUANTISE_VALUES, "bar"),
    follow: boolField(true),
    page: clampedInt(0, MAX_PAGE, 0),
  }),
};

export default definePackage({
  controllerApps: [MI_MAP],
});
````

Create `packages/lsdj-launchpad/ts/appRuntime.ts`:

````ts
// The MI.MAP app's RUNTIME half (docs/modular-graph-phase-f3-design.md section 4): the app function, the playback model
// it reads and its launch target, registered by the generated script entry before the session node (whose own module
// names no app). No schema: a script pack's bundle carries no zod, and neither does this module.
//
// The predictor is the leaf, not @retroplug/lsdj/playback: that barrel also exports the observed model and the
// sav-derived table builder, which would pull the WRAM reader and the whole sav codec into the bundle.
import type { ControllerAppRuntime, ControllerPlaybackModel } from "@retroplug/launchpad/apps";
import { PredictedLsdjModel, normaliseRowTicks } from "@retroplug/lsdj/playback/predict";
import { lsdjMidiMap } from "./lsdjMidiMap";
import { lsdjMidiMapTarget } from "./launchTarget";

/** The predictor over the song's per-row timing table. The table is whatever shape the app's song type has, and
 *  `normaliseRowTicks` is the one place that reads it. */
const playbackModel = (songRowTicks: unknown): ControllerPlaybackModel =>
  PredictedLsdjModel.fromRowTicks(normaliseRowTicks(songRowTicks));

const runtime: ControllerAppRuntime = {
  id: "lsdj-midimap",
  factory: () => lsdjMidiMap,
  playbackModel,
  target: lsdjMidiMapTarget,
};

export default runtime;
````

````ts
// Where a controller app's row launches go (docs/modular-graph-phase-f3-design.md section 4): the contract between an
// app and whichever wire its launches reach. The app decides WHICH row to launch; the target owns what that means.
//
// The implementation belongs to the app's owner, not here: the MI.MAP target that encodes a row as a NoteOn lives with
// the LSDj bridge (@retroplug/lsdj-launchpad/launchTarget), because the note numbers are MI.MAP's protocol and this
// package knows no tracker. A host builds the target and hands the session a `send` that reaches the cart.
//
// A target that discards everything is here rather than with a tracker, because it names no wire: it is what a session
// with no cart attached yet runs, so an app can light its grid and respond to presses before one exists.

/** A sink for row launches. Implementations own the wire format; the app only names rows. */
export interface TrackerTarget {
  /** The highest launchable row. An app uses this to bound its grid rather than assuming 255. */
  readonly maxRow: number;
  launch(row: number): void;
  /** Release the launched row - the app's own release message, if it has one. */
  release(row: number): void;
}

/** A target that discards everything - for a session with no cart attached yet, so an app can light its grid and
 *  respond to presses without a launch path existing. `maxRow` is the app's own range: this knows no tracker's. */
export function nullTarget(maxRow: number): TrackerTarget {
  return { maxRow, launch(): void {}, release(): void {} };
}
````

`config` as the package's own schema, and this task's `menu` rows), `ControllerRegistry`, and no app function and no
mode string. `apps/index.ts` is the runtime side: `ControllerAppRuntime` (`id`, `factory`, `playbackModel`, `target`),
`registerControllerApps`, `controllerApp(id)`, and `ControllerPlaybackModel` - the tracker's `PredictivePlaybackModel`
plus `setRowTicks` and `anchorTo`, so the node keeps its in-place table adoption and its start anchor without naming a
model. `session.ts` and `controllerSession.ts` lose the last LSDj-specific words too: the node builds its session from
the runtime, holds the model across rebuilds keyed by the app id, defaults `app` to the empty string (the client names
the app; a document that names none runs nothing, which is the one C++ case's document that relied on the old default,

`packages.mjs` gains `controllerApps` in `renderPackages` (`CONTROLLER_APPS`, the apps' lists spread in product order,
and `CONTROLLER_APP_SOURCES`, each contributing package's own list so a refusal can name both packages), the pairing
checks against the manifests' `protocol.apps` (rendered as `RUNTIME_APP_IDS`), the static duplicate-runtime-id
refusal, a generated-identifier collision refusal (a `a-b`+`c` vs `a`+`b-c` fixture), and `CONTROLLER_SYNC` in
`protocol.ts` from each entry's `syncOverride` (`node` and `mode` required, `listening` with `off`, an `off` with no
`listening` refused, an unknown key refused, and the named node type one a package declares). `renderScriptNodes`
imports each app's runtime module and registers it BEFORE the nodes, comparing the registered set to the manifests'
ids import by import and naming the module and both ids when they differ. `contributions()` builds new app objects and
does not write onto the parsed manifests. The fixtures follow: the expected three modules hold the new lists and the
sync table, the fixture tree's `alpha` gains a control-plane half and a runtime half (and a `launchpad` fixture
package owns the kind), and `run-generator.mjs` prints `mode: message` for each new refusal so the cases can hold the
words.

````ts
// The launcher package's runtime registry, as the fixture tree sees it: the generated script entry calls
````

- [ ] **Step 6: The shell reads the registry and the generated table**

`src/controller/registry.ts` fills a `ControllerRegistry` from the generated `CONTROLLER_APPS` and keeps
`parseAppConfig` (it stays: it is the publishers' door, and moving zod parsing into a generated module is what it
exists to avoid). `graph/controller.ts`'s `controllerSyncOverride` looks the app up in `CONTROLLER_SYNC` and resolves
the system with the same `controllerTarget` the launches are tagged with, and `buildGraph.ts` compares `role.node ===
sync.node` so it holds no type and no id. `menuDefs.ts` cycles the registry's list. `lsdj/ts/lsdjSyncBytes.ts` gets
the one-word correction the moved encoder needed, and the native `lsdj-launchpad` test names the package.

- [ ] **Step 7: The bridge's scenario and tests, and the clocked tick fix**

`lsdj-launchpad`'s scenario walks what the bridge adds: the MI.MAP app over a predictor driven through bars, a seek
and a stop; the app's helpers; the predictor's edit and re-anchor paths (`setRowTicks` with a row losing its chain and
a chain shortened under the ticks already played, `anchorTo`, `stop`, `reset`, junk normalised); `songRowTicks` from a
decoded song's arithmetic; the target's releases, its range edges and the null target; every quantise mode through a
session with no cart; and the sync override's four answers. Its heap is measured, not claimed: 144960 bytes least,
budget 184320 (the launchpad core's is 61440 and 76800; both are a scenario's own figures, not the box's 64 KiB
arena). The clocked-tick fix is here, in `session.ts` and the node, and it is the reason this commit re-records a
digest: the node walks the cart's own `TickClock` and hands the session the previous block's **count**, so the
predictor advances by exactly what the cart was sent. `relocate`, the `lastTick` diff and the `started` gate are gone;
a loop wrap, a seek made while stopped and a device taken again keep their block, and `connect()`'s lost block is gone
with them.

````ts
// The launchpad package's two tables (ts/registry.ts and ts/apps/index.ts): the control plane's app registry, and the
// runtime registry the generated script bundle fills. Each is looked up by id, so a re-registration replaces rather than
// duplicating, and an unknown id - an Object.prototype name among them - is nothing.
import { test, expect } from "@retroplug/testing";
import { ControllerRegistry, type ControllerAppContribution } from "../registry";
import { controllerApp, controllerApps, registerControllerApps, type ControllerAppRuntime } from "../apps";

const entry = (id: string, label = id): ControllerAppContribution => ({
  id,
  label,
  config: { parse: (v: unknown) => (v ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown> },
});

const runtimeOf = (id: string): ControllerAppRuntime => ({
  id,
  factory: () => () => {},
  playbackModel: () => ({
    channelCount: 4,
    position: () => ({ playing: false, channels: [] }),
    grid: () => ({ rowCount: 1, channelCount: 4, hasContent: () => false }),
    setRowTicks: () => {},
    anchorTo: () => {},
    launch: () => {},
    advance: () => {},
    stop: () => {},
    reset: () => {},
  }),
  target: () => ({ maxRow: 1, launch: () => {}, release: () => {} }),
});

test("the control-plane registry registers by id, in order, and replaces in place", () => {
  const r = new ControllerRegistry();
  r.register(entry("a"));
  r.register(entry("b"));
  expect(r.list().map((app) => app.id)).toEqual(["a", "b"]);
  r.register(entry("a", "Mine"));
  expect(r.get("a")!.label).toBe("Mine");
  expect(r.list().map((app) => app.id)).toEqual(["a", "b"]); // its position holds
});

test("an unknown id returns undefined rather than throwing, an Object.prototype name included", () => {
  const r = new ControllerRegistry();
  for (const id of ["nope", "toString", "__proto__", ""]) {
    expect(r.get(id)).toBe(undefined);
    expect(r.defaultConfig(id)).toBe(undefined);
  }
});

test("defaultConfig parses the app's schema with nothing given", () => {
  const r = new ControllerRegistry();
  r.register({ ...entry("a"), config: { parse: () => ({ filled: true }) } });
  expect(r.defaultConfig("a")).toEqual({ filled: true });
});

test("the runtime registry registers by id, and the generated bundle fills it", () => {
  registerControllerApps([runtimeOf("one")]);
  expect(controllerApp("one")!.id).toBe("one");
  expect(controllerApps().map((app) => app.id).includes("one")).toBe(true);
  registerControllerApps([runtimeOf("two")]);
  registerControllerApps([runtimeOf("one")]); // a reload replaces, keeping the order
  const ids = controllerApps().map((app) => app.id);
  expect(ids.indexOf("one")).toBeLessThan(ids.indexOf("two"));
  expect(ids.filter((id) => id === "one").length).toBe(1);
});

test("the runtime registry knows no app it was not handed", () => {
  for (const id of ["nope", "toString", "__proto__", ""]) expect(controllerApp(id)).toBe(undefined);
});
````

Create `packages/lsdj-launchpad/ts/scenario/lsdjLaunchpad.ts`:

````ts
// The LSDj bridge, end to end, through the bridge's own PORTABLE code only - run by
// packages/retroplug/scripts/build-device-pack.mjs --scenario under Node and under MicroQuickJS, whose two transcripts
// must match byte for byte (pnpm test, ts/test/scenario.test.ts).
//
// The launchpad core has a scenario of its own (packages/launchpad/ts/scenario/launchpadCore.ts): the surface, the
// decoder, the session and the scan. This one walks what the BRIDGE adds - the MI.MAP app, the predictor it reads and
// the launch target - so a path neither a node nor that scenario runs is still proven where the box would run it: every
// quantise mode, the predictor's edit and re-anchor paths, a song built from a decoded song rather than a table, and the
// launches the target sends to the cart.
//
// It imports the package's own modules and its declared dependencies only (launchpad and lsdj), which the scenario mode
// allows and a node pack's bundle does not.
import { PRO_MK3, Palette, palette, type Led } from "@retroplug/launchpad";
import type { TrackerTarget } from "@retroplug/launchpad/launchTarget";
import { ControllerSession, type ControllerApp } from "@retroplug/launchpad/session";
import { PredictedLsdjModel, normaliseRowTicks, songRowTicks } from "@retroplug/lsdj/playback/predict";
import type { Song } from "@retroplug/lsdj/model";
import runtime from "../appRuntime";
import { lsdjMidiMap, MAX_PAGE, QUANTISE_VALUES, rowAt, channelAt, followRow } from "../lsdjMidiMap";
import { launchMessage, lsdjMidiMapTarget, LSDJ_MAX_ROW } from "../launchTarget";
import { nullTarget } from "@retroplug/launchpad/launchTarget";

const out = (line: string): void => console.log(line);
const emit = (what: string, data: unknown): void => out(what + " " + JSON.stringify(data));

// --- the app over a predictor -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

// Rows 0..5 hold one phrase (96 ticks) on pu1/pu2, rows 0..3 on wav; noi is empty. Enough to see the playhead move, a
// row end, and channels diverge.
const table: (number | null)[][] = [];
for (let ch = 0; ch < 4; ch++) {
  const rows: (number | null)[] = [];
  const filled = ch < 2 ? 6 : ch === 2 ? 4 : 0;
  for (let r = 0; r < 256; r++) rows.push(r < filled ? 96 : null);
  table.push(rows);
}

const launches: number[][] = [];
const model = runtime.playbackModel(table);
const session = new ControllerSession(runtime.factory(), {
  playback: model,
  target: runtime.target((d) => launches.push(d)),
  config: { quantise: "bar", follow: true, page: 0 },
});

const pad = (x: number, y: number, velocity: number): number[] => [0x90, (7 - y) * 10 + x + 11, velocity];
const cc = (n: number, value: number): number[] => [0xb0, n, value];

emit("connect", session.connect());

interface Block {
  input: number[][];
  tick: number;
  transport: boolean;
  /** The ticks the host clocked in the previous block, as walkTicks counted them. */
  ticks: number;
}
const blocks: Block[] = [
  { input: [], tick: 0, transport: false, ticks: 0 },
  { input: [pad(0, 2, 127), pad(0, 2, 0)], tick: 0, transport: false, ticks: 0 }, // stopped: launches at once
];
for (let tick = 0; tick <= 480; tick += 12) {
  const input: number[][] = [];
  if (tick === 108) input.push(pad(1, 4, 100)); // playing: waits for the bar
  if (tick === 300) input.push(cc(PRO_MK3.buttons.up, 127), cc(PRO_MK3.buttons.up, 0));
  if (tick === 312) input.push(cc(PRO_MK3.buttons.down, 127));
  if (tick === 396) input.push(pad(6, 1, 90)); // row 9, on the right-hand pane
  blocks.push({ input, tick, transport: true, ticks: 12 });
}
blocks.push({ input: [], tick: 4000, transport: true, ticks: 0 }); // a seek: the cart was sent no clocks
blocks.push({ input: [], tick: 480, transport: false, ticks: 0 });

for (let i = 0; i < blocks.length; i++) {
  launches.length = 0;
  const leds = session.update(blocks[i]);
  if (leds.length > 0 || launches.length > 0) emit("block " + i, { leds, launches: launches.slice() });
}
emit("position", model.position());
emit("grid", [model.grid().rowCount, model.grid().channelCount, model.grid().hasContent(0, 5),
  model.grid().hasContent(0, 6), model.grid().hasContent(3, 0)]);
emit("disconnect", session.disconnect());

// --- the app's own helpers ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

emit("layout", [rowAt(0, 0, 0), rowAt(0, 4, 0), rowAt(0, 3, 7), rowAt(16, 7, 7), channelAt(0), channelAt(3), channelAt(4)]);
emit("follow", [
  followRow({ playing: true, channels: [{ playing: false, songRow: null }, { playing: true, songRow: 3 }] }),
  followRow({ playing: false, channels: [{ playing: false, songRow: null }] }),
  MAX_PAGE,
  QUANTISE_VALUES.length,
]);
const app: ControllerApp = lsdjMidiMap;
emit("app", typeof app);

// --- the predictor's edit and re-anchor paths -----------------------------------------------------------------------

const edited = normaliseRowTicks(table);
edited[0][1] = null; // pu1 row 1 loses its chain
edited[1][1] = 24; // pu2 row 1's chain gets shorter than the ticks it has already played
const p = PredictedLsdjModel.fromRowTicks(normaliseRowTicks(table));
p.launch(1);
p.advance(150);
emit("model playing", p.position());
p.setRowTicks(edited);
emit("model edited", p.position());
p.anchorTo([3, null, 2, null]);
emit("model anchored", p.position());
p.advance(500);
emit("model advanced", p.position());
p.stop();
emit("model stopped", p.position());
p.reset();
emit("model reset", p.position());
emit("normalised junk", normaliseRowTicks({ not: "a table" })[0].slice(0, 3));

// A song built from a decoded song rather than a table - the arithmetic the control plane runs (songRowTicks): a custom
// groove, a chain ending at a hole, and a groove of zeroes that must fall back.
const rows: { chains: (number | null)[] }[] = [];
for (let r = 0; r < 8; r++) rows.push({ chains: [r < 4 ? 0 : null, r < 2 ? 1 : null, null, r === 0 ? 2 : null] });
const song = {
  rows,
  chains: [{ phrases: [0, 1, null, 3] }, { phrases: [5] }, { phrases: [null, 4] }],
  grooves: [{ steps: [4, 8, 0, 6] }],
} as unknown as Song;
const fromSong = songRowTicks(song);
emit("song ticks", [fromSong[0][0], fromSong[1][1], fromSong[3][0], fromSong[0][5]]);
const zero = songRowTicks({ ...song, grooves: [{ steps: [0, 0] }] } as Song);
emit("zero groove", zero[0][0]);

// --- the target ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

const release: number[][] = [];
const target: TrackerTarget = lsdjMidiMapTarget((d) => release.push(d));
target.release(5);
target.release(200);
target.launch(300); // past the last addressable row: dropped rather than wrapping
target.launch(LSDJ_MAX_ROW);
emit("target release", release);
emit("launch encoding", [launchMessage(0), launchMessage(127), launchMessage(128), launchMessage(LSDJ_MAX_ROW),
  launchMessage(254), launchMessage(-1), launchMessage(1.5), launchMessage(3, false)]);
emit("null target", [nullTarget(LSDJ_MAX_ROW).maxRow, typeof nullTarget(LSDJ_MAX_ROW).launch,
  typeof nullTarget(LSDJ_MAX_ROW).release]);

// --- every quantise mode, through a session with no cart attached -----------------------------------------------------

const paletteLed: Led = { mode: "static", colour: palette(Palette.greenBright) };
emit("led", paletteLed);
for (const quantise of QUANTISE_VALUES) {
  const sent: number[][] = [];
  const s = new ControllerSession(lsdjMidiMap, {
    playback: runtime.playbackModel(table),
    target: lsdjMidiMapTarget((d) => sent.push(d)),
    config: { quantise, follow: false, page: MAX_PAGE },
  });
  s.connect();
  let leds = 0;
  for (let tick = 0; tick <= 300; tick += 6) {
    const input: number[][] = [];
    if (tick === 0) input.push(cc(PRO_MK3.buttons.up, 127)); // page up from the last page
    if (tick === 6) input.push(pad(0, 0, 127)); // first launch: immediate whatever the mode
    if (tick === 30) input.push(pad(0, 3, 127)); // second launch: quantised
    if (tick === 60) input.push(cc(PRO_MK3.buttons.session, 127)); // session button: follow on
    if (tick === 90) input.push(cc(PRO_MK3.buttons.down, 127), cc(PRO_MK3.buttons.down, 127));
    if (tick === 120) input.push(pad(7, 7, 127)); // the window's last row
    leds += s.update({ input, tick, transport: tick > 0, ticks: tick > 0 ? 6 : 0 }).length;
  }
  emit("quantise " + quantise, { launches: sent, ledMessages: leds });
}
const detached = new ControllerSession(lsdjMidiMap, {
  playback: runtime.playbackModel(table), target: nullTarget(LSDJ_MAX_ROW),
});
emit("null target session", detached.update({ input: [pad(0, 0, 127)], tick: 0, transport: false, ticks: 0 }).length);
````

````ts
// The MI.MAP app's control-plane half (ts/app.ts): its id, its menu label and the schema its config is parsed with - plus
// the sync mode it needs the cart its launches drive to be in, which is DATA in the package's manifest
// (protocol.apps[].syncOverride) because the planner applies it and must carry no app and no zod. It reuses
// RoleConfigSchema for the knobs, so the interesting assertions are the ones about tolerance: a stale or garbage config
// must snap to something sane rather than fail the parse, because these values come off disk and a user should never be
// locked out of their own controller by a bad enum.
import { test, expect } from "@retroplug/testing";
import contribution from "../app";
import { MAX_PAGE, QUANTISE_VALUES } from "../lsdjMidiMap";
import runtime from "../appRuntime";

const apps = contribution.controllerApps ?? [];
const miMap = apps.find((app) => app.id === "lsdj-midimap")!;

test("the app is contributed under the id a project stores, with the menu's label", () => {
  expect(apps.map((app) => app.id)).toEqual(["lsdj-midimap"]);
  expect(miMap.label).toBe("LSDj MI.MAP");
  expect(typeof miMap.config.parse).toBe("function");
});

test("the schema fills the documented defaults", () => {
  expect(miMap.config.parse({})).toEqual({ quantise: "bar", follow: true, page: 0 });
});

test("a garbage config snaps to sane values instead of failing to load", () => {
  expect(miMap.config.parse({ quantise: "sometime", follow: "yes", page: 99 }))
    .toEqual({ quantise: "bar", follow: true, page: MAX_PAGE });
  expect(miMap.config.parse({ page: -5 })).toEqual({ quantise: "bar", follow: true, page: 0 });
});

test("valid values are preserved", () => {
  expect(miMap.config.parse({ quantise: "rowEnd", follow: false, page: 3 }))
    .toEqual({ quantise: "rowEnd", follow: false, page: 3 });
});

test("every quantise mode the menu offers is one the schema accepts", () => {
  for (const quantise of QUANTISE_VALUES) expect(miMap.config.parse({ quantise }).quantise).toBe(quantise);
});

test("the two halves are joined by id", () => {
  // The generated script bundle registers the runtime and the app's registry holds this half: a document names one id,
  // so the two must name the same app.
  expect(runtime.id).toBe(miMap.id);
});
````

Create `packages/lsdj-launchpad/ts/test/scenario.test.ts`:

````ts
// The LSDj bridge's scenario (packages/lsdj-launchpad/ts/scenario/lsdjLaunchpad.ts) through the device-pack toolchain's
// scenario mode: bundled, lowered to ES5, scanned for library calls MicroQuickJS lacks (the scenario's bundle AND the
// package's whole portable core), then run under Node and on build/bin/retroplug-mqjs-run, whose transcripts must agree
// byte for byte inside the heap it is given.
//
// The toolchain is Node's (esbuild and TypeScript are not txiki modules), so this runs it in a node child: the runner's
// own node (RP_NODE, which scripts/run-tests.mjs sets), else the node on the PATH when run by hand.
import { test, expect } from "@retroplug/testing";

// Just enough of txiki's spawn and a child's pipe, declared locally as bundle-no-zod.test.ts does.
interface ByteStream {
  getReader(): { read(): Promise<{ done: boolean; value?: Uint8Array }> };
}
declare const tjs: {
  env: Record<string, string | undefined>;
  readFile(path: string): Promise<Uint8Array>;
  spawn(
    args: string[],
    opts: { stdout: "pipe"; stderr: "pipe" },
  ): {
    stdout: ByteStream | null;
    stderr: ByteStream | null;
    wait(): Promise<{ exit_status: number; term_signal: string | null }>;
  };
};

async function text(stream: ByteStream | null): Promise<string> {
  if (!stream) return "";
  const chunks: Uint8Array[] = [];
  const reader = stream.getReader();
  for (;;) {
    const { done, value } = await reader.read();
    if (done) break;
    if (value) chunks.push(value);
  }
  let total = 0;
  for (const c of chunks) total += c.length;
  const all = new Uint8Array(total);
  let at = 0;
  for (const c of chunks) {
    all.set(c, at);
    at += c.length;
  }
  return new TextDecoder().decode(all);
}

// The suite runs from packages/retroplug.
const SCENARIO = "../../packages/lsdj-launchpad/ts/scenario/lsdjLaunchpad.ts";
const PACK_DIR = "../../packages/lsdj-launchpad";
const OUT = ".test-build/lsdj-launchpad-scenario";
// The bridge's own heap, measured the way the launchpad core's is, by bisecting --heap-bytes on this tree: the run
// passes at 144960 bytes and fails at 144896 (the four quantise sessions' tables are live at once), and the budget is
// 1.25x that. The scenario's figure, NOT the box's 64 KiB arena, which no controller pack claims.
const LEAST_HEAP = 144960;
const HEAP = Math.ceil((LEAST_HEAP * 1.25) / 1024) * 1024; // 184320

async function runScenario(): Promise<{ ok: boolean; out: string; err: string }> {
  const args = [tjs.env.RP_NODE || "node", "scripts/build-device-pack.mjs", "--scenario", SCENARIO,
                "--name", "lsdj-launchpad", "--heap-bytes", String(HEAP), "--out-dir", OUT, "--pack-dir", PACK_DIR];
  const child = tjs.spawn(args, { stdout: "pipe", stderr: "pipe" });
  // Both pipes drained beside the wait, so a child that fills one cannot block on it.
  const [out, err, status] = await Promise.all([text(child.stdout), text(child.stderr), child.wait()]);
  return { ok: !status.term_signal && status.exit_status === 0, out, err };
}

test("the LSDj bridge runs on MicroQuickJS as on Node, byte for byte", async () => {
  const run = await runScenario();
  expect(run.ok, `the toolchain refused the scenario:\n${run.out}${run.err}`).toBe(true);
  expect(run.out.includes("matches Node byte for byte")).toBe(true);
  expect(run.out.includes("device pack scenario lsdj-launchpad OK")).toBe(true);
  // The package's whole core is scanned, its control-plane half (ts/app.ts, which is zod's) aside: a call the engine
  // lacks on a path the scenario never takes is refused there.
  expect(run.out.includes("no library calls outside MicroQuickJS's stdlib, in the core's ")).toBe(true);

  // The transcript the two engines agreed on: the app driving the predictor, the predictor's edit and anchor paths, a
  // song's arithmetic, every quantise mode and the target's bytes. A run that stopped early would still agree with
  // itself, so the sections are asserted.
  const transcript = new TextDecoder().decode(await tjs.readFile(`${OUT}/lsdj-launchpad.transcript.txt`));
  const lines = transcript.split("\n");
  expect(lines.length > 25, `${lines.length} transcript lines`).toBe(true);
  for (const part of [
    'connect [[240,0,32,41,2,14,14,1,247]]', // Programmer mode
    '"launches":[[144,2,100]]', // the stopped-transport press launched at once (row 2, at the top)
    "position {", // where the predictor ended, after the bars, the seek and the stop
    "grid [256,4,true,false,false]",
    "layout [0,8,7,31,0,3,0]",
    "follow [3,null,15,4]",
    'model playing {"playing":true,"channels":[{"playing":true,"songRow":2}', // a launch, then 150 ticks
    "model edited {", // a row losing its chain, a chain shortened under the ticks already played
    'model anchored {"playing":true,"channels":[{"playing":true,"songRow":3}',
    "model stopped {",
    "song ticks [192,96,null,null]", // a custom groove, a chain ending at a hole
    "zero groove 192", // an all-zero groove falls back to the factory one
    "target release [[128,5,0],[129,72,0],[145,125,100]]", // release, release, and a row past the range dropped
    "launch encoding [[144,0,100],[144,127,100],[145,0,100],[145,125,100],null,null,null,[128,3,0]]",
    "quantise immediate {",
    "quantise beat {",
    "quantise bar {",
    "quantise rowEnd {", // the four modes: the launches land the same rows, the LED traffic counts differ
    "null target session 1",
  ])
    expect(transcript.includes(part), part).toBe(true);
});
````

Expected: exit 0: `# 26 passed, 0 skipped, 0 failed` (stage 2's own run, at a tree whose two new cases are these).

- [ ] **Step 8: The whole-core scan skips the app module, and its two cases**

A package's control-plane half carries zod and runs only under the desktop, so the scenario mode's core scan covers
every module under `ts/` **but** its `test/`, `testSupport/` and the module the manifest names as `app`. The skip is
tested both ways: `app-module-skip` has an app that calls what the engine lacks (accepted, because nothing on the
device runs it), and `app-module-sibling` has an app that imports such a module, which is REFUSED naming the helper's
line - so the skip cannot hide a core that reaches into one.

Create `packages/retroplug/test/graph/device-pack/scenario/app-module-sibling/package.json`:

````json
{
  "name": "@retroplug/test-app-module-sibling",
  "private": true,
  "retroplug": { "app": "ts/app.ts" }
}
````

An image carries the day it was built: the Pico SDK's standard binary info stamps it with `__DATE__`
(`pico_standard_binary_info`, since nothing sets `PICO_NO_BI_PROGRAM_BUILD_DATE`), once, a fixed-length string. So the
check counts that string (it must be exactly one) and hashes a copy with it normalised to 8 November 2026, as
`/tmp/f3pro/norm-sha.sh` normalises it for the baseline's and every stage's run; nothing else may differ, and the
sizes the device scripts print do not move with the date. The bytes also rest on the build's inputs, so a hash
compares only an image built from this worktree's path, against the same SDK checkouts (`/opt/pico-sdk` for the check,
`/workspaces/pico-sdk` for the box), the same Pico-PIO-USB checkout (`/workspaces/Pico-PIO-USB`) and
`arm-none-eabi-g++` 13.2.1.

````bash
git commit -F - <<'EOF'
feat(packages): the controllerApps kind, and the LSDj bridge that contributes MI.MAP

Add the `controllerApps` contribution kind and packages/lsdj-launchpad, the bridge that gives the
Launchpad's MI.MAP app to the app and to the script bundle, so neither `launchpad` nor `lsdj` knows
the other (docs/modular-graph-phase-f3-design.md sections 2 and 4).

The kind has two halves, joined by the id a project stores. The control-plane half is a package's
`app` module contributing `{ id, label, config: <zod schema> }`, which the generated packages.ts
concatenates in product order into CONTROLLER_APPS and the shell's registry fills its
ControllerRegistry with: the menu cycles it and the publishers parse a saved config with the app's
own schema. The runtime half is the same package's `protocol.apps` entry, `{ id, module, syncOverride? }`,
whose module default-exports `{ id, factory, playbackModel, target }`: the app, the playback model it
reads and the launch target its launches go to. The generated script entry registers the runtimes
BEFORE the session node, which now looks an app up by id and names none; it holds each registered id
to its own manifest entry, naming the module and both ids when they differ.

The sync override is DATA, not code: `syncOverride: { node, mode, listening, off }` names the cart
sync node type the app's launches need, the mode that node is put in, and the polled SYNC value that
counts as the cart listening (any other puts it in `off`; one that cannot be read yet is assumed
willing). The generator renders it into generated/protocol.ts as CONTROLLER_SYNC, so a bundle of the
planner carries no app and no zod (the app modules have both), and buildGraph applies it with no app
id and no node type of its own: the resolved system comes from the same helper the launches are
tagged with. A pack author declares the mode in a manifest and gets it, and a second app with
another cart's node type is an entry, not a branch in the shell.

`protocol.module` is optional when a package declares no nodes, so an app-only bridge ships no empty
nodes module; a module named with no nodes is refused instead. `launchpad` owns the launch target
contract (ts/launchTarget.ts, with `nullTarget(maxRow)`) and names no tracker; the bridge owns the
MI.MAP target and the encoder. The generated local identifiers are checked as they are made, so two
packages whose names and app ids mangle to one name are refused naming both, and a duplicate
control-plane id is refused naming both packages (with a fixture case); `contributions()` builds new
objects rather than writing derived fields onto the parsed manifests.

packages/lsdj-launchpad holds the MI.MAP app, its LSDj launch target (the row encoder, LSDj's row
range), the PredictedLsdjModel wiring, the app's schema half and its scenario. The app, the target
and their tests are git renames out of launchpad and the shell. `launchpad` loses its `lsdj`
dependency and moves after `core` in the product list, the bridge follows `lsdj`, and the shell
declares it; one plain pnpm install.

The session is advanced by the ticks the host CLOCKED, which the node counts with the same walk the
cart's own protocol node runs (packages/core/ts/ticks.ts), not by the distance between two
positions: a host loop wrap, a seek made while stopped, or a device taken again inside a block would
read as no elapsed time and leave the predicted playhead behind the cart for good. Two node cases
hold the wrap and the swap, red first, and the session's relocate flag goes with the inference it
served.

The bridge's portability scenario walks what it adds (every quantise mode, the predictor's edit and
anchor paths, a song's arithmetic, the target's bytes) under Node and MicroQuickJS, in a heap
measured at 144960 bytes and budgeted at 184320; the scenario mode also scans the package's whole
core with the control-plane half skipped, because that half is zod's and runs on the desktop alone,
and the fixture holds both halves of that rule. It is run by pnpm test, and its transcript is kept
and asserted.

The session node's `app` setting defaults to empty (the client names the app); the C++ script-pack
reload case now names lsdj-midimap in its document, as a document must.
EOF
````

---

### Task 3: the pack's native half, its provider and its facet

Design sections 2, 3, 9's third stage and section 8's re-records. The E2 shape, in this tree's words: a **portable
target** (`retroplug-launchpad`, `device: true`) that holds the node-facing contract and the two surface nodes, and a
**desktop target** (`retroplug-launchpad-desktop`) that holds the transport, the pool, the cross-process claim, the
RtMidi opener, the provider and the facet. The nodes lose `threads` (the link's callback and writer threads are the
desktop provider's) and become `device: true`, so they plan on the Pico and the device-mode test builds them; the
legacy host keeps running every product until Task 4, through an adapter that implements `/2` by reporting generation 1.

`SurfaceLink` goes to **/2**: `generation()` replaces the connected flag (0 means nothing attached, otherwise the
claim's number, bumped on every connect, so a pair swapped inside one block reads as a new device), `dropped()` stays
and now says what it counts in both directions, and `NoSurface` answers generation 0 and counts every push as lost. The
two counters cross the graph as control values **wrapped at 2^24** - a generation into `1..2^24-1`, so a wrap never
reads as "nothing attached" - and `surface-in` gains a `drops` output beside `in` and `connected`.

`ControllerLink` is the branch's `src/host/controller/` rewritten onto fixed slots: an array of 256 generation-tagged
`DeviceMessage` slots with one producer (the current port's callback) and one consumer (the audio thread, which skips an
earlier claim's slots **in place**, so a disconnect rewinds nothing and the UI thread never drains - the race the legacy
link has); a POD `SpscRing` of 32 for audio-to-device, drained by the link's **writer thread** (WinMM blocks about 170 ms
on a bulk SysEx); close bytes replayed on disconnect and on destruction; and a 16-message UI queue the writer drains so
`send()` never waits for a write in flight.

The provider installs the link under `launchpad` / `rp.launchpad.surface-link/2`, owns the pool and the facet, and wires
the pool's held edge to the host table's `suspend_hardware_inputs`. The facet is `LaunchpadRpc`'s twelve synchronous
methods, TS's only door to a port. **The ABI is 2**: `reserve_midi`, `suspend_hardware_inputs` and `restored` on
`rp_device_host`, and `wake` on `rp_provider` (generated as `rp_wake_providers`), with strict equality both ways. Every
product must now say which providers it starts: `retroplug_product(... PROVIDERS ...)`, no default. In this stage no
product names `launchpad`, so the legacy host keeps working and the plugin (which names `n8` alone, and whose
`plugin.cmake` now refuses a plugin target linked to the pack's desktop target) starts no control surface.

This is also the stage where the three goldens move, and the task's own steps say which command wrote each: the
`[packages]` golden (the two types register from their own package after `core`), the role goldens' `drops` wire (one
wire per controller document, and nothing else in that file) and the two surface descriptor goldens, which are **new
files** - the tree had none for the legacy nodes, so nothing is re-recorded there. The device check's image hash moves
from `8cc7ae7d` to `38665e2c` (the fix pass's `1..2^24-1` generation mapping; the stage's first cut was `706e26cf`), and
the box's two images and the `bliptoaster` pack's bytes do not move.

The stage's first cut had two defects the review called Critical, and both are in this task's blocks: every product
started every listed provider (which made the provider's surface link refuse the SDL's own install, so the standalone's
Launchpad was dead), and a pair whose input and output share a name could never be claimed (two locks refused each
other). `PROVIDERS` is the first's fix and the same-name guard is the second's, with a real config dir behind the
facet's cases so the guard is exercised through `flock`.

- [ ] **Step 2: The portable target, and the legacy adapter that has to speak /2**

`packages/launchpad/native/CMakeLists.txt` registers two targets: `retroplug-launchpad` (`ENTRY` a generated package
entry, `DEVICE` so the `-fno-exceptions -fno-rtti` object library is built, and the two node sources) and
`retroplug-launchpad-desktop` (`PROVIDER rp_launchpad_provider`, `RPC` the facet's header and register function,
`LINKS` `rtmidi`, and no `ENTRY`, so a product that lists the package without naming its provider keeps the node types
and neither the provider nor the transport). `SurfaceLink.hpp` is the `/2` contract with its reasoning written where a
reader of the header will find it. The package's manifest gains both native entries, `packages/native` drops its
`rp_launchpad_package` entry and keeps `@retroplug/launchpad` as a dependency for the adapter it still holds, and the
device check's package list gains `launchpad` so the surface types join the image.

Create `packages/launchpad/native/CMakeLists.txt`:

````cmake
# The Launchpad pack (docs/modular-graph-phase-f3-design.md sections 2 and 3): rp.launchpad.surface-in / -out, the
# control surface as nodes, and the link interface they drive the device through (launchpad/SurfaceLink.hpp), with the
# desktop's half beside it: the claimed pair's transport (ControllerLink), the loose MIDI ports a TS scan opens
# (MidiPortPool), the cross-process claim (PortClaim), the RtMidi backend (RtMidiPort), the provider that installs the
# link and the facet the TS client reaches it through. Added by retroplug_package(launchpad) (cmake/packages.cmake).
# Like any pack it depends on node-sdk alone; nothing here links a packages/native target.

# --- retroplug-launchpad: the rp_launchpad_package entry and rp.launchpad.surface-in / -out
# (src/launchpad/SurfaceNodes.cpp), over the rp::launchpad::SurfaceLink a host binds by name (rp.host.devices/2). A
# `device` entry: the desktop build compiles it as a device does too (-fno-exceptions, -fno-rtti, through the
# -device object library every package's device entry gets), and the device check links it into the RP2350 image. The
# nodes own no thread and no port; the link's own callback and writer threads are the desktop provider's.
retroplug_package_library(retroplug-launchpad
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/launchpad/SurfaceNodes.cpp)
target_include_directories(retroplug-launchpad PUBLIC ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src)
target_link_libraries(retroplug-launchpad PUBLIC retroplug-node-sdk)

# The device build stops here: the desktop's half below is MIDI ports, file locks and threads, which a device has none
# of, and its manifest entry is not `device`.
if(RP_DEVICE_BUILD)
    return()
endif()

# Threads: ControllerLink's writer thread, the pool's mutexes. Found here as well as in packages/native, as an imported
# target is visible only in the directory that finds it and below.
find_package(Threads REQUIRED)

# --- retroplug-launchpad-desktop: the transport (src/launchpad/desktop/): ControllerLink, the claimed pair with its
# fixed-slot rings and its writer thread; MidiPortPool, the loose ports a scan opens; PortClaim, the cross-process claim
# under <configDir>/locks; RtMidiPort, the only RtMidi user (SysEx on). Its manifest entry names the provider
# (rp_launchpad_provider, LaunchpadProvider.cpp: the link installed as `launchpad`, the pool, the facet's service) and
# the facet (LaunchpadRpc.hpp, implemented in LaunchpadRpc.cpp; only its registerRpc is a template, which a product's
# server instantiates, so the pack itself needs neither rpcpp nor QuickJS, only reflect-cpp's byte string). A product
# starts the provider through its generated rp_start_providers (cmake/packages.cmake) and names nothing here.
retroplug_package_library(retroplug-launchpad-desktop
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/launchpad/desktop/ControllerLink.cpp
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/launchpad/desktop/LaunchpadProvider.cpp
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/launchpad/desktop/LaunchpadRpc.cpp
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/launchpad/desktop/MidiPortPool.cpp
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/launchpad/desktop/PortClaim.cpp
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/launchpad/desktop/RtMidiPort.cpp)
target_link_libraries(retroplug-launchpad-desktop
    PUBLIC  retroplug-launchpad   # the include root, launchpad/SurfaceLink.hpp, the package id
            retroplug-node-sdk    # transport/SpscRing.hpp (the send ring), graph/rp_provider.h, reflect-cpp
    PRIVATE rtmidi                # deps/rtmidi, behind RtMidiPort.cpp alone (defined at root scope, cmake/rtmidi.cmake)
            Threads::Threads)     # ControllerLink's writer thread

# --- the pack's test binaries (cmake/test-binary.cmake), built by name; sources resolve against this directory.

# The transport, ported from feature/launchpad's Controller.test.cpp (docs/modular-graph-phase-f3-design.md section 8):
# the claimed pair on fixed slots, a generation per claim and the slots of an earlier one dropped by the audio thread,
# the span of messages one drain answers, a swap mid-drain driven from a producer thread and the audio thread (run under
# ThreadSanitizer by tools/run-sanitizer.sh's launchpad leg), the writer thread's ordering and the provider's per-frame
# wake, the close bytes replayed on disconnect and destruction, the audio path's two calls allocating nothing, the pool's
# inputs-held edge, PortClaim's one claim per machine, and the provider and the facet over a fake opener: no hardware,
# no MIDI system, no ALSA. The real RtMidi backend is linked (it is the desktop library's) but never opened.
retroplug_add_test_binary(
    NAME     retroplug-launchpad-test
    SOURCES  test/Controller.test.cpp
             test/SurfaceLink.test.cpp
             test/CountingAllocator.cpp       # the drain and the push allocate and free nothing
    LIBS     retroplug-launchpad-desktop   # the transport, the pool, the claim, the provider, the facet
    INCLUDES ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/test              # FakePorts.hpp
    DEFS     RP_LAUNCHPAD_GOLDEN_DIR="${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/test/golden")  # the two types' descriptors
````

````cpp
#pragma once

// The control surface's device link (docs/modular-graph-phase-f3-design.md section 3): the interface between the
// rp.launchpad.surface-in / -out nodes and whoever drives the Launchpad, which a host installs under the device name
// "launchpad" with the interface id "rp.launchpad.surface-link/2" (rp.host.devices/2, graph/rp_device.h). The engine
// knows nothing of it but that id. The host owns the device - the MIDI ports, pairing them, the farewell the device
// needs before a host lets it go - and a link is the whole of what a node may do with it: the device's own MIDI in both
// directions, kept out of the musical stream, its claim's generation, and what it lost.
//
// /2 is /1 plus `generation()`: a pair swapped faster than a block must still read as a NEW device, so the link numbers
// its claims and the node reports the number rather than a flag. /1 named the connected flag alone, which cannot tell a
// swap from nothing at all.
//
// As rp::n8::CartLink: no RTTI, a protected non-virtual destructor, and a link that outlives every plan whose nodes
// hold it, so a node may use it in its destroy.

#include <atomic>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>

namespace rp::launchpad {

// What the nodes ask for, and what a host installs its surface link as.
inline constexpr const char* kDeviceName           = "launchpad";
inline constexpr const char* kSurfaceLinkInterface = "rp.launchpad.surface-link/2";

// The widest message one link carries in either direction: a bulk LED SysEx at its worst (the Pro MK3's 106 RGB colour
// specifications at five bytes each, plus the 8-byte frame, is 538). The device's own replies are far shorter; one
// bound serves both ways, and a message past it is dropped and counted, never truncated into something the other end
// would misread.
inline constexpr std::size_t kMaxDeviceMessage = 560;

// One message in storage the caller owns: a drain copies into the node's own array, so nothing the block thread drops
// is freed there. It is also the slot a device link's own receive ring holds (ControllerLink's), which is why a message
// wider than it is refused by the link rather than truncated into it. There is no arrival frame: the device's traffic is
// not timed against the block, so a surface node places what it drains at frame 0.
struct DeviceMessage {
    std::uint16_t size                     = 0;
    std::uint8_t  data[kMaxDeviceMessage] = {};
};

// A control surface (rp.launchpad.surface-in / -out).
class SurfaceLink {
public:
    // [audio] Copy the messages the device sent under the current claim since the last drain into `out` and answer how
    // many: min(available, capacity), and fewer only when nothing is left, so a caller draining in batches can stop on a
    // short answer. An earlier claim's messages are discarded here rather than delivered, and nothing is delivered while
    // no claim is held (the ring is left where it is, for the claim that is arriving).
    // It allocates and frees nothing: both ends keep every message in a fixed slot of their own, and one the caller
    // has no room for stays queued rather than being dropped or freed here.
    virtual std::size_t drainInput(DeviceMessage* out, std::size_t capacity) = 0;
    // [audio] Queue one message for the device (an LED frame, a mode change). Never blocks; drops (and counts in
    // dropped()) when nothing is connected, the message is wider than kMaxDeviceMessage, or what the link holds for the
    // device is full.
    virtual void pushOutput(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size) = 0;
    // [any] Which claim is attached: 0 when nothing is, else a number the link never reuses, bumped on every connect
    // (a disconnect included). A node reports it as its `connected` stream, so a pair swapped inside one block still
    // reads as a new device and the session takes it again.
    virtual std::uint32_t generation() const = 0;
    // [any] What the link lost, both directions: a message handed to it for the device that went nowhere (nothing was
    // connected, or what the link holds for the device was full or could not carry it), and a message FROM the device
    // that its receive ring had no room for. A node reads one number for what the device and the session were each
    // promised and did not get, and repaints when it moves.
    virtual std::uint64_t dropped() const = 0;

protected:
    ~SurfaceLink() = default;
};

// What the surface nodes run on when the host answers their acquire with null (the render host, the harness, a product
// that starts no provider): nothing queued, nothing received, and every push counted as dropped. Each node's own
// member, so a document plans and runs the same in every host.
class NoSurface final : public SurfaceLink {
public:
    std::size_t   drainInput(DeviceMessage*, std::size_t) override { return 0; }
    void          pushOutput(const std::uint8_t*, std::size_t size) override {
        if (size != 0) dropped_.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    }
    std::uint32_t generation() const override { return 0; }
    std::uint64_t dropped() const override { return dropped_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed); }

private:
    // 32 bits, as NoCart's: a 64-bit atomic is a library call on the RP2350's Cortex-M33, and nothing reads a stub's
    // count but the node that owns it. The stub is what both nodes run in a device image, which has no host of this
    // package.
    std::atomic<std::uint32_t> dropped_{0};
};

}  // namespace rp::launchpad
````

- [ ] **Step 3: The desktop target**

The transport in `rp::launchpad`: `ControllerLink` (the fixed slots, the generation skip, the writer thread, the close
bytes, the UI queue), `MidiPort` / `RtMidiPort` (the only RtMidi user, SysEx on, a probe before any object so a
machine with no MIDI system is "no ports" rather than an ended process), `MidiPortPool` (loose ports for a scan, the
inputs-held edge, a batch open), `PortClaim` (`<configDir>/locks`, `flock` and an unshared `CreateFile`, with
`ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` counted as held), `LaunchpadProvider` (installs the link, owns the pool and the facet, gives the
facet the product's config dir and `reserve_midi`, runs the per-frame pump) and `LaunchpadRpc` (the twelve methods;
the claim runs the branch's order and takes ONE token when the names match; a refusal at the claims keeps the
reservation). `packages/launchpad/ts/client.ts` is `createLaunchpadClient(call)`, as `@retroplug/n8`'s
`createN8Client` is.

````cmake
# RtMidi (deps/rtmidi submodule): cross-platform MIDI I/O for live-MIDI hosts: the SDL standalone, the CLI's N8 bridges
# and a pack's own MIDI ports (the Launchpad's, packages/launchpad/native's desktop target). Static; ALSA on Linux (JACK
# off: the handheld path is ALSA/PipeWire); RtMidi's own CMake selects the platform API and its link libs.
# EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL, so the `rtmidi` target is built only because a target links it.
#
# Included at ROOT scope, before cmake/packages.cmake: a package's native/CMakeLists.txt is added while that list's
# packages are configured, and one of them (launchpad) links this target, which must exist by then. packages/native's
# cmake/deps.cmake used to add it; its own targets link the target defined here.
set(RTMIDI_BUILD_SHARED_LIBS OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
set(RTMIDI_API_JACK OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
set(RTMIDI_BUILD_TESTING OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
add_subdirectory(${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/deps/rtmidi ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/rtmidi EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL)
retroplug_silence_dep_warnings(rtmidi)
# A product that starts a provider links a package's desktop library, and the plugin formats are shared modules: the
# archive has to be PIC wherever it is added from. packages/native's cmake/deps.cmake added it inside a directory whose
# targets already were; at root scope the property is off unless it is asked for.
set_target_properties(rtmidi PROPERTIES POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE ON)
````
