Create `packages/launchpad/ts/client.ts`:

````ts
// The Launchpad facet's TS client (docs/modular-graph-phase-f3-design.md section 3), as @retroplug/n8's createN8Client
// is the N8's: the control plane's only door to the pack's ports, over the host's RPC `call`. Nothing here knows the
// protocol (that is profile.ts / protocol.ts / portScan.ts) or any native type: the client decodes the facet's answers
// into what a menu line or a scan needs, and a host that mounted no facet makes each call throw its own error.
//
// The claimed-pair half is the selection's, the pool half a scan's. Both are synchronous, as the facet is: a scan steps
// a few calls per UI frame with a clock it is told (portScan.ts), so no native thread scans and no wall-clock stall can
// wedge it.

/** One `call(method, ...args)` of the host's RPC server: the products' is synchronous and answers the method's value,
 *  throwing when the host did not mount the facet or the call failed. */
export type LaunchpadCall = (method: string, ...args: unknown[]) => unknown;

/** The system's MIDI ports, by the names the backend reports: unfiltered, because a Launchpad also speaks TRS/DIN and
 *  arrives under an interface's name. */
export interface LaunchpadPorts {
  inputs: string[];
  outputs: string[];
}

/** The claimed pair's state: what the menu's status line reads. `generation` is the claim's number (the session's
 *  `connected` value), `dropped` what the link lost since the claim. */
export interface LaunchpadStatus {
  connected: boolean;
  generation: number;
  sent: number;
  dropped: number;
  input: string;
  output: string;
  error: string;
}

/** What a scan's read answers: the messages that arrived since the last read, and how many the queue lost. */
export interface LaunchpadRead {
  messages: Uint8Array[];
  dropped: number;
}

export interface LaunchpadClient {
  /** The system's MIDI inputs and outputs. */
  ports(): LaunchpadPorts;
  /** Claim a pair, with the bytes that let the device go (replayed on release and at shutdown). */
  claim(input: string, output: string, closeBytes: Uint8Array): LaunchpadStatus;
  /** Give the device back: its close bytes first, then the shared stream may have the pair again. */
  release(): LaunchpadStatus;
  status(): LaunchpadStatus;
  /** Write a message to the claimed pair now (letting the device go while it stays claimed). */
  send(bytes: Uint8Array): boolean;
  /** The startup rendezvous's end: a product that held MIDI and audio for the claim resumes them here. */
  restored(): boolean;
  // --- the pool, a scan's ---
  openInputs(names: string[]): number[];
  openOutput(name: string): number;
  sendOn(handle: number, bytes: Uint8Array): boolean;
  read(handle: number): LaunchpadRead;
  close(handle: number): boolean;
  portError(): string;
}

const strings = (value: unknown): string[] =>
  Array.isArray(value) ? value.filter((v): v is string => typeof v === "string") : [];

const bool = (value: unknown): boolean => value === true;

const bytes = (value: unknown): Uint8Array => {
  if (value instanceof Uint8Array) return value;
  if (Array.isArray(value)) return Uint8Array.from(value as number[]);
  return new Uint8Array(0);
};

const statusOf = (value: unknown): LaunchpadStatus => {
  const v = (value ?? {}) as Partial<LaunchpadStatus>;
  return {
    connected: bool(v.connected),
    generation: Number(v.generation ?? 0),
    sent: Number(v.sent ?? 0),
    dropped: Number(v.dropped ?? 0),
    input: typeof v.input === "string" ? v.input : "",
    output: typeof v.output === "string" ? v.output : "",
    error: typeof v.error === "string" ? v.error : "",
  };
};

/** A client of the Launchpad facet over `call`. Creating one calls nothing. */
export function createLaunchpadClient(call: LaunchpadCall): LaunchpadClient {
  return {
    ports: () => {
      const v = (call("launchpadPorts") ?? {}) as Partial<LaunchpadPorts>;
      return { inputs: strings(v.inputs), outputs: strings(v.outputs) };
    },
    claim: (input, output, closeBytes) => statusOf(call("launchpadClaim", input, output, closeBytes)),
    release: () => statusOf(call("launchpadRelease")),
    status: () => statusOf(call("launchpadStatus")),
    send: (data) => bool(call("launchpadSend", data)),
    restored: () => bool(call("launchpadRestored")),
    openInputs: (names) => {
      const value = call("launchpadOpenInputs", names);
      return Array.isArray(value) ? value.map((h) => Number(h ?? 0)) : [];
    },
    openOutput: (name) => Number(call("launchpadOpenOutput", name) ?? 0),
    sendOn: (handle, data) => bool(call("launchpadPortSend", handle, data)),
    read: (handle) => {
      const v = (call("launchpadPortRead", handle) ?? {}) as { messages?: unknown[]; dropped?: unknown };
      return {
        messages: (v.messages ?? []).map(bytes),
        dropped: Number(v.dropped ?? 0),
      };
    },
    close: (handle) => bool(call("launchpadPortClose", handle)),
    portError: () => String(call("launchpadPortError") ?? ""),
  };
}
````

````cpp
#include <cstring>
#include <exception>
#include <utility>

namespace rp::launchpad {

ControllerLink::ControllerLink(MidiPortOpener opener, bool writerThread)
    : opener_(std::move(opener)), useWriter_(writerThread) {}

ControllerLink::~ControllerLink() {
    disconnect();
}

std::string ControllerLink::lastError() const {
    return error_;
}

bool ControllerLink::connect(const std::string& inName, const std::string& outName,
                             std::vector<std::uint8_t> closeBytes) {
    disconnect();  // idempotent; also releases a previously claimed pair (with its close bytes) first
    if (!opener_) {
        error_ = "no MIDI backend";
        return false;
    }
    // The claim's number is fixed BEFORE the input opens, and the receiver is bound to it, so the first message the new
    // device sends is already tagged as this claim's - not the previous one's, and not "nothing" because the number had
    // not been published yet.
    if (++nextGen_ == 0) nextGen_ = 1;  // 0 means "nothing held"
    const std::uint32_t gen = nextGen_;
    try {
        // Output first, so the input's callback can never run against a half-built link. The receiver runs on the
        // backend's callback thread; `this` outlives the port (in_ is reset before the link is destroyed, and resetting
        // it cancels the callback), so capturing it is safe.
        out_ = opener_(false, outName, nullptr);
        in_  = opener_(true, inName,
                       [this, gen](const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t n) { pushInputRing(data, n, gen); });
    } catch (const std::exception& e) {
        error_ = e.what();
        in_.reset();
        out_.reset();
        return false;
    }
    if (!in_ || !out_) {
        error_ = "MIDI port unavailable";
        in_.reset();
        out_.reset();
        return false;
    }
    error_.clear();
    sent_.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);  // "since connect": a new device starts its own count
    dropped_.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    closeBytes_ = std::move(closeBytes);
    inName_     = inName;
    outName_    = outName;
    generation_.store(gen, std::memory_order_release);
    connected_.store(true, std::memory_order_release);
    startWriter();
    return true;
}

void ControllerLink::disconnect() {
    // Stop the audio thread queueing first, so nothing is still arriving while we say goodbye.
    connected_.store(false, std::memory_order_release);
    stopWriter();  // from here this thread is the output ring's only consumer
    if (out_) {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> seat(popMutex_);  // the ring's consumer, now that the writer has stopped
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(sendMutex_);
        // Flush what the last block queued, so the device is not left half-painted - then the goodbye.
        OutMessage m;
        while (outRing_.tryPop(m)) {
            if (m.gen != generation_.load(std::memory_order_acquire) || m.len == 0) continue;
            out_->send(m.data, m.len);
            sent_.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
        }
        if (!closeBytes_.empty()) out_->send(closeBytes_.data(), closeBytes_.size());
    }
    in_.reset();  // cancels the callback: no receiver runs after this returns
    out_.reset();
    closeBytes_.clear();
    inName_.clear();
    outName_.clear();
    // The input ring is NOT rewound here: the audio thread is its only consumer and may be mid-drain. What is left in it
    // carries this claim's number, which no later claim will share, so drainInput drops it.
}

void ControllerLink::pushInputRing(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t n, std::uint32_t gen) {
    if (!data || n == 0) return;
    if (n > kMaxDeviceMessage) {  // wider than the node-facing slot: dropped and counted, never truncated
        dropped_.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
        return;
    }
    const std::size_t t    = inTail_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
    const std::size_t next = (t + 1) % kInCapacity;
    if (next == inHead_.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) {  // full -> drop
        dropped_.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
        return;
    }
    InSlot& slot = inRing_[t];
    std::memcpy(slot.msg.data, data, n);
    slot.msg.size = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(n);
    slot.gen      = gen;
    inTail_.store(next, std::memory_order_release);
}

std::size_t ControllerLink::drainInput(DeviceMessage* out, std::size_t capacity) {
    if (!out || capacity == 0) return 0;
    const std::uint32_t live = generation();
    // Nothing claimed right now: answer nothing and leave the ring alone. A connect publishes its number only after both
    // ports are open, so a drain that ran between the open and the publish would otherwise consume (and discard) the new
    // claim's first messages.
    if (live == 0) return 0;
    std::size_t         h    = inHead_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
    const std::size_t   t    = inTail_.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
    std::size_t         n    = 0;
    while (h != t && n < capacity) {
        InSlot& slot = inRing_[h];
        // An earlier claim's message is skipped here, in place: nothing on another thread drains this ring, so a
        // disconnect never has to rewind it (and could not safely).
        if (slot.gen == live) out[n++] = slot.msg;
        h = (h + 1) % kInCapacity;
    }
    inHead_.store(h, std::memory_order_release);
    return n;
}

void ControllerLink::pushOutput(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size) {
    const std::uint32_t gen = generation();
    if (gen == 0 || !data || size == 0) {
        // A paint sent while nothing is attached went nowhere: counted, so the session repaints when a device appears.
        if (data && size != 0) dropped_.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
        return;
    }
    if (size > kMaxDeviceMessage) {  // longer than any message a controller app can produce - a bug upstream
        dropped_.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
        return;
    }
    OutMessage m;
    m.gen = gen;
    m.len = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(size);
    std::memcpy(m.data, data, size);
    if (!outRing_.tryPush(m)) dropped_.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
}

void ControllerLink::writeQueued() {
    // The send ring has ONE consumer (whoever is writing here: the writer thread, pump() without one, or the UI thread's
    // send() and disconnect() flushing), and this is the seat: a ring that two threads popped would tear. It is held for
    // the drain's length and not by the send lock, so send() on the UI thread waits for the write in flight, never for
    // the queue behind it (a WinMM SysEx blocks ~170 ms).
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> seat(popMutex_);
    OutMessage                  m;
    while (outRing_.tryPop(m)) {
        if (m.len == 0) continue;
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(sendMutex_);
        // Produced for an earlier claim (queued just before a swap): not this device's to hear. Compared with the
        // claim's PUBLISHED number, not generation(), which already reads 0 while disconnect() is flushing this claim's
        // last frames.
        if (!out_ || m.gen != generation_.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) continue;
        out_->send(m.data, m.len);
        sent_.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    }
}

void ControllerLink::pump() {
    if (!useWriter_) {
        writeQueued();
        return;
    }
    {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(wakeMutex_);
        wakeFlag_ = true;
    }
    wake_.notify_one();
}

bool ControllerLink::send(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t n) {
    if (!isConnected() || !data || n == 0 || n > kMaxDeviceMessage) return false;
    writeQueued();  // what the session already queued goes first
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(sendMutex_);
    if (!out_) return false;
    out_->send(data, n);
    sent_.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    return true;
}

void ControllerLink::startWriter() {
    if (!useWriter_ || writer_.joinable()) return;
    writerRun_.store(true, std::memory_order_release);
    writer_ = std::thread([this] {
        while (writerRun_.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) {
            {
                // Woken by pump() once a frame; the timeout only bounds the wait if the frame loop stalls.
                std::unique_lock<std::mutex> lk(wakeMutex_);
                wake_.wait_for(lk, std::chrono::milliseconds(50),
                               [this] { return wakeFlag_ || !writerRun_.load(std::memory_order_acquire); });
                wakeFlag_ = false;
            }
            writeQueued();
        }
    });
}

void ControllerLink::stopWriter() {
    if (!writer_.joinable()) return;
    {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(wakeMutex_);
        writerRun_.store(false, std::memory_order_release);
    }
    wake_.notify_one();
    writer_.join();
}

}  // namespace rp::launchpad
````

````cpp
#pragma once

#include <array>
#include <atomic>
#include <condition_variable>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <memory>
#include <mutex>
#include <string>
#include <thread>
#include <vector>

#include "launchpad/SurfaceLink.hpp"
#include "launchpad/desktop/MidiPort.hpp"
#include "transport/SpscRing.hpp"

namespace rp::launchpad {

// Host-side link to a control surface on its own in/out pair, kept out of the shared musical MIDI stream, and the
// rp::launchpad::SurfaceLink a plan's surface nodes bind (docs/modular-graph-phase-f3-design.md section 3). Messages
// from the device arrive on the backend's callback thread and are drained by the audio thread; what the session
// produced for the device during processBlock is pushed by the audio thread and written out by the link's own WRITER
// thread.
//
// This is the transport and nothing else: the protocol, the choice of ports and their persistence all live in TS
// (packages/launchpad/ts, ui/screens/menu/launchpadDevices.ts). Four decisions worth knowing before touching anything
// here:
//
//   1. **Both rings are fixed slots, because the audio thread is one end of each.** Device -> audio keeps one
//      DeviceMessage per slot, tagged with the claim's generation: the producer is the callback thread, and the audio
//      thread copies bytes out and frees nothing. Audio -> writer is a POD SpscRing of the same bound, because there
//      the producer IS the audio thread.
//   2. **Every inbound slot carries the claim it belongs to** (its generation), and the audio thread is the ONLY
//      consumer of the ring. A disconnect never rewinds it from the control thread - that would make the UI thread a
//      second consumer, and the race a UI-thread drain of a vector-slot ring was (the branch's c60a3cf86). Instead
//      whoever consumes a slot drops it when it belongs to an earlier claim.
//   3. **Output leaves on a writer thread, not the audio thread or the UI's frame.** A frame of latency is invisible on
//      a light, and the write can block: WinMM waits for a SysEx to leave the wire, which is ~170 ms for a 538-byte
//      repaint over DIN - a frozen UI if the frame loop did it.
//   4. **The close bytes are an opaque blob.** A device can need telling that it is being let go (a Launchpad in
//      Programmer mode has its own front panel locked until it is), and that has to happen on paths where the JS
//      runtimes may already be gone. TS hands the bytes over with connect(); this class replays them in disconnect()
//      and in its destructor, and never parses them.
class ControllerLink final : public SurfaceLink {
public:
    // The messages the receive ring holds, one DeviceMessage each: 256 slots is a burst of a pad's presses, a scan's
    // replies and a bulk inquiry, with room to spare.
    static constexpr std::size_t kInCapacity = 256;
    // The audio thread's send ring: a whole repaint is one message, and a frame's worth of LED traffic is a handful.
    static constexpr std::size_t kOutCapacity = 32;

    /** `writerThread` false keeps output on the caller's pump() - what the unit tests use, so a write can be asserted
     *  on deterministically. The provider runs the thread. */
    explicit ControllerLink(MidiPortOpener opener, bool writerThread = true);
    ~ControllerLink();  // not virtual: a SurfaceLink is deleted through the host, which owns it, never through this
    ControllerLink(const ControllerLink&)            = delete;
    ControllerLink& operator=(const ControllerLink&) = delete;

    // --- control (UI / main thread) ---
    /** Claim the named pair. Releases any pair already held first (replaying ITS close bytes). On failure nothing is
     *  held and lastError() says why. */
    bool connect(const std::string& inName, const std::string& outName, std::vector<std::uint8_t> closeBytes);
    void disconnect();
    bool isConnected() const { return connected_.load(std::memory_order_acquire); }
    /** The claim's number: a new one on every successful connect, 0 while nothing is held. What the surface nodes report
     *  as the device's generation, so a pair swapped faster than a block still reads as a NEW device. */
    std::uint32_t generation() const override {
        return connected_.load(std::memory_order_acquire) ? generation_.load(std::memory_order_acquire) : 0;
    }
    const std::string& inputName() const { return inName_; }
    const std::string& outputName() const { return outName_; }
    std::string        lastError() const;

    /** Wake the writer: call once per host frame (never blocks). Without a writer thread this writes queued output
     *  here instead. */
    void pump();

    /** Write `bytes` to the device now, after whatever is already queued (UI thread). For a message that is not the
     *  session's - letting the device go when the app driving it is switched off, while the pair stays claimed. */
    bool send(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t n);

    // --- audio thread ---
    /** Copy the messages received under the CURRENT claim since the last call into `out`, at most `capacity`, and answer
     *  how many: fewer than `capacity` only when the ring has nothing left. A slot from an earlier claim is skipped and
     *  freed in place. Allocation-free. */
    std::size_t drainInput(DeviceMessage* out, std::size_t capacity) override;
    /** Queue one message for the device. Lock-free, never blocks; drops (and counts) when the ring is full, the
     *  message is oversized, or nothing is connected. */
    void pushOutput(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t size) override;

    // --- status ---
    std::uint64_t messagesSent() const { return sent_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed); }
    /** Lost to a full ring, an oversized message, or a push while nothing was attached, since connect. A change in this
     *  between blocks means the device is missing LED updates the session believes it sent. */
    std::uint64_t dropped() const override { return dropped_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed); }

private:
    void pushInputRing(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t n, std::uint32_t gen);  // backend callback thread
    void writeQueued();  // the ring's consumer: the writer thread, or pump() without one
    void startWriter();
    void stopWriter();

    struct InSlot {
        DeviceMessage msg;
        std::uint32_t gen   = 0;  // the claim this arrived under
    };
    struct OutMessage {
        std::uint32_t gen                  = 0;  // the claim the session produced it for
        std::uint16_t len                  = 0;
        std::uint8_t  data[kMaxDeviceMessage] = {0};
    };

    MidiPortOpener             opener_;
    bool                       useWriter_;
    std::unique_ptr<IMidiPort> out_;
    std::unique_ptr<IMidiPort> in_;          // reset() cancels the callback before we return
    std::vector<std::uint8_t>  closeBytes_;  // opaque, from TS
    std::string                inName_, outName_;
    std::string                error_;       // main thread only (connect writes, the status reads)
    std::uint32_t              nextGen_ = 0; // main thread only

    std::atomic<bool>          connected_{false};
    std::atomic<std::uint32_t> generation_{0};
    std::atomic<std::uint64_t> sent_{0};
    std::atomic<std::uint64_t> dropped_{0};

    // device -> audio. Fixed slots, ONE producer (the current port's callback: the previous port's is cancelled before
    // the next opens) and ONE consumer (the audio thread). Overflow drops and counts.
    std::array<InSlot, kInCapacity> inRing_{};
    std::atomic<std::size_t>        inHead_{0};  // consumer index (audio thread ONLY)
    std::atomic<std::size_t>        inTail_{0};  // producer index (callback thread)

    // audio -> writer. POD slots: the producer is the audio thread, so nothing here may allocate.
    SpscRing<OutMessage, kOutCapacity> outRing_;

    // The writer thread and what it waits on. popMutex_ is the send ring's single-consumer seat (the writer's drain,
    // send()'s flush and disconnect()'s), and sendMutex_ serialises every write to out_ (the same three), so the port is
    // never written from two threads at once and the UI thread waits for one write, not for a whole queue of them.
    std::mutex              popMutex_;
    std::mutex              sendMutex_;
    std::mutex              wakeMutex_;
    std::condition_variable wake_;
    bool                    wakeFlag_ = false;  // guarded by wakeMutex_
    std::atomic<bool>       writerRun_{false};
    std::thread             writer_;  // LAST: joined before the members it uses go away
};

}  // namespace rp::launchpad
````

````cpp
#include "launchpad/desktop/LaunchpadProvider.hpp"

#include <cstdio>
#include <exception>
#include <string>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>

#include "launchpad/SurfaceLink.hpp"
#include "launchpad/desktop/RtMidiPort.hpp"

namespace rp::launchpad {
namespace {

// Everything the provider owns, in the order it is built and the reverse of the order it goes: the host it was handed
// (copied, so the product's strings are read once and outlive the provider), the link, the pool and the facet over both.
// The link is cleared from the registry before any of them is freed, so a lookup after the stop finds nothing: an
// acquire answers null and the node that asks runs on its stub. That does not make it safe to stop the provider under a
// plan, as a node holds the link it acquired (rp_device.h): a product reclaims its plans before it stops its providers.
struct Provider {
    Provider(const rp_device_host& given, MidiPortOpener portOpener, PortLister lister)
        : host(given),
          opener(std::move(portOpener)),
          link(opener),
          pool(opener),
          rpc(link, pool, &host, std::move(lister)) {
        // One claim per machine (PortClaim): two standalones restoring one config.json must not both take one device.
        // The config dir is the product's, copied above, so the locks live where its other state does.
        const std::string configDir = host.config_dir ? host.config_dir : "";
        rpc.setClaim([configDir](const std::string& port) { return claimPort(configDir, port); });
        // A scan's held edge: while the pool holds any input, the product suspends its shared stream's hardware inputs
        // (a Windows input is exclusive, so a scan could not otherwise hear the interface the user picked). A product
        // with nothing to suspend ignores the call.
        pool.setOnInputsHeld([this](bool held) {
            if (host.suspend_hardware_inputs) host.suspend_hardware_inputs(host.ctx, held);
        });
        // A refusal (a full table, the name taken) leaves the surface nodes on NoSurface, so it is said, not swallowed.
        installed = host.install && host.install(host.ctx, kDeviceName, kSurfaceLinkInterface,
                                                 static_cast<SurfaceLink*>(&link), nullptr, nullptr);
        if (!installed) std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug] the Launchpad surface link was not installed\n");
    }
    ~Provider() {
        if (installed && host.clear) host.clear(host.ctx, static_cast<SurfaceLink*>(&link));
        // The goodbye goes out while the cross-process claim is still held: the facet owns those tokens and is destroyed
        // before the link is, so without this another process could take the lock and open the port this one is still
        // writing its close bytes to.
        link.disconnect();
    }
    Provider(const Provider&)            = delete;
    Provider& operator=(const Provider&) = delete;

    rp_device_host host;
    MidiPortOpener opener;  // the link's and the pool's: a test's fake is therefore the one a scan gets too
    ControllerLink link;
    MidiPortPool   pool;
    LaunchpadRpc   rpc;
    bool           installed = false;
};

Provider& providerOf(void* self) {
    return *static_cast<Provider*>(self);
}

// The table's entries throw nothing (graph/rp_provider.h): a create that throws (an allocation) answers null and says
// why.
void* createWithRtMidi(const rp_device_host* host) noexcept {
    try {
        return createProvider(host, rtMidiPortOpener("RetroPlug Launchpad"),
                              [] {
                                  const PortNames names = listMidiPorts();
                                  return LaunchpadPortsDto{names.inputs, names.outputs};
                              });
    } catch (...) {
        std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug] the Launchpad provider did not start\n");
        return nullptr;
    }
}

// Nothing is persisted here: config.json's `controlSurface` is TS's, and the control plane claims the pair through the
// facet once it has read it. A product that starts the provider and never hears from TS holds no port.
void restore(void* self) noexcept {
    (void)self;
}

void* rpcService(void* self) noexcept {
    return &providerOf(self).rpc;
}

void destroy(void* self) noexcept {
    delete static_cast<Provider*>(self);
}

// The product's frame: what the audio thread queued for the device goes out now, rather than at the writer thread's
// next timeout. Without a writer thread pump() writes on this thread, which is what a test asserts deterministically.
void wake(void* self) noexcept {
    providerOf(self).link.pump();
}

}  // namespace

void* createProvider(const rp_device_host* host, MidiPortOpener opener, PortLister lister) {
    if (!host || host->abi_version != RP_PROVIDER_ABI_VERSION) return nullptr;
    try {
        return new Provider(*host, std::move(opener), std::move(lister));
    } catch (const std::exception& e) {
        std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug] the Launchpad provider did not start: %s\n", e.what());
    } catch (...) {
        std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug] the Launchpad provider did not start\n");
    }
    return nullptr;
}

ControllerLink& providerLink(void* self) {
    return providerOf(self).link;
}

}  // namespace rp::launchpad

extern "C" const rp_provider* rp_launchpad_provider(void) {
    static const rp_provider kProvider{RP_PROVIDER_ABI_VERSION, "launchpad", &rp::launchpad::createWithRtMidi,
                                       &rp::launchpad::restore, &rp::launchpad::rpcService, &rp::launchpad::destroy,
                                       &rp::launchpad::wake};
    return &kProvider;
}
````

````cpp
// claimed pair, its rings and its writer thread), the MidiPortPool (the ports a TS scan opens) and the facet's service
// (launchpad/desktop/LaunchpadRpc.hpp), and installs the link in the engine's registry as `launchpad` /
// rp.launchpad.surface-link/2 (launchpad/SurfaceLink.hpp) for the surface nodes to bind. rp_launchpad_provider is the

// provider threw (said on stderr): nothing it throws leaves here, as nothing may cross the C table.
````

````cpp
#include "launchpad/desktop/LaunchpadRpc.hpp"

#include <algorithm>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <utility>

namespace rp::launchpad {
namespace {

// rfl::Bytestring is a vector of std::byte; the link and the pool speak std::uint8_t. One conversion each way, so no
// call site has to know.
std::vector<std::uint8_t> bytesOf(const rfl::Bytestring& bytes) {
    const auto* at = reinterpret_cast<const std::uint8_t*>(bytes.data());
    return std::vector<std::uint8_t>(at, at + bytes.size());
}

rfl::Bytestring byteStringOf(const std::vector<std::uint8_t>& bytes) {
    const auto* at = reinterpret_cast<const std::byte*>(bytes.data());
    return rfl::Bytestring(at, at + bytes.size());
}

LaunchpadStatusDto statusOf(ControllerLink& link, const std::string& claimError) {
    LaunchpadStatusDto dto;
    dto.connected  = link.isConnected();
    dto.generation = link.generation();
    dto.sent       = link.messagesSent();
    dto.dropped    = link.dropped();
    dto.input      = link.inputName();
    dto.output     = link.outputName();
    dto.error      = !claimError.empty() ? claimError : link.lastError();
    return dto;
}

}  // namespace

LaunchpadRpc::LaunchpadRpc(ControllerLink& link, MidiPortPool& pool, const rp_device_host* host, PortLister lister)
    : link_(link), pool_(pool), host_(host), lister_(std::move(lister)) {}

LaunchpadRpc::~LaunchpadRpc() = default;

void LaunchpadRpc::reserve(const std::string& input, const std::string& output) {
    // The product keeps the claimed pair out of its shared MIDI stream (a second reader would answer the scan's probes
    // and take the user's pad presses as music). Empty names undo it. A host with no shared stream answers true; a
    // refusal only means the pair is also in the stream, which is a menu complaint, not a lost device.
    if (host_ && host_->reserve_midi) host_->reserve_midi(host_->ctx, input.c_str(), output.c_str());
}

LaunchpadPortsDto LaunchpadRpc::launchpadPorts() {
    return lister_ ? lister_() : LaunchpadPortsDto{};
}

LaunchpadStatusDto LaunchpadRpc::launchpadStatus() {
    return statusOf(link_, error_);
}

LaunchpadStatusDto LaunchpadRpc::launchpadClaim(std::string input, std::string output, rfl::Bytestring closeBytes) {
    error_.clear();
    // The OLD pair goes first, while its ports and its claim are still held: it is closed (with the bytes that unlock
    // its front panel), its cross-process claims are given back and it rejoins the shared stream. Only then is the new
    // one picked up, so the product never has two pairs to reopen around and a refused claim cannot leave the previous
    // device connected and unlocked.
    link_.disconnect();
    claimIn_.reset();
    claimOut_.reset();
    reserve("", "");
    const auto fail = [&](std::string why) {
        reserve("", "");
        error_ = std::move(why);
        return statusOf(link_, error_);
    };
    if (input.empty() || output.empty()) return fail("no port chosen");
    // Both ports must be HERE before anything is reserved: a stale or unplugged pick would otherwise reserve, fail to
    // open and hand back - two reopens of the shared stream, and two audio restarts, for nothing.
    if (lister_) {
        const LaunchpadPortsDto ports = lister_();
        if (std::find(ports.inputs.begin(), ports.inputs.end(), input) == ports.inputs.end())
            return fail("not connected: " + input);
        if (std::find(ports.outputs.begin(), ports.outputs.end(), output) == ports.outputs.end())
            return fail("not connected: " + output);
    }
    // Then the cross-process claims, on BOTH ports: two instances with different inputs must not share one output
    // either. Held before anything opens, so a refusal opens nothing. An interface whose input and output are one
    // name (ALSA's "client:port N:M", CoreMIDI's endpoint, WinMM's "LPProMK3 MIDI" both ways) is ONE claim: a second
    // claim of the same name is refused by our own lock, which would make the ordinary device unclaimable.
    if (claim_) {
        claimIn_  = claim_(input);
        claimOut_ = output == input ? claimIn_ : claim_(output);
        if (!claimIn_ || !claimOut_) {
            claimIn_.reset();
            claimOut_.reset();
            // Held by another RetroPlug - and so still kept OUT of this one's shared stream. Giving it back here would
            // let this process hear every pad press the other one is taking as raw notes (a row launch in this cart
            // too), and mirror its own MIDI out onto the other one's pads.
            reserve(input, output);
            error_ = "in use by another RetroPlug";
            return statusOf(link_, error_);
        }
    }
    // BEFORE the open: the shared stream must have let go of both (a Windows input it still held could not be opened
    // at all), and what the stream holds is the product's to change (it may stop audio for it).
    reserve(input, output);
    if (!link_.connect(input, output, bytesOf(closeBytes))) {
        claimIn_.reset();
        claimOut_.reset();
        return fail(link_.lastError());
    }
    return statusOf(link_, error_);
}

LaunchpadStatusDto LaunchpadRpc::launchpadRelease() {
    // The close bytes go out first: the device's front panel is locked until they do, and the claim keeping it out of
    // the shared stream ends after the port is closed.
    link_.disconnect();
    reserve("", "");
    claimIn_.reset();
    claimOut_.reset();
    error_.clear();
    return statusOf(link_, error_);
}

bool LaunchpadRpc::launchpadSend(rfl::Bytestring data) {
    const std::vector<std::uint8_t> bytes = bytesOf(data);
    return link_.send(bytes.data(), bytes.size());
}

bool LaunchpadRpc::launchpadRestored() {
    // The rendezvous's end (docs/modular-graph-phase-f3-design.md section 3): the control plane read its selection,
    // claimed the pair and is now ready, so a product that held MIDI and audio for the claim starts them. The provider
    // is the only one that can tell the product (rp_device_host::restored), which is why a product names no class of
    // this pack. Always true: a product that holds nothing has nothing to resume.
    if (host_ && host_->restored) host_->restored(host_->ctx);
    return true;
}

std::vector<std::int32_t> LaunchpadRpc::launchpadOpenInputs(std::vector<std::string> names) {
    const std::vector<int> handles = pool_.openInputs(names);
    std::vector<std::int32_t> out;
    out.reserve(handles.size());
    for (int h : handles) out.push_back(h);
    return out;
}

std::int32_t LaunchpadRpc::launchpadOpenOutput(std::string name) {
    return pool_.openOutput(name);
}

bool LaunchpadRpc::launchpadPortSend(std::int32_t handle, rfl::Bytestring data) {
    const std::vector<std::uint8_t> bytes = bytesOf(data);
    return pool_.send(handle, bytes.data(), bytes.size());
}

LaunchpadReadDto LaunchpadRpc::launchpadPortRead(std::int32_t handle) {
    LaunchpadReadDto dto;
    for (auto& message : pool_.read(handle)) dto.messages.push_back(byteStringOf(message));
    dto.dropped = pool_.dropped(handle);
    return dto;
}

bool LaunchpadRpc::launchpadPortClose(std::int32_t handle) {
    pool_.close(handle);
    return true;
}

std::string LaunchpadRpc::launchpadPortError() {
    return pool_.lastError();
}

}  // namespace rp::launchpad
````

````cpp
#pragma once

// The Launchpad facet (docs/modular-graph-phase-f3-design.md section 3): what a product that starts the pack's provider
// mounts on its RPC server, through the rp_register_package_rpc cmake/packages.cmake generates for it from the pack's
// manifest (its `rpc` field names this header and registerRpc). Both halves are answered on the thread the server
// answers on, the control thread, and both are synchronous: a scan steps a few calls per frame, and a claim opens two
// ports.
//
// It is TS's only door to ports. The claimed-pair half is what the control plane drives once a Launchpad is chosen: the
// port names, the claim (with the opaque close bytes the device is let go with), the release, the status a menu line
// reads, and a raw send for a message that is not the session's. The pool half is what a SCAN is built from: single
// port handles, opened in a batch, written to and read from, closed. The probe's bytes, the timing, the meaning of an
// answer and which device answered are all TS's (packages/launchpad/ts/portScan.ts), so native never learns the
// protocol and a second surface is a TS change.
//
// A product that does not mount it has no Launchpad submenu, since the UI takes "the facet answers" for "this host has
// the control-surface seam" (hasLaunchpad). The provider owns the link, the pool and the host's reserve calls; this
// class is the table over them.

#include <cstdint>
#include <functional>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include <rfl/Bytestring.hpp>

#include "graph/rp_provider.h"
#include "launchpad/desktop/ControllerLink.hpp"
#include "launchpad/desktop/MidiPortPool.hpp"
#include "launchpad/desktop/PortClaim.hpp"

namespace rp::launchpad {

// One entry of the port pickers: the system's MIDI inputs, then its outputs, by the names the backend reports.
struct LaunchpadPortsDto {
    std::vector<std::string> inputs;
    std::vector<std::string> outputs;
};

// What the menu's status line and the TS client read: whether the pair is held, its generation (what the session
// compares), the bytes sent and lost since the claim, the pair's names and the last failure's words.
struct LaunchpadStatusDto {
    bool          connected = false;
    std::uint32_t generation = 0;
    std::uint64_t sent = 0;
    std::uint64_t dropped = 0;
    std::string   input;
    std::string   output;
    std::string   error;
};

// What a scan's read answers: the messages that arrived since the last read, and how many the queue lost.
struct LaunchpadReadDto {
    std::vector<rfl::Bytestring> messages;
    std::uint64_t                dropped = 0;
};

// The port names the picker and a scan's "open every port" need: the provider's lister (the real RtMidi enumeration, or
// a test host's scripted one), so a test opens nothing.
using PortLister = std::function<LaunchpadPortsDto()>;

// A claim on one port against other PROCESSES (PortClaim's claimPort in production; a null token = held elsewhere).
// Injected so a test needs no filesystem, and unset means no cross-process coordination.
using ClaimFn = std::function<PortClaim(const std::string& port)>;

class LaunchpadRpc {
public:
    // `host` may be null (a test): it is only read to keep the claimed pair out of the product's shared MIDI stream
    // (rp_device_host::reserve_midi, docs/modular-graph-phase-f3-design.md section 3), which a host with no shared
    // stream has no need of.
    LaunchpadRpc(ControllerLink& link, MidiPortPool& pool, const rp_device_host* host, PortLister lister);
    // The cross-process claim the provider installs (claimPort under the product's config dir). Unset: this process is
    // the only one that might hold a port.
    void setClaim(ClaimFn fn) { claim_ = std::move(fn); }
    ~LaunchpadRpc();
    LaunchpadRpc(const LaunchpadRpc&)            = delete;
    LaunchpadRpc& operator=(const LaunchpadRpc&) = delete;

    // --- the claimed pair (the control plane's) ---

    // The system's MIDI inputs and outputs.
    LaunchpadPortsDto launchpadPorts();
    // The pair's state: held or not, its generation, its counts, the names and the last error.
    LaunchpadStatusDto launchpadStatus();
    // Claim the named pair, with the bytes that let the device go (an opaque blob, replayed on release and at
    // shutdown), in this order: the pair already held is closed (its close bytes) and its claims given back, both ports
    // are checked to be present, both are claimed against other processes (one claim when the input and the output are
    // one name, as an interface's ports commonly are), the pair is kept out of the product's shared MIDI stream BEFORE
    // the ports are opened (a Windows input the stream still held could not be opened at all), and then it is opened.
    // A claim that fails leaves nothing held, keeps the pair out of the stream, and answers its error in `error`.
    LaunchpadStatusDto launchpadClaim(std::string input, std::string output, rfl::Bytestring closeBytes);
    // Give the device back (its close bytes first) and let the shared stream have the pair again.
    LaunchpadStatusDto launchpadRelease();
    // Write `data` to the claimed pair now, after what the session queued. For letting the device go while the pair
    // stays claimed (the app switched off); false when nothing is held.
    bool launchpadSend(rfl::Bytestring data);
    // The startup rendezvous's end (design section 3): a product that held MIDI and audio for the claim resumes them
    // here, through the provider's rp_device_host::restored (the product names no class of this pack). Always true, and
    // a product that holds nothing answers at once.
    bool launchpadRestored();

    // --- the pool (a scan's) ---

    // Open every named input as ONE held edge (a Windows input is exclusive, so the shared stream's inputs step aside
    // for the batch): a handle per name, 0 for each that would not open.
    std::vector<std::int32_t> launchpadOpenInputs(std::vector<std::string> names);
    // Open one output: a handle, or 0.
    std::int32_t launchpadOpenOutput(std::string name);
    bool         launchpadPortSend(std::int32_t handle, rfl::Bytestring data);
    LaunchpadReadDto launchpadPortRead(std::int32_t handle);
    bool         launchpadPortClose(std::int32_t handle);
    // The pool's last failure's words (the first port that refused in a batch, else empty).
    std::string launchpadPortError();

private:
    void reserve(const std::string& input, const std::string& output);

    ControllerLink&       link_;
    MidiPortPool&         pool_;
    const rp_device_host* host_;
    PortLister            lister_;
    ClaimFn               claim_;
    // The last claim's own failure (a port held by another process, a refused open): the link's lastError is its own,
    // and a claim refused before anything opens leaves the link with nothing to say.
    std::string           error_;
    PortClaim             claimIn_;
    PortClaim             claimOut_;
};

// Mount the facet on `server`: an rpcpp TypedRpcServer whose codec carries rfl::Bytestring, which the products' QuickJS
// codec does as a Uint8Array (the tests mount it on the same) and the JSON codec cannot. `service` is the provider's
// (rp_provider.rpc_service), a LaunchpadRpc; null (the provider did not start) mounts nothing, so the UI reads the host
// as having no Launchpad seam. The one template of the facet: it adds the methods to a server, and the methods are the
// pack's library's.
template <class Server>
void registerRpc(Server& server, void* service) {
    if (!service) return;
    LaunchpadRpc& rpc = *static_cast<LaunchpadRpc*>(service);
    server.template addMethod<&LaunchpadRpc::launchpadPorts>(rpc);
    server.template addMethod<&LaunchpadRpc::launchpadStatus>(rpc);
    server.template addMethod<&LaunchpadRpc::launchpadClaim>(rpc);
    server.template addMethod<&LaunchpadRpc::launchpadRelease>(rpc);
    server.template addMethod<&LaunchpadRpc::launchpadSend>(rpc);
    server.template addMethod<&LaunchpadRpc::launchpadRestored>(rpc);
    server.template addMethod<&LaunchpadRpc::launchpadOpenInputs>(rpc);
    server.template addMethod<&LaunchpadRpc::launchpadOpenOutput>(rpc);
    server.template addMethod<&LaunchpadRpc::launchpadPortSend>(rpc);
    server.template addMethod<&LaunchpadRpc::launchpadPortRead>(rpc);
    server.template addMethod<&LaunchpadRpc::launchpadPortClose>(rpc);
    server.template addMethod<&LaunchpadRpc::launchpadPortError>(rpc);
}

}  // namespace rp::launchpad
````

````cpp
#pragma once

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <functional>
#include <memory>
#include <string>

namespace rp::launchpad {

// A MIDI endpoint owned EXCLUSIVELY by whoever opened it. Injected rather than concrete so everything above it depends
// on no MIDI library and is testable with nothing plugged in; RtMidiPort.cpp is the only translation unit here that
// includes RtMidi.h.
//
// Nothing here knows what device is on the other end. Every byte that crosses - LED traffic, the probe a scan sends,
// the bytes that release a device on close - is built and parsed in TS (packages/launchpad/ts), so supporting another
// control surface is a TS change, never a C++ one.
class IMidiPort {
public:
    // Delivered on the MIDI backend's OWN callback thread, once per received message.
    using Receiver = std::function<void(const std::uint8_t*, std::size_t)>;

    virtual ~IMidiPort() = default;
    virtual void send(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t n) = 0;
};

/** Open ONE port: an input when `input` (delivering to `receiver`), else an output (whose `receiver` is unused; an
 *  output port never calls it, and an input port's send() is a no-op). Throws when the named port is absent or will
 *  not open. */
using MidiPortOpener =
    std::function<std::unique_ptr<IMidiPort>(bool input, const std::string& name, IMidiPort::Receiver receiver)>;

}  // namespace rp::launchpad
````

````cpp
#include "launchpad/desktop/MidiPortPool.hpp"

#include <exception>
#include <utility>

namespace rp::launchpad {

std::vector<int> MidiPortPool::openInputs(const std::vector<std::string>& names) {
    std::vector<int> handles;
    if (names.empty()) return handles;
    if (!opener_) {
        error_ = "no MIDI backend";
        return std::vector<int>(names.size(), 0);
    }
    // Raised BEFORE the opens, so the host's own stream has already let go of the inputs we are about to ask
    // for. Undone below if none of them opened and no other input is held.
    const bool  wasHeld = inputs_ > 0;
    std::string firstError;
    if (!wasHeld) heldEdge(true);
    for (const std::string& name : names) {
        handles.push_back(openOne(true, name));
        if (handles.back() == 0 && firstError.empty()) firstError = error_;
    }
    error_ = firstError;  // the first refusal, not whichever port happened to be last
    if (!wasHeld && inputs_ == 0) heldEdge(false);
    return handles;
}

int MidiPortPool::openOutput(const std::string& name) {
    if (!opener_) {
        error_ = "no MIDI backend";
        return 0;
    }
    return openOne(false, name);
}

int MidiPortPool::openOne(bool input, const std::string& name) {
    if (!opener_) {
        error_ = "no MIDI backend";
        return 0;
    }
    Entry e;
    e.input = input;
    e.queue = std::make_shared<Queue>();
    try {
        IMidiPort::Receiver receiver;
        if (input) {
            receiver = [q = e.queue](const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t n) {  // backend callback thread
                if (!data || n == 0) return;
                std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(q->m);
                if (q->messages.size() >= kMaxQueued) {
                    q->dropped++;
                    return;
                }
                q->messages.emplace_back(data, data + n);
            };
        }
        e.port = opener_(input, name, std::move(receiver));
        if (!e.port) error_ = "MIDI port unavailable";
    } catch (const std::exception& ex) {
        error_ = ex.what();
        e.port.reset();
    }
    if (!e.port) return 0;
    error_.clear();
    const int handle = next_++;
    ports_.emplace(handle, std::move(e));
    if (input) inputs_++;
    return handle;
}

bool MidiPortPool::send(int handle, const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t n) {
    auto it = ports_.find(handle);
    if (it == ports_.end() || it->second.input || !data || n == 0) return false;
    it->second.port->send(data, n);
    return true;
}

std::vector<MidiPortPool::Message> MidiPortPool::read(int handle) {
    std::vector<Message> out;
    auto                 it = ports_.find(handle);
    if (it == ports_.end() || !it->second.input) return out;
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(it->second.queue->m);
    out.swap(it->second.queue->messages);
    return out;
}

std::uint64_t MidiPortPool::dropped(int handle) const {
    auto it = ports_.find(handle);
    if (it == ports_.end() || !it->second.input) return 0;
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(it->second.queue->m);
    return it->second.queue->dropped;
}

void MidiPortPool::close(int handle) {
    auto it = ports_.find(handle);
    if (it == ports_.end()) return;
    const bool input = it->second.input;
    ports_.erase(it);  // the port is destroyed here, cancelling its callback
    if (input && --inputs_ == 0) heldEdge(false);
}

void MidiPortPool::closeAll() {
    const bool hadInputs = inputs_ > 0;
    ports_.clear();
    inputs_ = 0;
    if (hadInputs) heldEdge(false);
}

}  // namespace rp::launchpad
````

````cpp
#pragma once

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <functional>
#include <map>
#include <memory>
#include <mutex>
#include <string>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>

#include "launchpad/desktop/MidiPort.hpp"

namespace rp::launchpad {

// Single-direction MIDI ports opened and driven from TS on the UI thread, by integer handle. This is what a
// control-surface SCAN is built from (open every input, write a probe out of each output in turn, read what
// came back), and it is deliberately the generic shape rather than a scanner: the probe, the timing and the
// meaning of the answers are all TS's, so a second kind of device (or an extension that needs to talk to some box
// once to configure it) needs no native code.
//
// Not real-time. Inputs queue what arrives (on the backend's callback thread) behind a mutex, and TS reads
// the queue once a frame. Every call is UI-thread only.
class MidiPortPool {
public:
    using Message = std::vector<std::uint8_t>;

    /** Fired on the UI thread when the number of open INPUTS goes 0 -> 1 (`held` true) and back to 0. A
     *  Windows MIDI input is exclusive, so the host takes its shared stream's hardware inputs down while the
     *  pool holds any - otherwise a scan could not hear the very interface the user picked as their input,
     *  which is exactly the rig a DIN-attached control surface is on. Outputs deliberately do not count: the
     *  host's output is the user's synth, and cutting it for a scan would hang held notes; a scan simply
     *  cannot probe a port that output holds. Tied to the pool rather than to a hook TS calls, so a scan that
     *  dies half way still gives the inputs back on close. */
    using InputsHeldFn = std::function<void(bool held)>;

    /** Messages kept per input between reads. A port with a sequencer on it can talk continuously and is
     *  read once a frame; overflow drops the newest and counts it. */
    static constexpr std::size_t kMaxQueued = 256;

    explicit MidiPortPool(MidiPortOpener opener) : opener_(std::move(opener)) {}
    ~MidiPortPool() { closeAll(); }
    MidiPortPool(const MidiPortPool&)            = delete;
    MidiPortPool& operator=(const MidiPortPool&) = delete;

    void setOnInputsHeld(InputsHeldFn fn) { onInputsHeld_ = std::move(fn); }

    /** Open several inputs as ONE held edge: a scan opens every input at once, and opening them one by one
     *  would cost the host an audio stop/start for every leading input that refuses. A handle per name, 0
     *  for each that would not open (lastError() says why, for the first). */
    std::vector<int> openInputs(const std::vector<std::string>& names);
    /** Open one output. A handle > 0, or 0 when it would not open. */
    int openOutput(const std::string& name);
    std::string lastError() const { return error_; }

    /** Write to an output handle. False for an unknown handle or an input. */
    bool send(int handle, const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t n);

    /** Move out what an input handle received since the last read. Empty for an output / unknown handle. */
    std::vector<Message> read(int handle);

    /** Messages an input dropped to a full queue since it opened. */
    std::uint64_t dropped(int handle) const;

    void        close(int handle);
    void        closeAll();
    std::size_t inputCount() const { return inputs_; }

private:
    struct Queue {
        std::mutex           m;
        std::vector<Message> messages;
        std::uint64_t        dropped = 0;
    };
    struct Entry {
        bool                       input = false;
        std::shared_ptr<Queue>     queue;  // shared with the receiver, so it outlives a late callback
        std::unique_ptr<IMidiPort> port;   // LAST: destroyed first, cancelling the callback
    };

    int openOne(bool input, const std::string& name);  // no held edges
    void heldEdge(bool held) {
        if (onInputsHeld_) onInputsHeld_(held);
    }

    MidiPortOpener       opener_;
    InputsHeldFn         onInputsHeld_;
    std::map<int, Entry> ports_;
    int                  next_   = 1;
    std::size_t          inputs_ = 0;
    std::string          error_;
};

}  // namespace rp::launchpad
````

````cpp
#include "launchpad/desktop/PortClaim.hpp"

#include <cstdint>
#include <cstdio>
#include <filesystem>
#include <system_error>

#if defined(_WIN32)
#    ifndef WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN
#        define WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN
#    endif
#    include <windows.h>
#else
#    include <cerrno>
#    include <fcntl.h>
#    include <sys/file.h>
#    include <unistd.h>
#endif

namespace rp::launchpad {
namespace {

/** A port name as a file name: FNV-1a, since names carry spaces, colons and client numbers. */
std::string lockFileName(const std::string& port) {
    std::uint64_t h = 1469598103934665603ull;
    for (unsigned char c : port) {
        h ^= c;
        h *= 1099511628211ull;
    }
    char buf[40];
    std::snprintf(buf, sizeof buf, "control-%016llx.lock", static_cast<unsigned long long>(h));
    return buf;
}

}  // namespace

PortClaim claimPort(const std::string& dir, const std::string& port) {
    if (dir.empty() || port.empty()) return std::make_shared<int>(0);  // nowhere to coordinate: claim locally
    std::error_code ec;
    const std::filesystem::path locks = std::filesystem::path(dir) / "locks";
    std::filesystem::create_directories(locks, ec);
    const std::filesystem::path path = locks / lockFileName(port);
#if defined(_WIN32)
    // Share mode 0: a second CreateFile on the same path, from any process, fails until this handle closes.
    HANDLE h = CreateFileW(path.wstring().c_str(), GENERIC_READ | GENERIC_WRITE, 0, nullptr, OPEN_ALWAYS,
                           FILE_ATTRIBUTE_NORMAL | FILE_FLAG_DELETE_ON_CLOSE, nullptr);
    if (h == INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE) {
        // Held elsewhere is a sharing violation, and also the window in which the holder is closing a
        // FILE_FLAG_DELETE_ON_CLOSE handle (the file is delete-pending, and any open reports access denied): both mean
        // taken, never "cannot coordinate". Any other failure (an unwritable dir) must not refuse.
        const DWORD error = GetLastError();
        return error == ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION || error == ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED ? nullptr : std::make_shared<int>(0);
    }
    return PortClaim(h, [](void* p) { CloseHandle(static_cast<HANDLE>(p)); });
#else
    const int fd = ::open(path.c_str(), O_CREAT | O_RDWR | O_CLOEXEC, 0644);
    if (fd < 0) return std::make_shared<int>(0);  // cannot coordinate (read-only dir): do not refuse over it
    if (::flock(fd, LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB) != 0) {
        // Only "someone else holds it" refuses. Any other failure - a home on SMB/NFS without lock support
        // (ENOLCK, EOPNOTSUPP), some FUSE mounts - means we cannot coordinate, and must not lock the user out
        // of their own device over it.
        const bool held = errno == EWOULDBLOCK || errno == EAGAIN;
        ::close(fd);
        return held ? nullptr : std::make_shared<int>(0);
    }
    return PortClaim(new int(fd), [](void* p) {
        int* fdp = static_cast<int*>(p);
        ::close(*fdp);  // closing the descriptor drops the lock
        delete fdp;
    });
#endif
}

}  // namespace rp::launchpad
````

````cpp
#pragma once

#include <memory>
#include <string>

namespace rp::launchpad {

// A claim on a control-surface port that OTHER PROCESSES can see. RtMidi lets two processes open the same port on ALSA
// and CoreMIDI, so two RetroPlug standalones that both restore the same config.json would both claim one Launchpad:
// every pad press launches in both, and whichever quits first sends the device back to Live mode under the other. (On
// Windows the second open simply fails, which is no better a message: the refusal cannot say why.)
//
// An OS file lock per port, in <dir>/locks/: flock() on POSIX, an unshared CreateFile on Windows. The OS drops it when
// the holder exits, crash included, so a stale lock cannot outlive its process. The returned token IS the claim; null
// means another process holds it.
using PortClaim = std::shared_ptr<void>;

PortClaim claimPort(const std::string& dir, const std::string& port);

}  // namespace rp::launchpad
````

````cpp
#include "launchpad/desktop/RtMidiPort.hpp"

#include <cstdio>
#include <memory>
#include <optional>
#include <stdexcept>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>

#include "RtMidi.h"

#if defined(__APPLE__)
#include <CoreMIDI/CoreMIDI.h>

#include <chrono>
#include <thread>
#endif

namespace rp::launchpad {
namespace {

/** True when an RtMidiIn/RtMidiOut can safely be CONSTRUCTED. On macOS this creates the process's CoreMIDI client first:
 *  RtMidi makes it inside a function declared throw(), whose failure path throws, and a throw across that boundary is
 *  std::terminate - so a failed MIDIClientCreate would abort the host and no catch here could see it. The client is kept
 *  for the process's life on purpose, so RtMidi's own singleton rides on a warm connection. Elsewhere RtMidi reports a
 *  failure as an exception, which the opener catches. Everything that builds an RtMidi object asks this first: this
 *  file's opener and its lister, which are the package's only two.
 *  (packages/native/src/host/input/MidiIo.cpp guards its own RtMidi objects the same way, for the same reason; a package
 *  cannot include it, so the probe is said here too.) */
bool midiSystemUsable() {
#if defined(__APPLE__)
    static const bool ok = [] {
        MIDIClientRef client = 0;
        for (int attempt = 0; attempt < 3; ++attempt) {
            if (MIDIClientCreate(CFSTR("RetroPlug"), nullptr, nullptr, &client) == noErr) return true;  // never disposed
            std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(50));
        }
        std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug] MIDI unavailable: CoreMIDI would not create a client (no Launchpad ports)\n");
        return false;
    }();
    return ok;
#else
    return true;
#endif
}

/** Index of the port named exactly `name` on an open RtMidi endpoint, or none. Exact match, because the caller picked
 *  this name out of the very list these functions enumerated. */
template <class T>
std::optional<unsigned> findPort(T& endpoint, const std::string& name) {
    const unsigned count = endpoint.getPortCount();
    for (unsigned i = 0; i < count; ++i)
        if (endpoint.getPortName(i) == name) return i;
    return std::nullopt;
}

// One port, one direction. An input keeps its RtMidiIn (destroyed first by declaration order, cancelling the callback
// before the receiver dies); an output keeps only its RtMidiOut and ignores send() when it has none.
class RtMidiSinglePort final : public IMidiPort {
public:
    RtMidiSinglePort(const std::string& clientName, bool input, const std::string& name, Receiver receiver)
        : receiver_(std::move(receiver)) {
        if (input) {
            in_            = std::make_unique<RtMidiIn>(RtMidi::UNSPECIFIED, clientName);
            const auto idx = findPort(*in_, name);
            if (!idx) throw std::runtime_error("MIDI input port not found: " + name);
            // (sysex, time, sense) - false means DELIVER. SysEx is a control surface's language; clock is kept because
            // what to do with it is the reader's call, not the port's; active sensing (a keepalive nothing here wants)
            // is dropped.
            in_->ignoreTypes(false, false, true);
            in_->setCallback(&RtMidiSinglePort::onMidiIn, this);
            in_->openPort(*idx, name);
        } else {
            out_           = std::make_unique<RtMidiOut>(RtMidi::UNSPECIFIED, clientName);
            const auto idx = findPort(*out_, name);
            if (!idx) throw std::runtime_error("MIDI output port not found: " + name);
            out_->openPort(*idx, name);
        }
    }

    ~RtMidiSinglePort() override {
        in_.reset();
        out_.reset();
    }

    void send(const std::uint8_t* data, std::size_t n) override {
        if (!out_ || n == 0) return;
        try {
            out_->sendMessage(data, static_cast<std::size_t>(n));
        } catch (RtMidiError&) {
            // A transient send failure (the device was unplugged) must not take down the caller's frame.
        }
    }

private:
    static void onMidiIn(double, std::vector<unsigned char>* message, void* userData) {
        if (!message || message->empty()) return;
        auto* self = static_cast<RtMidiSinglePort*>(userData);
        if (self->receiver_) self->receiver_(message->data(), message->size());
    }

    Receiver                   receiver_;
    std::unique_ptr<RtMidiOut> out_;
    std::unique_ptr<RtMidiIn>  in_;  // LAST: destroyed first, cancelling the callback
};

}  // namespace

MidiPortOpener rtMidiPortOpener(std::string clientName) {
    return [clientName = std::move(clientName)](bool input, const std::string& name,
                                                IMidiPort::Receiver receiver) -> std::unique_ptr<IMidiPort> {
        if (!midiSystemUsable()) throw std::runtime_error("no MIDI system");
        try {
            return std::make_unique<RtMidiSinglePort>(clientName, input, name, std::move(receiver));
        } catch (RtMidiError& e) {
            throw std::runtime_error(e.what());  // one exception type for the link and the pool to catch
        }
    };
}

PortNames listMidiPorts() {
    PortNames out;
    if (!midiSystemUsable()) return out;
    try {
        RtMidiIn in(RtMidi::UNSPECIFIED, "RetroPlug");
        for (unsigned i = 0; i < in.getPortCount(); ++i) out.inputs.push_back(in.getPortName(i));
        RtMidiOut op(RtMidi::UNSPECIFIED, "RetroPlug");
        for (unsigned i = 0; i < op.getPortCount(); ++i) out.outputs.push_back(op.getPortName(i));
    } catch (const std::exception& e) {
        // A MIDI system that comes up but refuses an endpoint (a bare container): no ports, said once.
        std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug] the MIDI system is unavailable: %s\n", e.what());
        out.inputs.clear();
        out.outputs.clear();
    }
    return out;
}

}  // namespace rp::launchpad
````

- [ ] **Step 4: Provider ABI 2**

`rp_provider.h` is at **2**, and it says why: a provider that holds a port pair has to keep it out of the product's
shared stream and cannot do that alone, so `rp_device_host` gains `reserve_midi(ctx, input, output)` (empty names undo
it), `suspend_hardware_inputs(ctx, bool)` (the held edge a scan raises; only Windows acts on it) and `restored(ctx)`
(the rendezvous's product half, so the product names no class of the pack); `rp_provider` gains `wake(self)`, the
per-frame pump, generated as `rp_wake_providers(providers)` and placed last so a provider with nothing to write leaves
it null. A host and a provider refuse each other across a version in both directions: a null-safe optional read would
let a mixed pair run, and there is no mixed pair to run. `ProviderHost` answers the three with no-ops that record
nothing (Task 4 implements the SDL's), the N8 provider reads neither, and `cmake/test-binary.cmake` learns the
`PROVIDERS` pass-through so a test binary that is a product can name its providers.
