````bash
feat(launchpad): the pack's native half, its provider and its facet

Give packages/launchpad its native half (docs/modular-graph-phase-f3-design.md sections 2, 3 and 8): a portable
target with the surface nodes, a desktop target with the transport a Launchpad needs, a provider a product starts
without naming a class of the pack, and the facet TS reaches the hardware through.

The portable target (retroplug-launchpad, `device: true`) holds the rp::launchpad::SurfaceLink contract and the two
nodes, moved out of packages/native (git mv, so their history follows them). The contract is /2: `generation()`
replaces the connected flag, because a pair swapped inside one block must read as a NEW device, and `dropped()` is
what the link lost in BOTH directions (a message it could not hand the device, and one the device sent that its
receive ring had no room for), which a session repaints from. rp.launchpad.surface-in declares no threads (the
link's callback and writer threads are the desktop provider's) and gains a `drops` control output; buildGraph wires
it to the session's controllerDrops, so the drop repaint is live rather than a port nothing reads. The two counters
cross the graph as control values wrapped at 2^24, and the generation is mapped into 1..2^24-1: 0 means "nothing
attached", so a generation that wraps must read as a claim, never as a device going away.

The desktop target (retroplug-launchpad-desktop) is the branch's transport rewritten onto the fixed-slot link:
ControllerLink (the claimed pair; a device-to-audio ring of generation-tagged DeviceMessage slots whose only
consumer is the audio thread, which skips an earlier claim's slots in place, so a disconnect rewinds nothing and
skips nothing it should deliver - and which answers nothing at all while no claim is held, so a drain between the
open and the publish cannot eat the new claim's first messages; a POD SpscRing audio-to-device drained by the
link's own writer thread, with one consumer seat so a UI-thread send() waits for the write in flight rather than for
the queue behind it; the close bytes replayed on disconnect and on destruction), MidiPortPool (the loose ports a TS
scan opens, with the inputs-held edge), PortClaim (one claim per port across processes: flock under
<configDir>/locks, an unshared CreateFile on Windows, where a delete-pending holder's ACCESS_DENIED counts as taken),
and RtMidiPort (the only RtMidi user, SysEx on, and the port lister). On macOS both of its entry points ask a
CoreMIDI probe of their own first: RtMidi makes the client inside a throw() function whose failure throws, so a
failed MIDIClientCreate aborts the host and no catch here can see it (packages/native's MidiIo.cpp guards its own
objects the same way; a package cannot include it).

rp_launchpad_provider installs the link as `launchpad` / rp.launchpad.surface-link/2, as the N8's provider installs
its cart link, and gives the facet its claims and its reserve calls. It disconnects the link in its destructor, before
the facet's claim tokens go, so the goodbye goes out while the cross-process claim is still held. LaunchpadRpc is the
facet: the port lists, the claim, the release, the status, the send, restored(), and the pool's
open-inputs/open-output/send/read/close/error. Its claim follows the branch's order: the pair already held is closed
(with its close bytes) and its claims given back, both ports are checked to be PRESENT against the lister, both are
claimed across processes, the pair is reserved before the ports are opened, and only then is it opened. An input and
an output that carry ONE name - ALSA's "client:port N:M", CoreMIDI's endpoint, WinMM's "LPProMK3 MIDI" both ways -
are one claim, since a second claim of the same name is refused by our own lock and would make the ordinary device
unclaimable. packages/launchpad/ts/client.ts is the facet's client, as @retroplug/n8's createN8Client is the N8's.

The provider ABI stays 2 (unreleased, so it is extended rather than bumped): rp_device_host gains reserve_midi,
suspend_hardware_inputs and restored, the last being the rendezvous's product half, which the facet's restored()
calls so the product resumes the MIDI and audio it held without any product naming a class of the pack. rp_provider
gains wake, the per-frame pump the generated glue exposes as rp_wake_providers(providers): a writer thread woken once
a frame writes the frame the session painted instead of it waiting out its timeout (WinMM blocks ~170 ms on a bulk
SysEx). The N8 provider reads none of them; the products' ProviderHost answers the three with no-ops that record
nothing, which is where the SDL's MidiIo implementation goes.

A product now says which providers it STARTS: retroplug_product(... PROVIDERS <package>...). A package listed in
PACKAGES and not named there contributes its node types and neither its provider nor its desktop target, which is the
closest shape packages.cmake allows for "a third-party pack is carried without its hardware". There is no default:
every product names what it starts. In this commit the SDL standalone, the headless host, the CLI, the engine-graph
test binary and the plugin name n8, which is the set they started before (the headless host starts its own over a fake
cart). No product names launchpad: the SDL keeps running the legacy host this commit does not delete, and the plugin
links no RtMidi, no ALSA/CoreMIDI/WinMM and no system framework for the pack (plugin.cmake refuses a plugin target
that links the pack's desktop half, and refuses one that drops the pack's node types). Stage 4 opts the SDL, the
headless host and the CLI in; the plugin never. Providers.test.cpp holds both halves: this product's generated header
starts the N8's provider alone and installs no surface link and mounts no Launchpad facet, and a header naming the
launchpad package starts it into the product's own engine.

The legacy native host (src/host/launchpad) stays, and its two test files stay with it as
retroplug-launchpad-legacy-test: the products still run on it, so the promises they rest on (the close bytes on both
paths, the rings' bounds, LaunchpadHost's launchpad.cfg, LaunchpadScanner) are still held until stage 4 deletes the
host. Its rp::launchpad::SurfaceLink adapter implements /2 by reporting generation 1 while a pair is held.

rtmidi moves to root scope (cmake/rtmidi.cmake): a package's desktop target links it, and a package is configured
before packages/native's deps.cmake used to add it. It is asked for PIC there, since the plugin formats are shared
modules.

Tests. feature/launchpad's Controller.test.cpp is retargeted onto the fixed-slot link as the pack's own binary
(retroplug-launchpad-test), and every one of its 34 cases is accounted for: 31 are the same case on the new transport
(the claim and its generations, the drain's batches, what an earlier claim queued, the writer thread, the close bytes
on both paths, the pool's held edge and its bounds, PortClaim, the facet's port list, its reservation before the open,
its refusal paths and its claim of a port another process holds), one is its restored case retargeted to the ABI's
restored reaching the product, and two - "switching pairs lets the OLD device go before reserving the new one" and
"reserves nothing for a pick whose ports are not here" - are ported here with the ordering fix they pin. New cases:
the audio path's four calls allocating and freeing nothing (the counting allocator the engine's tests use, compiled
into this binary), the provider's per-frame wake, a same-named pair claimed through a REAL config dir, a claim kept
one-per-port across processes through that dir, a facet whose lister refuses a stale pick, the generation and drops
wraps, and the swap case rewritten to the review's gaps: delivery from a producer thread that runs only between a
connect and its disconnect, pushes from the audio thread too, drained tags never decreasing, and output on claim N's
port carrying nothing older than claim N (tools/run-sanitizer.sh's thread mode now builds and runs this binary, and
tip-verify.sh's tsanlp leg does the same). ProtocolNodes gains the two things a generation and a drop count are for,
driven through buildGraph's real document: a pair swapped inside one block is re-taken (the hello and the full paint
again) and a lost push while attached repaints without re-taking the device.

Intended re-records, each named: the [packages] golden (the two launchpad types register from their own package after
core, not from packages/native's entries: the same set, a new order); the role goldens (the drops wire in eleven
controller documents); one ProtocolNodes digest, and NOT for the drops wire: it was measured that removing that wire
changes no byte of either digest, and the log of the fix pass's own run shows the same new value before the wire

clocks the cart instead of by the distance between two ppq positions, so the first playing block's tick 0 and the
````

---

### Task 4: the products on the pack's provider, and the shell on its facet

Design sections 3, 5, 7, 8 and 9's fourth stage. Everything a user touches lands here: the products start the pack's
provider and implement the ABI's three capability calls, the standalone performs the **startup rendezvous**, the headless
host runs the **real facet over a scripted device** so `test:native` and CI drive it without hardware, the shell's
`launchpadDevices.ts` and menu are rewritten on the facet client and persist through `config.json`'s `controlSurface`,
the legacy host is deleted, and `pnpm sdl:controller` arrives **with its port filter**.

What each product names: `PROVIDERS n8 launchpad` for the SDL, the headless host and the CLI; `n8` alone for the plugin,
whose `plugin.cmake` refuses a plugin target linked to the pack's desktop target and one that does not link the portable
one. The SDL's `AppState` gains the three callbacks - `onReserveMidi` (stop audio, `midi.setReserved(in, out)`, start, and
only when a port this stream holds actually moves), `onSuspendInputs` (the same dance, a true no-op off Windows) and
`onRestored` - and `restoreControlSurface` pumps the JS loop until `restored` lands or **500 ms of wall time** pass,
before `loadMidiConfig`, `midi.open` and `startAudio`. Its frame loop calls `rp_wake_providers`, so the frame the session
painted is the frame the device hears.

`MidiIo` ports the branch's reserved-PAIR half: `setReserved(in, out)`, `reservationChanges`, `reservedOutput`,
`suspensionChanges`, `inputsFor`/`outputFor` - so a change that reopens nothing costs no audio restart - and it skips a
reserved output when it opens hardware. `ProviderHost` carries the product's half as a `Calls` struct with a `record` for
a product that implements none of them (which is what a test reads through the engine facet's harness half,
`setProductCalls`/`drainProductCalls`, mounted by `registerHarnessRpc` and not on the SDL or the plugin), plus
`installLinks`, which the headless host sets false because the graph's control surface there must stay the harness link
that parity stages pad presses into.

The shell: `controlSurface: {input, output, device, enabled}` in `userConfig.ts` (a `.preprocess` one level up, like
`render`, so a malformed block takes the fields' defaults), a **merge-on-write** store (the branch's `1c1c89f1b`: every
setter re-reads the file, applies only its own change, and adopts it only after `writeFileAtomic` says it landed), and
`launchpadDevices.ts` on `createLaunchpadClient` - the port-stem re-match, the close bytes on every claim and release, the
scan (`PortScan` stepped from the frame poll), the model confirmation, forget, and the close bytes a couple of polls after
the project stops driving the controller. The menu's rows come from the app's contribution (`ControllerAppField`), its
cart-sync label from the app's own answer, and the default app id from the registry's first app, so the shell names no
app. The CLI's probe drives the facet, with `--loopback` deliberately still on the shared stream (the facet has no
virtual port, and the loopback measures the stream musical MIDI rides).

**The hardware-safety episode, and the filter it produced.** The first `sdl:controller` harness run - this stage's, and
the `tip-verify` leg that ran it - listed and opened every system MIDI port, the Zoom L6 and a CH345 included, and its
scan sent a Device Inquiry to every output. The fix pass added `RP_MIDI_PORT_ALLOW` (a comma-separated list of name
substrings), honoured by the pack's lister, its opener, the pool, the link and `MidiIo` (whose "All Devices" shrinks to
the allowed ports and which checks the name on the object that opens, since a hot-plug shifts indices); made the harness
refuse to run when a caller has preset the variable; and put a **listing-only** proof first. A review then found the
first list (`LPProMK3 MIDI,RPTestKeys`) would also have admitted a real Pro MK3, so the fake's client name became
`RPFakeLPProMK3`, the list is the two fakes' **whole RtMidi names** built at run time from their own `ready` lines, and
the run fails if a listed port that is not a fake contains `LPProMK3` or `Launchpad`. The rule is held twice (the package
boundary forbids a shared header) and one table-driven case in `retroplug-midi-test` holds the two copies to each other.
`tools/run-sdl-smoke.sh` and `tools/run-sdl-pipewire.sh` gained a scratch `RETROPLUG_USER_CONFIG_DIR` and
`RP_MIDI_PORT_ALLOW=RP_NO_PORT` (an empty list means "every port", so a matches-nothing list has to name something),
because a saved, enabled `controlSurface` is claimed at startup and written to at quit: a smoke on the user's own config
is a hardware test in disguise.

- [ ] **Step 1: The products name their providers**

`retroplug_product(... PROVIDERS n8 launchpad)` for the SDL, the headless host and the CLI; `cmake/packages.cmake`
grows the rule that a product starts only the providers it names (a package listed and not named contributes its node
types and neither its provider entry nor its desktop target - a provider opens ports and runs threads, so a product
says what it starts), refuses a duplicate in the list, and refuses a manifest item that carries BOTH an `entry` and a
`provider` (a product that listed the package without naming it would silently lose the node type, and the link error
would be far from the manifest). `plugin.cmake`'s two refusals hold and now pass, because the plugin's product names
no launchpad provider. `rp_provider.h`'s version-2 note gains `wake`, and `cmake/rtmidi.cmake`'s comment says what PIC
is for now that the pack's own target asks for it. `ProviderHost` becomes the product's half: a `Calls` struct
(`reserveMidi`, `suspendHardwareInputs`, `restored`, each optional), a RECORD of the calls for a product that
implements none (what `drainProductCalls` reads), and `installLinks`.

````diff
diff --git a/cmake/packages.cmake b/cmake/packages.cmake
index b260c6de3..de42e72b5 100644
--- a/cmake/packages.cmake
+++ b/cmake/packages.cmake
@@ -209,6 +209,14 @@ function(_retroplug_read_manifest name _manifest)
             endif()
             list(APPEND _providerEntries ${_entry})
         endif()
+        # An entry is a node TYPE and a provider is a SERVICE that need not belong together: a product that lists the
+        # package and not its PROVIDERS must be able to carry the types and none of the service. One item holding both
````

- [ ] **Step 2: The SDL's rendezvous, the headless fake, and the CLI**

`packages/native/sdl/main.cpp`: the legacy host's members and hooks are gone, replaced by `deviceHost` (with
`AppState`'s three static callbacks) and `providers`; `audioLive` and `controlSurfaceRestored` are the rendezvous's
state; teardown stops the providers after the plans are reclaimed and the display is detached, and
`RETROPLUG_SDL_TEST_SCAN` drives the scan the harness's fourth leg needs. `packages/native/src/main.cpp` starts the
pack's provider over `scriptedOpenerFor`/`listerFor` (a Pro MK3 on `LPProMK3 MIDI` both ways that answers, and an
interface's port that answers nothing) in its own scratch config dir, honours `RETROPLUG_LAUNCHPAD_CLAIM_DIR` and
removes only a directory it created, and keeps the harness surface link. The CLI's `Calls` are three no-ops (it owns
no stream), and `run-native-tests.mjs` exports a claim directory per file so two hosts can share one lock.

````diff
+// ---- the control surface, as this product answers for it ------------------------------------------
+//
+// The three calls a provider makes of the product that owns the shared MIDI stream (rp_provider.h, design section 3).
+// The Launchpad pack's facet asks for them and knows nothing about MidiIo; what they mean here is the two hazards a
+// claimed port has in a stream that is already open: the stream must let go of it BEFORE it is opened (a Windows input
+// is exclusive, and everywhere a pad press reaching both would fire every launch twice while notes out of the stream
+// would light the surface's pads), and reopening RtMidi's hardware ports under a running callback is exactly what
+// reconfigureMidi stops audio for. So: stop audio, re-apply, start - and only when a port this stream holds actually

+    auto& a = *static_cast<AppState*>(ctx);

+    const bool bounce = a.audioLive && a.midi.reservationChanges(input, output);
+    if (bounce) stopAudio(a);
+    a.midi.setReserved(input, output);

+void AppState::onSuspendInputs(void* ctx, bool suspended) {
+    // The scan's held edge, and the one platform where it is real (MidiIo.hpp's scanSuspendsInputs). Answering before
+    // touching the stream is what makes this a no-op off Windows rather than a MIDI outage for the scan's length.
+    if (!retroplug::scanSuspendsInputs()) return;
+    auto& a = *static_cast<AppState*>(ctx);
+    if (a.midi.hardwareInputsSuspended() == suspended) return;
+    // A Windows MIDI input is exclusive, so the stream must let go of the inputs a scan is about to listen on. Off Windows
+    // (ALSA's sequencer, CoreMIDI) an input is SHARED: the scan hears everything the stream does without it closing
+    // anything, so the guard above returns first and neither the user's MIDI nor the audio is disturbed.
+    const bool bounce = a.audioLive && a.midi.suspensionChanges(suspended);
+    if (bounce) stopAudio(a);
+    a.midi.setHardwareInputsSuspended(suspended);
+    if (bounce) startAudio(a);
+}
+
+void AppState::onRestored(void* ctx) { static_cast<AppState*>(ctx)->controlSurfaceRestored = true; }
+
+// Let the control plane apply the control surface it persisted (config.json, launchpadDevices.ts restoreLaunchpad)
+// before MIDI opens and audio starts. A claim made from here lands with audio not yet started, so it is reserved
+// before the shared stream ever opens the port and costs no restart; a claim that arrives after the bound below is a
+// MIDI-SESSION reserve, which onReserveMidi handles the same way a later Connect does.
+//
+// What it waits on is the facet's restored() reaching this product (rp_device_host::restored), because the selection
+// is TS's and the claim is asynchronous with respect to the mount: React runs the restore in an effect, on a later
+// pump of the JS loop. So pump the loop until it lands. Bounded in TIME, not pumps: a pump does not block, so a count
+// would be over in a millisecond. A UI that never reports (a broken bundle, no facet at all) costs half a second at
+// startup and then starts anyway, so a missing or unreadable config.json can never keep the app silent.
+void restoreControlSurface(AppState& a) {
+    const Uint32 start = SDL_GetTicks();
+    while (!a.controlSurfaceRestored && SDL_GetTicks() - start < 500) {
+        a.ui.tick();
+        if (!a.controlSurfaceRestored) SDL_Delay(1);
+    }

+        std::fprintf(stderr, "[retroplug-sdl] control surface: the UI did not report its restore; continuing\n");
+}
````

- [ ] **Step 3: The shell's selection in `config.json`**

`controlSurface` is additive, so no migration step and the schema version stays 3; `serializeUserConfig` writes it (it
diffs two serializations, so a field the writer forgot could never be toggled), and the store gains

- [ ] **Step 4: The facet client, the menu, and the app's own rows**

`launchpadDevices.ts` is the branch's file rewritten on the facet: `resolveClient()` probes the client once with
`status()` (a host that mounted no facet throws there and the module goes inert), `setLaunchpadClient()` is the seam
the tests use, and the rest is the port-stem re-match, `looksLikeLaunchpad` (a prefix match on the stem), the scan
with its model confirmation and publish-once latch, `applyLink` (close bytes on every claim, a failed claim warned in
the facet's words), `restoreLaunchpad` (which ends with the facet's `restored()`), `connectLaunchpad`,
`forgetLaunchpad`, and `pollControllerRole`. `useLaunchpadScanWatch` steps the scan from the frame poll, `App.tsx`
runs the startup restore, and `menuDefs.ts` builds the app's rows from the contribution's `ControllerAppField` (each
knob's default from the app's schema, `parse({})`), words the cart-sync row as "driving it" or "not driving it", and
greys the port pickers while connected or scanning and Forget while a scan runs. `registry.ts` gains `menu`, and the
app declares `quantise` (four labelled choices) and `follow` (a toggle); `page` stays off the menu, which the type
allows.

````diff
+function controllerAppRows(ctx: MenuContext, app: ControllerAppContribution | undefined, config: Record<string, unknown>): MenuItem[] {
+  if (!app || !app.menu) return [];
+  const project = ctx.stores.project;
+  const defaults = app.config.parse({}); // the schema is the source of a knob's default, as it is of its bounds

+  const set = (key: string, value: unknown) => project.setController({ appConfig: { [key]: value } });
+  return app.menu.map((field) => {
+    const id = `lp-app-${field.key}`;
+    if (field.toggle) return cycler(id, field.label, OFF_ON, current(field.key) === false ? 0 : 1, (n) => set(field.key, n === 1));
+    const choices = field.choices ?? [];
+    const at = choices.findIndex((c) => c.value === current(field.key));
+    return cycler(id, field.label, choices.map((c) => c.label), Math.max(0, at), (n) => set(field.key, choices[n].value));
+  });
+}
````

- [ ] **Step 6: The port filter**

One rule, in one header, honoured on five paths, with the reason written twice because the package boundary forbids
sharing a header with the shell: `allowedMidiPorts` hides a port from the scan's sweep and the pickers
(`RtMidiPort.cpp`), the opener throws `MIDI port not allowed: <name>` before it builds an RtMidi object,
`MidiPortPool` answers a 0 handle and that same reason without calling the opener, `ControllerLink::connect` refuses
both names before either port opens, and `MidiIo` applies `midiPortAllowed` on its own side (the pickers,
`inputPortsToOpen` so "All Devices" is every ALLOWED port, the output's match, and every open - checking
`getPortName(i)` on the object that opens, because a client hot-plugged between the probe and the open shifts the
indices). `ControllerLink` in the same block gains the **UI queue** (16 messages, counted when full) the writer
drains, so `send()` never waits for a write in flight nor for the queue behind it; `disconnect()` still joins the
writer and writes the close bytes on the calling thread, which is the owed Windows measurement `spec/07` will say is
owed. `MidiIo` gains the reserved pair and `scanSuspendsInputs()` (true under `_WIN32` only: an ALSA sequencer input
and a CoreMIDI endpoint are shared, so a scan hears the port the stream holds and closing it would cost the user their
MIDI and an audio restart). `Controller.test.cpp` gains the filter's case and the stale-slot case rewritten,
`FakePorts.hpp` grows `Rig::inputs` / `outputs` / `answering` a scripted port and a send delay, and
`MidiPortSelect.test.cpp` gains the shell's two cases and the Windows-only lever, and the configure gains the refusal
of a manifest item that is both an entry and a provider.

Create `packages/launchpad/native/src/launchpad/desktop/MidiPortFilter.hpp`:

````cpp
#pragma once

// The test-only MIDI port allow list, `RP_MIDI_PORT_ALLOW`: a comma-separated list of SUBSTRINGS of a port's name, and a
// port may be listed or opened only when its name contains one of them. Unset or empty means every port, so an ordinary
// run is unchanged.
//
// It exists because a check of this pack drives a REAL standalone: tools/run-sdl-controller.sh stands a fake Launchpad up
// on the ALSA sequencer and then runs the app, whose scan sends a Universal Device Inquiry out of every output the system
// lists and whose shared stream opens every input. On a development machine that is somebody's hardware - a mixer's
// ports, a USB MIDI cable, a Launchpad Pro MK3 - and a test must never write to, or take, a device it did not put there.
// Matching is on a substring because the name a backend reports is not known in advance: RtMidi's ALSA names carry the
// client and port numbers ("LPProMK3 MIDI:1 24:0"), and those move as other clients come and go. The harness therefore
// names its fakes by their WHOLE names, client number included, which is what makes an entry it wrote unable to match a
// real device: the fake's client is a name no device has.
//
// The filter is honoured by everything in this package that touches a port: listMidiPorts (what a scan and the port
// pickers enumerate), the RtMidi opener, MidiPortPool and ControllerLink. packages/native/src/host/input/MidiIo.hpp holds
// the same rule for the host's own shared stream, and cannot share this header (a package may include its own tree and
// its declared packages', not the shell's), so the two are kept in step by hand: one exact-spelling SUBSTRING list, read
// from the one variable. retroplug-midi-test runs both bodies over one table of inputs, so the two cannot drift apart
// without a failed case.
//
// It is NOT a safety feature for a user: a product does not set it, and a user who did would only lose ports from their
// own pickers.

#include <cstdlib>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

namespace rp::launchpad {

/** Whether `name` passes the allow list `spec` (RP_MIDI_PORT_ALLOW's text). An empty spec allows everything, as does a
 *  spec of separators alone ("the list I did not mean to write" is not "no ports at all"). An entry matches when the name
 *  CONTAINS it, case-sensitively. */
inline bool midiPortAllowedBy(const std::string& name, const std::string& spec) {
    std::string entry;
    std::string::size_type at = 0;
    bool any = false;
    while (at <= spec.size()) {
        const std::string::size_type comma = spec.find(',', at);
        entry = spec.substr(at, comma == std::string::npos ? std::string::npos : comma - at);
        // Trim the spaces around an entry, so "A, B" reads as two names rather than one that starts with a space.
        const std::string::size_type first = entry.find_first_not_of(" \t");
        const std::string::size_type last  = entry.find_last_not_of(" \t");
        entry = first == std::string::npos ? std::string() : entry.substr(first, last - first + 1);
        if (!entry.empty()) {
            any = true;
            if (name.find(entry) != std::string::npos) return true;
        }
        if (comma == std::string::npos) break;
        at = comma + 1;
    }
    return !any;
}

/** `midiPortAllowedBy(name, RP_MIDI_PORT_ALLOW)`. Read on every call, so a test can set it up and take it down around a
 *  case; the callers are a port listing or an open, never the audio thread. */
inline bool midiPortAllowed(const std::string& name) {
    const char* spec = std::getenv("RP_MIDI_PORT_ALLOW");
    return midiPortAllowedBy(name, spec ? spec : "");
}

/** The names in `names` that pass `midiPortAllowed`, in order: a port listing under the filter. */
inline std::vector<std::string> allowedMidiPorts(const std::vector<std::string>& names) {
    std::vector<std::string> out;
    for (const std::string& name : names)
        if (midiPortAllowed(name)) out.push_back(name);
    return out;
}

}  // namespace rp::launchpad
````

````diff
+TEST_CASE("send() on the UI thread never waits for the write in flight, nor for the queue behind it",
+          "[launchpad][link][wake]") {
+    // The Windows symptom this shape exists for: a 538-byte bulk SysEx blocks WinMM for ~170 ms, and the UI's own
+    // message (the bytes that let a device go) must not queue behind a whole frame of LED traffic. So send() hands the
+    // message to the writer and returns; only the writer touches the port.
+    Rig             rig;
+    rig.sendDelayMs = 120;  // a bulk write as WinMM takes it, shorter so the case is quick
+    ControllerLink  link(openerFor(rig), true);  // the provider's shape: its own thread
+    REQUIRE(link.connect("LP in", "LP out", {}));
+    const Bytes bulk(538, 0x7F);
+    push(link, bulk);
+    // Wait until the writer is INSIDE the port: from here a send() that wrote the port itself, or flushed the queue
+    // first, would block for the rest of the 120 ms.
+    const auto deadline = std::chrono::steady_clock::now() + std::chrono::seconds(5);
+    while (rig.sendsStarted.load() < 1 && std::chrono::steady_clock::now() < deadline) link.pump();
+    REQUIRE(rig.sendsStarted.load() >= 1);
+    const Bytes farewell{0xF0, 0x00, 0xF7};
+    const auto  began = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
+    REQUIRE(link.send(farewell.data(), farewell.size()));
+    const auto waited = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(std::chrono::steady_clock::now() - began);
+    CHECK(waited.count() < 40);  // queued in a mutex's time, not a write's
+    // ...and the writer still writes it, AFTER what the session queued: the ordering send() promises.
+    while (link.messagesSent() < 2 && std::chrono::steady_clock::now() < deadline) link.pump();
+    REQUIRE(link.messagesSent() == 2);
+    link.disconnect();
+    CHECK(rig.written["LP out"] == std::vector<Bytes>{bulk, farewell});
+}
+
+TEST_CASE("a stale claim's slots never reach the next claim's drain, deterministically", "[launchpad][link][swap]") {
+    // The racing case above cannot fail without the stale-slot filter: its tags only ever ascend, because the audio
+    // thread drains as fast as the device talks. This one makes the stale slots UNAVOIDABLE - the consumer is held off
+    // while four claims come and go, so when it finally drains, three claims are already over - and then requires every
+    // slot it is handed to belong to the claim that was live when it read the generation. Without the filter the drain
+    // hands back all sixteen (the earlier twelve included) under the fourth claim's number, and both checks are red.
+    Rig            rig;
+    ControllerLink link(openerFor(rig), false);  // no writer thread: nothing but this case touches the link
+    std::atomic<bool> drain{false};
+    std::atomic<int>  drained{0};
+    std::atomic<int>  stale{0};
+    std::thread       audio([&] {
+        DeviceMessage slots[32];
+        while (!drain.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) std::this_thread::yield();
+        const std::uint32_t live = link.generation();  // the claim live NOW: only its slots may come back
+        const std::size_t   n    = link.drainInput(slots, std::size(slots));
+        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
+            drained.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
+            // Every scripted message is {claim, 0x55}, and the claim's number is its generation - 1.
+            if (slots[i].size != 2 || static_cast<std::uint32_t>(slots[i].data[0]) + 1 != live)
+                stale.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
+        }
+    });
+    for (int claim = 0; claim < 4; ++claim) {
+        REQUIRE(link.connect("LP in", "out " + std::to_string(claim), {}));
+        for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) rig.deliver("LP in", {static_cast<std::uint8_t>(claim), 0x55});
+        if (claim < 3) link.disconnect();  // the last claim stays: the drain must have a live one to answer under
+    }
+    drain.store(true, std::memory_order_release);
+    audio.join();
+    CHECK(stale.load() == 0);
+    CHECK(drained.load() == 4);  // exactly the last claim's: the earlier twelve are dropped where they sit
+    CHECK(link.generation() == 4);
+}

+TEST_CASE("the port filter: a filtered lister hides what a filtered opener refuses", "[launchpad][filter]") {

+    // "RPTestKeys:RPTestKeys 129:0"), so the standalone's scan can neither list nor open anything else - no real device's

+    // client and port numbers that move as other clients come and go; a whole name is simply the strictest substring.
+    CHECK(rp::launchpad::midiPortAllowedBy("LPProMK3 MIDI:1 24:0", "LPProMK3 MIDI,RPTestKeys"));

+    CHECK_FALSE(rp::launchpad::midiPortAllowedBy("Zoom L6:1 20:0", "LPProMK3 MIDI,RPTestKeys"));
````

The review called the swap case weak: it compared what arrived while the audio thread raced the claims, so it could

consumer is held off, then it drains under the fourth claim's generation: `stale == 0`, `drained == 4`), and here is
how it looks with the skip disabled - one temporary `if (true)` in `drainInput`.

`test/menu/launchpad.test.ts` is the branch's 47 cases rebased onto the facet (this tree had 22), with a `FakeFacet
implements LaunchpadClient` injected by `setLaunchpadClient`; its claim path is the facet's order, so a refusal
behaves as `LaunchpadRpc`'s does and the facet's own words replace the legacy host's.
`test/config/user-config.test.ts` gains the branch's two `1c1c89f1b` cases (two writers, a failed write) and the
schema's tolerance; `test/controller/registry.test.ts` holds every row an app offers to a key of its own schema with
values that schema accepts; `test/graph/build-graph.test.ts` expects the `driving` flag. And three `test-native` files
drive the real facet over the headless host: `launchpad-facet.test.ts` (8 cases: ports, a scan that finds and
confirms, a claim's `reserve_midi` before the open, a refused claim that reserves nothing, `restored`, the held edge,
a swap's two reservations and a new generation, and the harness surface staging beside a held claim);
`launchpad-devices.test.ts` (5 cases over `launchpadDevices.ts`, the two-PROCESS refusal first, because it needs the
lock directory to survive another host's exit); and `n8-cart-link.test.ts` (1 case: the headless host's N8 provider
installs the cart link).

Create `packages/retroplug/test-native/launchpad-devices.test.ts`:

````ts
// The shell's OWN module, launchpadDevices.ts, against the headless host's real facet
// (docs/modular-graph-phase-f3-design.md section 8): the restore that claims the pair config.json remembers, the scan
// stepped to its end that persists the pair it found, Forget that gives the device back, a claim the lister cannot see,
// and the cross-PROCESS refusal. Everything below the module is the production code a standalone runs - the pack's
// provider, its facet, the claim path and the cross-process lock - over the host's SCRIPTED device
// (packages/launchpad/native/test/FakePorts.hpp), so the decisions launchpadDevices makes are held here and not only in
// `pnpm sdl:controller`, which no CI runs.
//
// The fake has a Pro MK3 on "LPProMK3 MIDI" both ways, which answers the Universal Device Inquiry and its own layout
// query, and an interface's port that answers nothing.
//
// Run: pnpm test:native launchpad-devices
import { test, expect } from "@retroplug/testing";
import { createAudioDriver } from "../src/audioDriver";
import { createRealBackend } from "../src/realBackend";
import { UserConfigStore } from "../src/userConfigStore";
import { createLaunchpadClient } from "@retroplug/launchpad/client";
import { PRO_MK3, exitToLiveMode } from "@retroplug/launchpad";
import { makeCall } from "../src/rpcClient";
import {
  applyLaunchpadScan, connectLaunchpad, forgetLaunchpad, getLaunchpadConfig, pollLaunchpadScan,
  resetLaunchpadScanForTest, restoreLaunchpad, setLaunchpadClient, setLaunchpadScanClock, startLaunchpadScan,
} from "../ui/screens/menu/launchpadDevices";

declare const __CONFIG_DIR__: string;
/** The test host's own seam: this file runs INSIDE the native host (txiki.js), whose spawn runs a second process. */
declare const tjs: {
  exePath: string;
  env: Record<string, string>;
  exit(code: number): void;
  spawn(
    args: string[],
    options?: {
      env?: Record<string, string>;
      stdout?: "inherit" | "pipe" | "ignore";
      stderr?: "inherit" | "pipe" | "ignore";
    },
  ): {
    wait(): Promise<{ exit_status: number; term_signal: string | null }>;
    kill(signal: string): void;
    stdout: { getReader(): { read(): Promise<{ done: boolean; value?: Uint8Array }> } } | null;
    stderr: { getReader(): { read(): Promise<{ done: boolean; value?: Uint8Array }> } } | null;
  };
};
declare const __SELF_BUNDLE__: string;
/** The test host's opt-in to keep pumping past its bounded spin (packages/native/src/main.cpp): a case that awaits a
 *  child PROCESS needs it, because the bounded spin has no sleep and never services the child's exit in time. */
declare const __rp_keepAlive: () => void;

const PRO = "LPProMK3 MIDI";
const PRO_NAME = PRO_MK3.name; // "Launchpad Pro [MK3]", the name a scan records
const CLOSE = Uint8Array.from(exitToLiveMode(PRO_MK3));

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The second PROCESS. The claim is one per machine across processes, so the only real proof of it is another process:
// this same bundle, re-run by the host with RP_LAUNCHPAD_HOLDER set, which claims the device through the facet and writes
// what the facet answered where the parent reads it. The branch runs before any test is registered, and exits: this
// process is a holder, not a test run.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
const HOLDER_ENV = "RP_LAUNCHPAD_HOLDER";
const ANSWER = `${__CONFIG_DIR__}/launchpad-holder.json`;
if (tjs.env[HOLDER_ENV] === "1") {
  const client = createLaunchpadClient(makeCall());
  const held = client.claim(PRO, PRO, CLOSE);
  const answer = JSON.stringify({ connected: held.connected, error: held.error, input: held.input });
  createRealBackend().writeFile(ANSWER, new TextEncoder().encode(answer));
  tjs.exit(0);
}

/** Drain the child's pipes concurrently with the wait: reading one then the other deadlocks a noisy child. */
async function drain(
  stream: { getReader(): { read(): Promise<{ done: boolean; value?: Uint8Array }> } } | null,
): Promise<string> {
  if (!stream) return "";
  const reader = stream.getReader();
  const chunks: Uint8Array[] = [];
  for (;;) {
    const { done, value } = await reader.read();
    if (done) break;
    if (value) chunks.push(value);
  }
  const text = new TextDecoder();
  return chunks.map((c) => text.decode(c)).join("");
}

/** A store over the host's own config.json, read as a fresh one reads it (a new store starts at the DEFAULTS until load). */
function store(): UserConfigStore {
  const cfg = new UserConfigStore(createRealBackend());
  cfg.load();
  return cfg;
}

// FIRST in the file on purpose: it is the one case that runs a SECOND process against this host's claim directory, and a
// child that touched that directory would make every later case's cross-process answer depend on this one having run. Held
// here, it also proves it needs nothing but a fresh config: no earlier case has claimed anything.
test("a second PROCESS cannot claim the port this one holds, and says so in the facet's words", async () => {
  __rp_keepAlive(); // the child outlasts the host's bounded spin
  const cfg = store();
  const client = createLaunchpadClient(makeCall());
  cfg.setControlSurface({ input: PRO, output: PRO, device: PRO_NAME, enabled: true });
  restoreLaunchpad(cfg);
  expect(client.status().connected).toBe(true);
  try {
    createRealBackend().deleteFile(ANSWER);
    const child = tjs.spawn([tjs.exePath, __SELF_BUNDLE__], {
      env: { ...tjs.env, [HOLDER_ENV]: "1" },
      stdout: "pipe",
      stderr: "pipe",
    });
    const [out, err, status] = await Promise.all([drain(child.stdout), drain(child.stderr), child.wait()]);
    expect(status.exit_status, `the holder process failed:\n${out}\n${err}`).toBe(0);
    const raw = createRealBackend().readFile(ANSWER);
    expect(raw === null).toBe(false);
    const answer = JSON.parse(new TextDecoder().decode(raw!)) as { connected: boolean; error: string };
    // The facet's own refusal (LaunchpadRpc's claim), reached through launchpadDevices' client in ANOTHER process while
    // this one holds the lock: the second host's claim opened nothing and took nothing.
    expect(answer.connected).toBe(false);
    expect(answer.error).toBe("in use by another RetroPlug");
    // ...and this process still holds it, so the child's run changed nothing here.
    expect(client.status().connected).toBe(true);
    expect(client.status().input).toBe(PRO);
  } finally {
    client.release();
    cfg.setControlSurface({ input: "", output: "", device: "", enabled: false });
  }
});

test("the restore claims the pair config.json remembers, then tells the host it is done", () => {
  const audio = createAudioDriver();
  const cfg = store();
  cfg.setControlSurface({ input: PRO, output: PRO, device: PRO_NAME, enabled: true });
  audio.drainProductCalls(); // whatever earlier cases did, this case reads from here
  restoreLaunchpad(cfg);
  const status = createLaunchpadClient(makeCall()).status();
  expect(status.connected).toBe(true);
  expect(status.input).toBe(PRO);
  // The product's own record, in order: the pair kept out of the shared stream BEFORE it is opened, then the rendezvous's
  // end. A product holds its MIDI and audio until that second line, which is why it matters that it always arrives.
  expect(audio.drainProductCalls()).toEqual([`reserve_midi:${PRO}|${PRO}`, "restored"]);
});

test("a scan stepped to its end finds the device, persists the pair and claims it", () => {
  const audio = createAudioDriver();
  const cfg = store();
  const client = createLaunchpadClient(makeCall());
  setLaunchpadClient(client);
  resetLaunchpadScanForTest();
  const clock = { ms: 1000 };
  setLaunchpadScanClock(() => clock.ms);
  try {
    // Wanted, but nothing known yet: what a user who has just enabled the feature, or one upgrading from the legacy
    // host, has in config.json.
    cfg.setControlSurface({ input: "", output: "", device: "", enabled: true });
    if (client.status().connected) client.release();
    restoreLaunchpad(cfg); // nothing to claim, and the word still goes out
    audio.drainProductCalls();
    expect(startLaunchpadScan()).toBe(true);
    // The frame poll's own step loop: the scan is a clocked state machine, and nothing advances it but this.
    for (let i = 0; i < 1000; i++) {
      const s = pollLaunchpadScan();
      if (!s || !s.busy) break;
      clock.ms += 16;
    }
    const done = pollLaunchpadScan()!;
    expect(done.busy).toBe(false);
    const found = applyLaunchpadScan(cfg, done);
    expect(found?.input).toBe(PRO);
    expect(found?.name).toBe(PRO_NAME);
    // Persisted (a fresh store reads config.json back) and claimed: the answer the instance submenu gates on.
    const saved = store().controlSurface();
    expect(saved.input).toBe(PRO);
    expect(saved.output).toBe(PRO);
    expect(saved.device).toBe(PRO_NAME);
    expect(client.status().connected).toBe(true);
    // The scan's held edge around the loose ports, then the claim: the stream is told about the inputs it must give up
    // BEFORE anything is opened, and the pair is reserved before the link opens it.
    const calls = audio.drainProductCalls();
    expect(calls.includes("suspend_hardware_inputs:1")).toBe(true);
    expect(calls.indexOf("suspend_hardware_inputs:1")).toBeLessThan(calls.lastIndexOf(`reserve_midi:${PRO}|${PRO}`));
    expect(calls[calls.length - 1]).toBe(`reserve_midi:${PRO}|${PRO}`);
  } finally {
    setLaunchpadClient(undefined);
    resetLaunchpadScanForTest();
  }
});

test("Forget clears the pair AND the name, and gives the device back", () => {
  const audio = createAudioDriver();
  const cfg = store();
  const client = createLaunchpadClient(makeCall());
  cfg.setControlSurface({ input: PRO, output: PRO, device: PRO_NAME, enabled: true });
  restoreLaunchpad(cfg);
  expect(client.status().connected).toBe(true);
  audio.drainProductCalls();
  forgetLaunchpad(cfg);
  // The pair and the NAME go; "Use in Project" is the project's switch, not the device's, and stays as the user left it.
  expect(cfg.controlSurface()).toEqual({ input: "", output: "", enabled: true, device: "" });
  expect(client.status().connected).toBe(false);
  // The pair rejoins the shared stream: an empty reservation for the product, which is what opens the ports again.
  expect(audio.drainProductCalls()).toEqual(["reserve_midi:|"]);
});

test("Connect resolves the hinted default, and a pair whose device is away is refused in the facet's words", () => {
  const cfg = store();
  const client = createLaunchpadClient(makeCall());
  if (client.status().connected) client.release();
  cfg.setControlSurface({ input: "", output: "", device: "", enabled: false });
  const before = getLaunchpadConfig(cfg)!;
  connectLaunchpad(cfg, true, before);
  expect(getLaunchpadConfig(cfg)!.connected).toBe(true);
  expect(cfg.controlSurface().input).toBe(PRO); // the Pro's own port, found by its hint, not picked by the user

  // Now a saved pick whose device is not on the machine: the claim fails, the row says why in the FACET's words
  // (LaunchpadRpc's presence check), and nothing is left held.
  client.release();
  cfg.setControlSurface({ input: "Some Synth", output: "Some Synth", device: "", enabled: true });
  const warn = console.warn;
  const warned: string[] = [];
  console.warn = (...parts: unknown[]) => void warned.push(parts.map(String).join(" "));
  try {
    restoreLaunchpad(cfg);
  } finally {
    console.warn = warn;
  }
  expect(warned.length).toBe(1);
  expect(warned[0].includes("not connected: Some Synth")).toBe(true);
  expect(client.status().connected).toBe(false);
  expect(getLaunchpadConfig(cfg)!.error).toBe("not connected: Some Synth");
  // The pick is kept: the device may be plugged back in, and forgetting it would make the user scan again.
  expect(cfg.controlSurface().input).toBe("Some Synth");
  cfg.setControlSurface({ input: "", output: "", device: "", enabled: false });
});
````

Create `packages/retroplug/test-native/launchpad-facet.test.ts`:

````ts
// The Launchpad facet through the real native host: the pack's provider and its RPC facet over a SCRIPTED device
// (packages/native/src/main.cpp starts it with packages/launchpad/native/test/FakePorts.hpp's rig - a Pro MK3 on
// "LPProMK3 MIDI" both ways, which answers the Universal Device Inquiry and its own layout query, and an interface's port
// that answers nothing). No hardware, no rtmidi, and the same facet code the standalone runs.
//
// What only this file can hold: that the facet's answers reach TS over the real RPC seam, and that what TS decides reaches
// the PRODUCT (rp_device_host's reserve_midi, suspend_hardware_inputs and restored, recorded by the headless host's
// ProviderHost and drained through the engine facet). The claim's cross-process half is the pack's own case in C++
// (Controller.test.cpp, over a real config dir), and the standalone's `pnpm sdl:controller` leg 5 is the two-PROCESS one.
//
// Run: pnpm test:native launchpad-facet
import { test, expect } from "@retroplug/testing";
import { createAudioDriver } from "../src/audioDriver";
import { createLaunchpadClient, type LaunchpadClient } from "@retroplug/launchpad/client";
import {
  PRO_MK3, deviceInquiry, exitToLiveMode, isModelReply, modelQuery, parseInquiryReply, profilesForFamily,
} from "@retroplug/launchpad";
import { PortScan } from "@retroplug/launchpad/portScan";
import { createRealBackend } from "../src/realBackend";
import { makeCall } from "../src/rpcClient";
import { toGraphJson } from "@retroplug/core/graphDocument";

const PRO = "LPProMK3 MIDI";
const IFACE = "MIDISPORT 2x2 Port A";

function facet(): LaunchpadClient {
  return createLaunchpadClient(makeCall());
}

/** A scan over the facet, driven to its end by a clock the test advances (the standalone's frame poll does this). */
function scanToEnd(
  client: LaunchpadClient,
): { found: { input: string; output: string; name: string } | null; wrote: number } {
  const ports = client.ports();
  const api = {
    openInputs: (names: readonly string[]) => client.openInputs(names.slice()),
    openOutput: (name: string) => client.openOutput(name),
    send: (h: number, bytes: readonly number[]) => client.sendOn(h, Uint8Array.from(bytes)),
    read: (h: number) => client.read(h).messages.map((m) => Array.from(m)),
    close: (h: number) => void client.close(h),
  };
  const scan = new PortScan(api, ports.inputs, ports.outputs, deviceInquiry(), 300, {
    followUp: (reply) => {
      const parsed = parseInquiryReply(reply.bytes);
      return parsed ? profilesForFamily(parsed.family).map((p) => modelQuery(p)) : [];
    },
  });
  let now = 1000;
  scan.step(now); // the first probe goes out now
  for (let i = 0; i < 1000 && scan.status().busy; i++) {
    now += 16;
    scan.step(now);
  }
  const st = scan.status();
  let found: { input: string; output: string; name: string } | null = null;
  for (const r of st.replies) {
    const parsed = parseInquiryReply(r.bytes);
    if (!parsed) continue;
    for (const profile of profilesForFamily(parsed.family))
      if (st.replies.some((x) => x.output === r.output && x.input === r.input && isModelReply(profile, x.bytes)))
        found = { input: r.input, output: r.output, name: profile.name };
  }
  return { found, wrote: now - 1000 };
}

  const ports = client.ports();
  expect(ports.inputs).toEqual([PRO, IFACE]);
  expect(ports.outputs).toEqual([PRO, IFACE]);
  expect(client.status().connected).toBe(false);
});

test("a scan through the facet finds and confirms the model on the pair that answered", () => {
  const client = facet();
  const { found, wrote } = scanToEnd(client);
  expect(found).toEqual({ input: PRO, output: PRO, name: PRO_MK3.name });
  // Every port was probed, and each window ran its course: milliseconds, not a wall-clock stall.
  expect(wrote >= 300 * 2).toBe(true);
});

test("a claim keeps the pair out of the product's shared MIDI stream, and a release gives it back", () => {
  const audio = createAudioDriver();
  audio.drainProductCalls(); // whatever the host's own startup did, this case reads from here
  const client = facet();
  const held = client.claim(PRO, PRO, Uint8Array.from(exitToLiveMode(PRO_MK3)));
  expect(held.connected).toBe(true);
  // A relative count: the provider is the process's, so an earlier case's claims are behind it.
  expect(held.generation > 0).toBe(true);
  expect(held.input).toBe(PRO);
  // The facet lets the OLD pair go first (nothing, here), then reserves the pick BEFORE it opens it, so the stream never
  // holds a port the surface is about to take. ONE reservation, not two: there is no empty pair in between, which is what
  // makes a swap a single audio restart. The record is what the facet SAID.
  expect(audio.drainProductCalls()).toEqual([`reserve_midi:${PRO}|${PRO}`]);

  const given = client.release();
  expect(given.connected).toBe(false);
  expect(given.generation).toBe(0);
  // Release reserves empty: the pair rejoins the shared stream.
  expect(audio.drainProductCalls()).toEqual(["reserve_midi:|"]);
});

test("a claim the lister cannot see is refused, and reserves nothing for it", () => {
  const audio = createAudioDriver();
  audio.drainProductCalls();
  const client = facet();
  const held = client.claim("Some Synth", "Some Synth", Uint8Array.from(exitToLiveMode(PRO_MK3)));
  expect(held.connected).toBe(false);
  expect(held.error).toBe("not connected: Some Synth");
  // Presence is checked before the pick is reserved: the refusal hands the reservation back and names no pair, so the
  // stream is never reopened for a stale pick, and a port another instance holds stays out of this one's stream until it
  // is released.
  expect(audio.drainProductCalls()).toEqual(["reserve_midi:|"]);
});

test("the facet's restored reaches the product: the rendezvous's end", () => {
  const audio = createAudioDriver();
  audio.drainProductCalls();
  const client = facet();
  expect(client.restored()).toBe(true);
  expect(audio.drainProductCalls()).toEqual(["restored"]);
});

test("a scan holds the stream's inputs, then gives them back", () => {
  const audio = createAudioDriver();
  audio.drainProductCalls();
  const client = facet();
  const input = client.openInputs([PRO])[0] ?? 0;
  expect(input > 0).toBe(true);
  expect(audio.drainProductCalls()).toEqual(["suspend_hardware_inputs:1"]);
  expect(client.close(input)).toBe(true);
  expect(audio.drainProductCalls()).toEqual(["suspend_hardware_inputs:0"]);

test("a claim that replaces a claim lets the old pair go before the new one is reserved", () => {
  const audio = createAudioDriver();
  const client = facet();
  const first = client.claim(PRO, PRO, Uint8Array.from(exitToLiveMode(PRO_MK3)));
  expect(first.connected).toBe(true);
  audio.drainProductCalls();
  const second = client.claim(IFACE, IFACE, Uint8Array.from(exitToLiveMode(PRO_MK3)));
  expect(second.connected).toBe(true);
  // The session's `connected` value, so a pair swapped inside one block reads as a NEW device. A relative count: the
  // provider is the process's, so an earlier case's claims are behind it.
  expect(second.generation).toBe(first.generation + 1);
  // One reservation for the swap: the old pair's gave way to the new one directly, with no empty pair between them (which
  // would be two reopens of the shared stream, and two audio restarts, for one swap).
  expect(audio.drainProductCalls()).toEqual([`reserve_midi:${IFACE}|${IFACE}`]);
  client.release();
  audio.drainProductCalls();
});

test("the fake device is not a claim on the graph: the harness surface still drives the document", () => {
  // The headless host's graph control surface is its harness link (stageControllerIn), and the facet's scripted device is
  // separate: a plan's surface nodes are not silently fed by a device a test claimed. Held to what the PLAN received, not
  // to stageControllerIn's return value: a document carries the press from the surface node to the host's MIDI out.
  const audio = createAudioDriver();
  const be = createRealBackend();
  const client = facet();
  expect(client.claim(PRO, PRO, Uint8Array.from(exitToLiveMode(PRO_MK3))).connected).toBe(true);
  const document = toGraphJson({
    nodes: [
      { id: "out", type: "rp.host.audio-out", settings: { buses: [1, 1] } },
      { id: "surface-in", type: "rp.launchpad.surface-in" },
      { id: "midi-out", type: "rp.host.midi-out", settings: { systems: [0] } },
    ],
    wires: [{ from: "surface-in.in", to: "midi-out.in1" }],
  });
  const placed = be.setGraph({ document, slots: [] });
  expect(placed.ok, JSON.stringify(placed.errors)).toBe(true);
  audio.renderBlocks(2, [{ frames: 64 }]); // the surface node binds the link and discards what it holds
  expect(audio.stageControllerIn([0x90, 0x51, 0x7f])).toBe(true);
  const delivered = audio.renderBlocks(2, [{ frames: 64 }]);
  expect(delivered.midiOut.length).toBe(1);
  expect(Array.from(delivered.midiOut[0].data)).toEqual([0x90, 0x51, 0x7f]);
  client.release();
});
````

Create `packages/retroplug/test-native/n8-cart-link.test.ts`:

````ts
// The headless host installs the N8 provider's cart link in the engine's registry, as a product's provider does
// (packages/native/src/main.cpp's ProviderHost, docs/modular-graph-phase-e2-design.md section 6). A plan that places
// rp.n8.nes acquires the link BY NAME from that registry (rp.host.devices/2), so a host that gives the provider a seat
// and installs nothing leaves the node on its "no cart" stub: it plans, it renders, and every byte and every capability
// job it takes goes nowhere. That is a wiring mistake no other test:native case saw, because nothing else here places a
// cart node.
//
// What distinguishes the two from TS: rp.n8.nes's capability jobs. The stub (rp::n8::NoCart) refuses every one of them
// "not connected"; the real link's own answer comes from N8Host, which refuses a battery job that names no ROM (and no
// ROM has been booted here) BEFORE it looks at whether the cart is streaming. So the words of that refusal are the
// proof that the registry held the link.
//
// Run: pnpm test:native n8-cart-link
import { test, expect } from "@retroplug/testing";
import { createAudioDriver } from "../src/audioDriver";
import { createRealBackend } from "../src/realBackend";
import { toGraphJson } from "@retroplug/core/graphDocument";

test("the headless host's N8 provider installs the cart link, so a plan's rp.n8.nes is the real link", async () => {
  const be = createRealBackend();
  const audio = createAudioDriver();
  const document = toGraphJson({
    nodes: [
      { id: "out", type: "rp.host.audio-out", settings: { buses: [1, 1] } },
      { id: "cart", type: "rp.n8.nes" },
    ],
    wires: [],
  });
  const placed = be.setGraph({ document, slots: [] });
  expect(placed.ok, JSON.stringify(placed.errors)).toBe(true);
  audio.renderBlocks(2, [{ frames: 64 }]); // the node activates here and acquires the link

  // The link's answer, not the stub's ("not connected"): a battery job that names no ROM and follows no boot.
  let refusal = "";
  await be.capability("cart", "sram.dump").catch((e: Error) => (refusal = e.message));
  expect(refusal).toBe(
    "a battery job needs the ROM's file name: name it, or boot the ROM through rom.upload first",
  );

  // The same door for the ROM capability, which also answers before it looks at the cart: an image that is not iNES.
  let uploadRefusal = "";
  await be.capability("cart", "rom.upload", { bytes: Uint8Array.from([0, 1, 2, 3]) })
    .catch((e: Error) => (uploadRefusal = e.message));
  expect(uploadRefusal).toBe("the upload is not an iNES image");
});
````

````diff
+  }

+    expect(h.held).toBe(null);
+    expect(h.released).toEqual([exitToLiveMode(PRO_MK3)]);

+function withCart(stores: AppStores, be: MockBackend, sync: number): void {

+    h.inputs = ["LPProMK3 MIDI:LPProMK3 MIDI 131:0"];
+    h.outputs = ["LPProMK3 MIDI:LPProMK3 MIDI 131:0"];
+  }, (h, stores) => {
+    restoreLaunchpad(stores.userConfig);
+    expect(h.current()?.input).toBe("LPProMK3 MIDI:LPProMK3 MIDI 131:0");
+    expect(stores.userConfig.controlSurface().input).toBe("LPProMK3 MIDI:LPProMK3 MIDI 131:0"); // and re-saved
+  }, { input: "LPProMK3 MIDI:LPProMK3 MIDI 128:0", output: "LPProMK3 MIDI:LPProMK3 MIDI 128:0", enabled: true });
+  // Two candidates with one stem (two identical interfaces): not guessed between.
+  withHost((h) => {
+    h.inputs = ["IF 1", "IF 2"];
+    h.outputs = ["IF 1", "IF 2"];
+  }, (h, stores) => {
+    restoreLaunchpad(stores.userConfig);
+    expect(stores.userConfig.controlSurface().input).toBe("IF 0"); // left as saved (the facet refuses it: not here)
+    expect(h.claims.some((c) => c.input === "IF 1" || c.input === "IF 2")).toBe(false);
+  }, { input: "IF 0", output: "IF 0", enabled: true });
+});
+
+test("the port pickers are greyed while connected", () => {
+  // Stepping one live would claim every pair it passed, sending Programmer-mode bytes to each device.
+  withHost(() => {}, (_h, stores, be) => {
+    restoreLaunchpad(stores.userConfig);
+    const rows = submenu(stores, be);
+    expect(findItem(rows, "lp-input")?.disabled).toBe(true);
+    expect(findItem(rows, "lp-output")?.disabled).toBe(true);
+    expect(findItem(rows, "lp-connect")?.disabled).toBe(undefined); // Disconnect is how to change them
+  }, { input: "LPProMK3 MIDI", output: "LPProMK3 MIDI", enabled: true });
+});
+
+test("the USB hint is the device's own MIDI port, not its other interfaces as Windows names them", () => {
+  expect(looksLikeLaunchpad("LPProMK3 MIDI")).toBe(true);
+  expect(looksLikeLaunchpad("LPProMK3 MIDI 0")).toBe(true); // RtMidi's Windows index
+  expect(looksLikeLaunchpad("LPProMK3 MIDI:LPProMK3 MIDI 128:0")).toBe(true); // ALSA
+  expect(looksLikeLaunchpad("MIDIIN2 (LPProMK3 MIDI) 1")).toBe(false); // the DIN interface, on Windows
+  expect(looksLikeLaunchpad("MIDIOUT3 (LPProMK3 MIDI) 2")).toBe(false); // the DAW interface
 });
````

- [ ] **Step 10: The fake, the harness, and the listing proof**

`tools/fixtures/fake-launchpad.c` is an ALSA sequencer client that answers the Universal Device Inquiry and the Pro
MK3's own layout query: the port is named `LPProMK3 MIDI` (the real device's USB MIDI interface, which is what the
pack's port hint looks for) and the CLIENT is `RPFakeLPProMK3`, a name no device has, so the allow list - which
matches substrings - cannot admit a real Pro MK3. `tools/run-sdl-controller.sh` starts both fakes, reads their `ready`
lines, writes `RP_MIDI_PORT_ALLOW` once as the two ports' **whole RtMidi names**, refuses a caller who preset it, and
runs a listing-only pass first: anything listed that is not a fake fails the run, and so does a listed port containing
`LPProMK3` or `Launchpad`. `run-sdl-smoke.sh` and `run-sdl-pipewire.sh` gain the scratch config dir and
`RP_MIDI_PORT_ALLOW=RP_NO_PORT`. **The fake is a source file and nothing else**: the harness compiles it with `cc`
into a temporary directory (the script and the proof below both do), so no binary is committed and none is run from
the tree.

Create `tools/fixtures/fake-launchpad.c`:

````cpp
// A fake Launchpad on the ALSA sequencer, for tools/run-sdl-controller.sh: one duplex port named like a Pro
// MK3's USB MIDI interface. It answers a Universal Device Inquiry the way the real device does, answers the
// Pro MK3's "which layout?" query in the Pro's own header (what tells it from a Mini MK3, which shares the
// inquiry bytes), and prints every message it receives as hex, one per line, flushed.
//
// Its CLIENT name is deliberately one no real device has ("RPFakeLPProMK3"), while its PORT keeps the USB
// interface's name ("LPProMK3 MIDI") because that is what a scan's port-hint matching looks for. The client name is
// what makes the harness's allow list safe: RtMidi names an ALSA port "<client>:<port> <client#>:<port#>", so an
// entry naming this client cannot also name a real Pro MK3, whose client is its own device name. What the port stem
// logic sees is therefore "RPFakeLPProMK3:LPProMK3 MIDI": a prefix match on "LPProMK3 MIDI" does NOT hold, so the
// fake is not offered as the default port and the harness reaches it through a scan (which matches on the inquiry
// reply, not the name).
//
// Arguments, any order:
//   chatter     also play a NoteOn every 50 ms, as a pad being pressed would - so a test can see whether those
//               reach the host's shared MIDI stream (they must not while the port is claimed)
//   client=NAME the ALSA client name (default "RPFakeLPProMK3")
//   name=NAME   the PORT name (default "LPProMK3 MIDI")
//   note=N      the note chatter plays (decimal, default 81)
//   noreply     answer nothing - an ordinary keyboard, not a Launchpad
//
// Build: cc -o fake fake-launchpad.c -lasound
#include <alsa/asoundlib.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <signal.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
static volatile int run = 1;
static void stop(int s) { (void)s; run = 0; }
static void sendBytes(snd_seq_t* seq, int port, unsigned char* data, long n) {
    snd_midi_event_t* enc;
    snd_midi_event_new(256, &enc);
    snd_seq_event_t ev;
    snd_seq_ev_clear(&ev);
    snd_seq_ev_set_source(&ev, port); snd_seq_ev_set_subs(&ev); snd_seq_ev_set_direct(&ev);
    if (data[0] == 0xF0) snd_seq_ev_set_sysex(&ev, n, data);
    else snd_midi_event_encode(enc, data, n, &ev);
    snd_seq_event_output_direct(seq, &ev);
    snd_midi_event_free(enc);
}
int main(int argc, char** argv) {
    int chatter = 0, noreply = 0, noteNum = 0x51;
    const char* client = "RPFakeLPProMK3";
    const char* name = "LPProMK3 MIDI";
    for (int i = 1; i < argc; i++) {
        if (!strcmp(argv[i], "chatter")) chatter = 1;
        else if (!strcmp(argv[i], "noreply")) noreply = 1;
        else if (!strncmp(argv[i], "client=", 7)) client = argv[i] + 7;
        else if (!strncmp(argv[i], "name=", 5)) name = argv[i] + 5;
        else if (!strncmp(argv[i], "note=", 5)) noteNum = atoi(argv[i] + 5) & 0x7F;
    }
    snd_seq_t* seq;
    // Non-blocking, or the drain loop below blocks waiting for the NEXT event once the queue is empty: then
    // neither a SIGTERM (it would never re-check `run`) nor chatter (it never reaches its timeout) gets a turn.
    if (snd_seq_open(&seq, "default", SND_SEQ_OPEN_DUPLEX, SND_SEQ_NONBLOCK) < 0) return 1;
    snd_seq_set_client_name(seq, client);
    int port = snd_seq_create_simple_port(seq, name,
        SND_SEQ_PORT_CAP_READ | SND_SEQ_PORT_CAP_SUBS_READ | SND_SEQ_PORT_CAP_WRITE | SND_SEQ_PORT_CAP_SUBS_WRITE,
        SND_SEQ_PORT_TYPE_MIDI_GENERIC | SND_SEQ_PORT_TYPE_APPLICATION);
    signal(SIGTERM, stop); signal(SIGINT, stop);
    snd_midi_event_t* dec; snd_midi_event_new(4096, &dec); snd_midi_event_no_status(dec, 1);
    printf("ready %d:%d\n", snd_seq_client_id(seq), port); fflush(stdout);
    int npfd = snd_seq_poll_descriptors_count(seq, POLLIN);
    struct pollfd pfd[4]; snd_seq_poll_descriptors(seq, pfd, npfd, POLLIN);
    while (run) {
        if (poll(pfd, npfd, chatter ? 50 : 200) <= 0) {
            if (chatter) { unsigned char note[] = {0x90, (unsigned char)noteNum, 0x7F}; sendBytes(seq, port, note, 3); }
            continue;
        }
        snd_seq_event_t* ev;
        while (snd_seq_event_input(seq, &ev) >= 0) {
            unsigned char buf[4096]; long n = snd_midi_event_decode(dec, buf, sizeof buf, ev);
            if (n <= 0) continue;
            for (long i = 0; i < n; i++) printf("%02x%s", buf[i], i + 1 < n ? " " : "\n");
            fflush(stdout);
            static const unsigned char inq[] = {0xF0, 0x7E, 0x7F, 0x06, 0x01, 0xF7};
            static const unsigned char layoutQuery[] = {0xF0, 0x00, 0x20, 0x29, 0x02, 0x0E, 0x00, 0xF7};
            if (noreply) continue;
            if (n == 6 && !memcmp(buf, inq, 6)) {
                unsigned char reply[] = {0xF0,0x7E,0x00,0x06,0x02,0x00,0x20,0x29,0x13,0x01,0,0,0,1,2,3,0xF7};
                sendBytes(seq, port, reply, sizeof reply);
            } else if (n == 8 && !memcmp(buf, layoutQuery, 8)) {
                unsigned char reply[] = {0xF0,0x00,0x20,0x29,0x02,0x0E,0x00,0x00,0x00,0xF7};  // layout 0, page 0
                sendBytes(seq, port, reply, sizeof reply);
            }
        }
    }
    snd_seq_close(seq);
    return 0;
}
````
